## 2026-06-16 — Track V-A2: unified aerial-perspective post-process (Batch 311)

- **NEW-ATMO-AERIAL-PERSPECTIVE-POSTPROCESS** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 311). A fullscreen post-process pass that applies ONE depth-correct atmosphere over the whole composited scene (terrain, 3D tiles, glTF models, geometry), unifying the per-tile ground-atmosphere drape — the "post-process lighting for the terrain" Takram-talk headline. **WGSL** (`Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/AerialPerspective.wgsl`): per pixel, (1) recover eye-space distance from the renderer-wide LOG depth (`logDepthToEyeDistance`, inlined `csm_reverseLogDepthToEyeDistance`); sky pixels (raw depth ≥ `skyCutoff`) pass through untouched so the sky/atmosphere shell shows through; (2) recover the world-space view ray as `inverseViewRotation × normalize(inverseProjection·NDC_at_near)` — the eye-space **direction** rotated to world, NOT a `pFar−pNear` world-position difference (that suffers FP32 catastrophic cancellation at Earth scale → NaN ray → black scene; this was the key bring-up bug); use the **near** plane (clip-z 0) for the inverse-projection unproject because the scene projection is near-finite/far-INFINITE so clip-z 1 maps to w≈0 → NaN; (3) march the camera→fragment segment for analytic single-scatter (Rayleigh + Mie, HG phase vs the sun, parity port of `AtmosphereCommon.glsl::computeScattering`); (4) EXTINCTION = `exp(−(βR·ODr+βM·ODm))` from the *marched* optical depth (NOT a transmittance-LUT ratio: for horizontal/downward rays both endpoints have a near-opaque path-to-TOA so a LUT ratio collapses to a meaningless ~0/0 → black). Compose `sceneColor·T + inscatter`. **Why analytic, not LUT-sampled:** the single-inscatter LUT's Y-up baked-sun parameterization can't represent view–sun azimuth (`ENABLE_SKY_INSCATTER_LUT=false`, `NEW-ATMOSPHERE-LUT-SUN-RELATIVE`) AND the compute engine that bakes the LUTs is dormant (`NEW-WEBGPU-COMPUTE-ENGINE-WIRING`) — so the analytic march is both correct AND runtime-functional today. The transmittance LUT view is still bound (group 0 binding 2, white 1×1 placeholder until populated) + `sampleTransmittance` kept for the V-A3 sun-radiance/derived-lighting follow-on. **TS** (`WebGPUAerialPerspectiveEffect.ts`, `PostProcessEffect`): output texture + pipeline + 56-float uniform (camera WC, sun WC, βR/βM + scale heights, mie-g/near/far/thickness, intensity/inscatterScale/skyCutoff, inverseProjection, inverseView); `setFrameData` packs per-frame, `setTransmittanceView` pushes the LUT. Runs FIRST in the post-process `execute()` chain (before AO/bloom/tonemap) so the haze participates in bloom + tonemap, mirroring how WebGL applies the ground atmosphere in the globe FS before post-process. Wired through `WebGPUPostProcessPipeline` (add/getter/hasActiveStages/execute/resize/destroy/recreate-reset) + `WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.configure` (lazy-init + per-frame `updateAerialPerspectiveFrameData` from `uniformState`). **Composition decision (DOCUMENTED):** the post-process is the SINGLE owner of distance haze when active; the in-globe ground-atmosphere + fog drape is gated OFF (`WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB` + `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileUB` read the new `frameState.aerialPerspective` flag Scene publishes, same dormant-gate pattern as `taaEnabled`) so the two don't double-apply. Opt-in via `scene.aerialPerspective = true` (default OFF → full backwards compat; WebGL ignores it). **Verified:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-aerial-perspective.mjs` — low oblique Rockies view; aerial perspective ON vs OFF: globe still renders (493910 non-black px), far band brightens +0.26 AND desaturates −0.028 (the depth-correct haze signature), no double-darkening (mean 0.44 ≥ 0.6×OFF), 0 console errors. Read the PNGs — distant terrain washes into a soft blue-grey haze toward the horizon while the foreground keeps detail, resembling the Takram reference. Standing gates green (collections-regression, far-camera, bloom-parity, logdepth-zfight, csm-soft-shadow, csm-cast-dispatch, sandcastle-smoke, upstream-regression-check).
- **NEW-ATMO-AERIAL-PERSPECTIVE-NEARFIELD-TUNE** (S, surfaced Batch 311 per Principle 9) — the default look (intensity 1, inscatterScale 1, `atmosphereLightIntensity` 50 from the SKY shell) hazes the near foreground a touch heavily (the bright sky-intensity drives the inscatter); a future pass could (a) calibrate the inscatter against the GROUND-atmosphere intensity (~10) + the WebGL `1−exp(−fExposure·x)` tonemap for a softer near-field, and (b) make `scene.aerialPerspectiveConfig.{intensity,inscatterScale}` mutable at runtime (today the config is read only at lazy-init; `setIntensity`/`setInscatterScale` exist on the effect but no scene-side sync wires them per-frame). Not blocking — the depth-correct fade is already visually correct. **Estimated effort:** 0.5 session + a WebGL-vs-WebGPU numeric ground-haze parity probe. (At HIGH sun the near foreground + a near surface MODEL read noticeably blue — the daytime Rayleigh inscatter looking up through the full atmosphere column dominates the near field; this is the near-field-tune item, NOT a V-A3 derived-lighting issue, whose derived sun is correctly near-white at noon — see V-A3 below.)

## 2026-06-16 — Track V-A3: atmosphere-derived sun + sky lighting + mixed mask (Batch 312)

- **NEW-ATMO-DERIVED-LIGHTING** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 312). Derives the directional SUN light (colour + intensity) and a SKY-IRRADIANCE ambient from the atmosphere so discrete glTF MODELS are lit consistently with the V-A2 aerial-perspective haze + the sky shell — the Takram-talk "light-source lighting for the ISS" half of the mixed-lighting pattern (terrain keeps the V-A2 post-process Lambertian; models use light-source PBR, both driven by ONE coherent atmosphere). **New module** `Scene/AtmosphereDerivedLighting.js` (backend-neutral, pure math): a short CPU Beer-Lambert sun-ray optical-depth march (same Rayleigh + Mie coefficients/scale-heights `AtmosphereLUT.wgsl` bakes + V-A2's `AP_*` use) → `exp(−(βR·ODr+βM·ODm))` gives the sun's transmitted colour (near-white at the zenith; blue+green extinguish first toward the horizon → warm sunset hue) + a horizon-falloff intensity (dims to ~0 as the sun sets). The sun ZENITH is measured against the **local up at the viewed site** (camera position direction), NOT the pole axis — passing a fixed +Z up made the colour ~constant over a day (the key bring-up bug; fixed by threading `localUpWC`). Plus a desaturated cool sky-irradiance ambient (Rayleigh tint blended 75% toward neutral grey, day/night-aware, ~0.2 magnitude at midday to match the historical flat ambient floor). **Why analytic, not LUT-sampled:** mirrors the V-A2 decision exactly — the Bruneton transmittance/irradiance LUTs (Batch 306) exist but the compute engine that bakes them is dormant (`NEW-WEBGPU-COMPUTE-ENGINE-WIRING`), so the analytic CPU path is both physically correct AND runtime-functional today; this module is the documented seam to swap to direct transmittance(sun)+irradiance(sky) LUT reads when the compute engine lands (public shape — colour+intensity+ambient — stays identical). **Wiring** (`Scene.js::updateFrameState`, gated on `aerialPerspective===true && isWebGPU && scene.light instanceof SunLight`): re-derives into a PRIVATE `_atmosphereDerivedLight` (SunLight) each frame and swaps it into `frameState.light` ONLY while aerial perspective is on — `scene.light` is never mutated (turning the flag off restores it untouched); publishes the ambient on the new `frameState.atmosphereSkyIrradiance`. Models pick up the sun for free (the WebGPU model renderer already reads `frameState.light.color`/`.intensity`); `WebGPUModelRenderer.js` reads `frameState.atmosphereSkyIrradiance` for its `ambientColor` (falls back to the historical neutral 0.2 floor when the flag is off / on WebGL). Sun direction is the previous frame's `uniformState.sunDirectionWC` (one frame stale — visually indistinguishable, same trick as `computeSkyBrightness`). **Mixed mask / no double-lighting:** the V-A2 post-process applies extinction+inscatter (NOT Lambertian shading — it has no normal buffer) over the whole scene incl. model pixels, so a lit model also correctly hazes with distance — that is real aerial perspective, not double-LIGHTING. **Verified:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-atmo-lighting.mjs` (NEW) — a 4000×-scaled CesiumMilkTruck on the globe near Denver, two sun states with aerial perspective ON: derived sun HIGH=`rgb 1.00,0.98,0.95 I=1.97` (near-white, full) vs LOW=`rgb 1.00,0.84,0.68 I=1.20` (warm, dimmed); model lit pixels shift warm (R/B 0.64→1.27) AND the model+sunlit terrain are BOTH warm at low sun (model R/B 1.27, globe R/B 1.70 — consistently lit); ON warmer than OFF (derived-light liveness); WebGL renders the scene (it ignores the flag); 0 console errors. Read the PNGs — the low-sun frame is a coherent golden sunset bathing model + terrain together (the headline result), the high-sun frame's blue is the V-A2 daytime inscatter (NEARFIELD-TUNE), not the derived sun. Standing gates green (collections-regression, pickmodel-instanced, model-ibl, bloom-parity, logdepth-zfight, csm-soft-shadow, csm-cast-dispatch, collections-far-camera, sandcastle-smoke, upstream-regression-check 26/26).
- **NEW-ATMO-DERIVED-LIGHTING-LUT-CONSUMPTION** (S, surfaced Batch 312 per Principle 9) — when `NEW-WEBGPU-COMPUTE-ENGINE-WIRING` lands and the Bruneton LUTs bake at runtime, swap the analytic CPU terms in `AtmosphereDerivedLighting.js` for direct LUT reads: the sun colour from the TRANSMITTANCE LUT (altitude × cosSunZenith) and the sky ambient from the IRRADIANCE LUT — more accurate (multiple-scattering-aware) and shareable with a GPU-side path. The module's public shape already matches; this is a body swap behind the same signature. **Estimated effort:** 0.5 session (after the compute engine is wired) + extend `probe-atmo-lighting.mjs` to assert the analytic vs LUT terms agree within tolerance.
  - **BLOCKED — premise reassessed (C4-ATMO-DERIVED-LIGHTING-LUT, 2026-07-04).** The gate `NEW-WEBGPU-COMPUTE-ENGINE-WIRING` (Batch 367) and the `NEW-WEBGPU-ATMOSPHERE-LUT-BGL-INCOMPAT` fix (Batch 396) are both in — the transmittance/irradiance LUTs now bake at runtime as GPU textures. **But the "body swap behind the same signature" is architecturally impossible as written:** `computeAtmosphereDerivedLighting` is a *synchronous per-frame CPU function* called in `Scene.js::updateFrameState` whose result is written straight into `frameState.light` (a `SunLight` color+intensity) for the CURRENT frame. The LUTs are **GPU-only** — `WebGPUAtmosphereLUT` exposes only `GPUTexture`/`GPUTextureView` (no `mapAsync`/readback, no CPU mirror; confirmed no Scene-side CPU consumer of `transmittanceView`/`irradianceView` exists). A CPU "LUT read" therefore requires either (a) an async GPU→CPU `mapAsync` readback each frame — a pipeline stall + inherently ≥1 frame stale + not same-signature (must go async), or (b) relocating the derived-lighting computation into a GPU pass where the model PBR shader samples the transmittance LUT by sun-zenith — a substantial `WebGPUModelRenderer`/`ModelPBRComplete.wgsl` change, NOT a same-signature swap of `AtmosphereDerivedLighting.js`. Additionally there is **no CPU correctness gap to close today:** the analytic path already evaluates the exact Bruneton *single-scatter* Rayleigh+Mie transmittance the LUT stores; the only value-add (multiple-scattering-aware irradiance) is only realizable on the GPU-side path (option b). **Re-scoped:** this is NOT an S body-swap. Reclassify as an M GPU-side task = "model PBR samples the atmosphere transmittance/irradiance LUTs directly (sun radiance + MS ambient), retiring the CPU analytic derived-light" — dependent on the model renderer, not on `AtmosphereDerivedLighting.js`. No runtime change landed for C4-ATMO-DERIVED-LIGHTING-LUT; tree left clean. **⏸ PARKED (formally, 2026-07-09 Campaign-7 batch 0):** the re-scoped M GPU-side task (model PBR samples the transmittance/irradiance LUTs directly, retiring the CPU analytic derived-light) is held until `C7-DPH47-ATMOSPHERE-RESOLVER` (queue #12, DP-H47-ATMOSPHERE-RESOLVER-INCREMENT) lands and clarifies the atmosphere-uniform seam the model consumer would read through. Not a standalone Campaign-7 queue item; blocked on that resolver, not deferred-forever. **UPDATE 2026-07-11:** the seam now EXISTS — `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUAtmosphereUniforms.ts` (`resolveAtmosphereScattering` / `resolveDynamicLighting`), landed by C7-DPH47-ATMO-RESOLVER (see DP-H47 below). The model consumer (`WebGPUDynamicEnvironmentMapManager.ts`) now reads its scattering params through that seam, so the re-scoped GPU-side derived-light task can pick it up as the canonical read point.

Real runtime correctness bug (not a test artifact): `GlobeSurfaceTile.js:660/:905` read `.waterMask` (→ undefined → `createWaterMaskTextureIfNeeded` never runs → ocean/water rendering breaks for quantized-mesh-as-3D-Tiles terrain); `GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js:1034-1035` read `.credits` (→ undefined → per-tile terrain attribution silently dropped, a legal-attribution concern). ## 2026-06-11 — Dual-axis Ultra-Review findings (49 new IDs)

Source of record: [audits/2026-06-11_ULTRA_REVIEW.md](audits/2026-06-11_ULTRA_REVIEW.md) (full report) + `audits/2026-06-11_ULTRA_REVIEW_findings.json` (all 195 confirmed-real findings with per-finding verdicts). Produced by the `webgpu-ultra-review` workflow (53 agents, adversarial-verified). Axis A = WebGPU vs our-WebGL; Axis B = our-WebGL vs upstream fork drift. The 2 CRITICALs were orchestrator-spot-checked against live code (both CONFIRMED REAL); medium/low await per-item check at fix time.

### CRITICAL (2 — verified)

- **NEW-PICKDEPTH-CAPABILITY-READBACK** (A) — ✅ PARTIALLY SHIPPED (Batch 221). Added `GraphicsContext.supportsSynchronousReadback` capability getter (WebGL true / WebGPU false) and switched the two `defined(context.readPixels)` backend-proxy checks (`PickDepth.update`/`getDepth`, `InstancingPipelineStage`) to it — `readPixels` is a required abstract method both backends implement, so `defined()` was always true and wrongly took the WebGL branch. This fixes `PickDepth` to take the async path + the **`InstancingPipelineStage` typed-array drop** for WebGPU instanced models, and removes the wrongly-allocated WebGL pick framebuffer on WebGPU. ~~**Remaining (see NEW-PICK-WEBGPU-DEPTH-RECONSTRUCTION below):** the depth VALUE reconstruction is still wrong on WebGPU, so `pickPosition` returns undefined (safe) rather than a position.~~ Layer 3 (the reconstruction) ✅ SHIPPED Batch 252 — see NEW-PICK-WEBGPU-DEPTH-RECONSTRUCTION below. **FULLY RESOLVED.** NOTE the review under-scoped this as "one getter" — it was a 3-layer fix (capability getter → async architecture → log-depth reconstruction).
- **NEW-PICK-WEBGPU-DEPTH-RECONSTRUCTION** (A, HIGH — split from the above, Batch 221) — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 252). `pickPosition`/`pickPositionWorldCoordinates`/camera-zoom-to-cursor return REAL world positions on WebGPU (was: garbage antipode at ~85,000 km, then SAFE undefined since Batch 221). The fix exploits the renderer-wide log-depth landing (Batch 251): the shared packed `globeDepth.globeDepthTexture` is now known fork-wide to carry LOG depth encoded against the FULL camera frustum, so `Picking.pickPositionWorldCoordinates` skips the per-slice `unprojectDepth` loop on contexts without sync readback and reconstructs ONCE with the untouched camera-frustum clone (gated on new capability getter `GraphicsContext.pickDepthFullFrustumLogEncode` — WebGPU mirrors `_logDepthWriteEnabled`, so the kill switch auto-restores the SAFE undefined state). The sync bridge: `PickDepth.getDepth` arms `_readDepthAsync` (now with the missing top-left y-flip for `copyTextureToBuffer` + 3-channel unpack matching the WGSL pack) and returns the one-frame-stale `_lastDepthValue` cache, validity-bounded by ±4 px and ≤4 RENDERED frames (update-count clock, so requestRenderMode keeps the cache valid) — number|undefined, never a Promise (consumers are all synchronous). `SceneTransforms.drawingBufferToWorldCoordinates` now feeds window depth straight through as NDC z when `Matrix4._depthRangeType === "webgpu"` ([0,1] clip range — `2d-1` broke the w reconstruction). Bonus both-backend fix: `SSCCInputHelpers.handleZoom` degenerate-axis guard (bit-identical center/target picks → `cross = 0` exactly while `dot < 1.0` → `Quaternion.fromAxisAngle` NaN throw). Evidence: `Tools/visual-regression/probe-pickposition-webgpu.mjs` rewritten from SAFE-state assert to parity assert — WebGL vs WebGPU dLon/dLat = 0.00000°, dH = 4.1 m (≤100 m tol), cold-cache frame 0 undefined → converges frame 1 (≤3 tol), wheel-zoom-to-cursor descends 2,000,000 m → 3,411 m on target with 0 console errors; gates probe-collections-regression / probe-orbital-catalog / sandcastle-smoke all PASS. Remaining interlocking siblings (NOT covered): NEW-PICK-RAY-ASYNC (offscreen ray-pick PickDepth instances never receive `update()` on WebGPU — `getDepth` still returns undefined there) / NEW-PICK-METADATA-READBACK (separate readback architecture). **RECONCILIATION (Batch 257, 2026-06-13):** the "FULLY RESOLVED" claim above was scoped to the GLOBE-surface depth path and did NOT cover picking over an OPAQUE Model/Primitive — that surface returned the globe behind/below the model because scene depth was never re-packed into `globeDepthTexture` after the OPAQUE pass (only after globe + 3D-tiles). Fixed as **DP-H45** (see the Data-pipeline pillar entry below) by adding a post-OPAQUE `executeUpdateDepth` re-pack in `WebGPUSceneRendererFrustumLoop.ts`. Probe: `probe-pickposition-model-webgpu.mjs`. So the Batch-252 reconstruction was correct depth *math* on the globe but read a *stale* (pre-opaque) packed depth over models — the DP-H45 fix completes the opaque-surface coverage.
- **NEW-OIT-COMPOSITE-FORMAT** (A) — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 222). `WebGPUOIT._createCompositePipeline` now takes the target format (was hardcoded `rgba8unorm`), and `executeComposite` rebuilds the composite pipeline on demand when `targetFormat` (the real `context._sceneColorFormat`: `bgra8unorm` default / `rgba16float` HDR) differs from the pipeline's `_compositeFormat`. The composite pipeline's color-target format now matches the attachment by construction, so the MRT-OIT composite can no longer fail WebGPU's format-match validation. Verified no-regression on a translucent OIT scene (0 console/validation errors); full positive verification of the MRT-OIT path needs a Gaussian-splat/forced-OIT scene (that path is fallback-only).
- **NEW-CAPABILITY-GETTER-CODIFY** (A, A13 from the 2026-06-11 ULTRA_REVIEW) — ⚠️ NEARLY CLOSED (Batch 303). The capability-getter-per-feature convention (CLAUDE.md §2: Scene rendering logic branches on `context.supportsX`, never `isWebGPU`/`rendererType`) is the canonical replacement for backend branches; the 2026-05-02 audit migrated the 15-branch / 11-file backlog the 2026-04-30 audit found. Batch 303 swept Scene + non-renderer code for residuals: migrated the one branch that re-appeared after the audit — `ComputeInstanceCollection.js:542` `!context.isWebGPU` → `!context.supportsComputeShaders` (the CPU-fallback gate; the getter is the precise capability — a future WebGL compute extension flips it and skips the fallback automatically). **Remaining residuals are intentionally NOT migrated:** (1) `ViewportQuad.js:144` `if (context.isWebGPU)` — divides on shader-SOURCE FORMAT (WGSL `ShaderSource` vs GLSL) + uniform-map shape, which a capability getter can't express; it is BLOCKED on the Materials API per-backend shader-source virtual method (a separate workstream — `Material` must return per-backend sources). Surfaced per Principle 9 as the concrete next step for a true fix. (2) `isWebGPUDrawCommand` checks (`Scene.js:3038`, `:5030`) are a COMMAND property, not a context branch (the 2026-04-30 audit itself classified these as non-violations). (3) Debug/external queries (`CesiumDebug`, `SceneDebug` label, `Picking.js` pragma-wrapped one-time warning, the `getDebugSnapshot` label) are legitimate per CLAUDE.md §2 ("external/extension code CAN query context type"). (4) Renderer-layer construction dispatch (`Texture3D.js:87` returns a `WebGPUTexture3D`; `ContextFactory`/`ContextRegistry`/worker host pick the backend) is the resource/factory layer that is PERMITTED to know the backend. Verified: `grep` of `Source/Scene` + non-renderer code shows no remaining `isWebGPU`/`rendererType===` branch in rendering logic except the ViewportQuad blocker; `tsc --noEmit` 0 errors; collections-regression green.
- **NEW-MATERIAL-PER-BACKEND-SHADER-SOURCE** (A, surfaced Batch 303 per Principle 9 — the blocker behind the last `NEW-CAPABILITY-GETTER-CODIFY` residual) — `ViewportQuad.js:144` (and any future `Material`-driven primitive on WebGPU) still branches on `context.isWebGPU` to pick between a WGSL `ShaderSource` + Float32Array uniform map and a GLSL `ShaderSource` + the material's `_uniforms` map. This CANNOT be expressed as a capability getter because the divergence is in the shader-SOURCE artifact itself, not a runtime capability. The clean fix: give `Material` a per-backend shader-source virtual method (e.g. `material.getShaderSource(context)` / `material.getUniformMap(context)`) so the caller is backend-agnostic and the WGSL/GLSL selection lives inside the material abstraction (mirrors how `GraphicsContext.createViewportQuadCommand` already virtualizes command creation). Until this lands, `ViewportQuad`'s single `isWebGPU` branch is the sanctioned exception. **Estimated effort:** 1 session (Material API surface + the ~3 built-in material shader pairs that have WGSL twins).

### HIGH — Axis A (WebGPU vs WebGL)

- **NEW-PICK-RAY-ASYNC** — ✅ sampleHeight/clampToHeight SHIPPED (Batch 284); pickFromRay (arbitrary ray) explicitly scoped out. Ray picks used the offscreen-render sync end()→stale-depth path on WebGPU. **History:** Batch 254 (FQ-5) landed only the honesty half — a `oneTimeWarning("WebGPU.rayPick.unsupported", …)` while all three still returned undefined. **Batch 284 makes the high-value half WORK:** `Scene.sampleHeight`/`Scene.clampToHeight` on WebGPU no longer route through the offscreen ray render (whose PickDepth instances never receive `update()`, and whose target depth is LOG-encoded against the MAIN camera, not the offscreen one). Instead `Picking._reconstructHeightSurfaceWebGPU` reuses the main scene's already-rendered depth: project the cartographic/cartesian target into the live view via `SceneTransforms.worldToWindowCoordinates`, reject off-screen positions, then read the surface beneath that pixel via `Picking.pickPositionWorldCoordinates` (the proven Batch-252 full-frustum log reconstruction). Same one-frame-stale sync-cache contract (cold query → undefined + arms readback → converges 1-2 frames). sampleHeight returns the reconstructed surface's height; clampToHeight returns the surface Cartesian3. Limitation: resolves only for positions currently visible in the view, and the reconstructed point lies on the CAMERA ray through the pixel (not the geodetic-normal ray) — near-nadir views match within a few metres, oblique views drift more. **pickFromRay over an ARBITRARY ray stays scoped out** (the offscreen object readback still works → hit object, but `position` is undefined): it now emits `oneTimeWarning("WebGPU.pickFromRay.noPosition", …)` instead of the old shared rayPick warning, and does NOT throw. Building arbitrary-ray async position would need an offscreen GlobeDepth pack + per-view async readback — a separate multi-day item; defer until a consumer needs it. Evidence: `probe-pick-ray-async.mjs` (new, canonical gate) — WebGPU sampleHeight cold→converge frame 1, dH 3.5 m vs WebGL, clampToHeight at exact (-75,40), pickFromRay undefined+warning no-throw, 0 errors; `probe-sampleheight-webgpu.mjs` rewritten from the SAFE-undefined assertion to the working-parity assertion; pickposition / model-pickposition / collections-regression / sandcastle-smoke all green.
- **NEW-PICK-METADATA-READBACK** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 285). `WebGPUPickFramebuffer.readCenterPixel` (consumed by `Picking.pickMetadata` + `Picking.pickVoxelCoordinate`) returned `_lastReadPixels.slice(...)` — the pixel from the most recent REGULAR `scene.pick()` COLOR pass, a STALE pixel from a DIFFERENT pass — and had no re-entrancy guard, so a rapid re-pick could read a half-written staging buffer. **Fix (mirrors PickDepth.getDepth's async contract):** `readCenterPixel` now arms its OWN 1x1 `copyTextureToBuffer` readback of the current center pixel of `_colorTexture` (fresh per-readback staging buffer, destroyed after unmap, never colliding with the color-path `_stagingBuffer`), guarded by a new `_centerReadbackInFlight` flag so an in-flight readback isn't re-read, and returns a one-frame-stale cache keyed to (center coord ±2 px + a `_updateCount` frame stamp advanced once per `begin()`, ≤4 picks stale). A cold query returns `[0,0,0,0]` (caller decodes "no metadata / no voxel") and arms the readback; a re-pick at the same spot 1-2 frames later returns the correct value. `bgra8unorm` byte order is normalized to `[R,G,B,A]` so the decoders see the same layout WebGL's `readPixels` produces. **`Picking.js` reorder:** `pickMetadata` + `pickVoxelCoordinate` now call `context.endFrame()` BEFORE `readCenterPixel` so the metadata/voxel render encoder is submitted ahead of the readback copy (the submission-order hazard documented in `_pickAsyncWithMode`); no-op on WebGL (endFrame only unbinds the default FBO; the pick FBO content persists and readCenterPixel re-binds it). **Bonus fix found during bring-up:** the WebGPU Voxel COLOR pipeline (`WebGPUVoxelRenderer.ts`) was missing the `multisample.count = context._msaaSamples` bake every other scene-FB renderer applies, so on any MSAA scene (default msaaSamples=4) WebGPU dropped every voxel color draw with "Attachment state of [Voxel color pipeline] is not compatible with [Scene Framebuffer Render Pass]" — added the bake + cache-invalidation on sample-count change (pick/velocity pipelines stay single-sample). **Verify:** `probe-pick-metadata.mjs` — drives `readCenterPixel` over a known-pickable opaque Box's pick FBO: WebGPU converges to the same non-zero pick color `[1,0,0,0]` WebGL reads synchronously (proving current-pass read, not stale), the `_centerReadbackInFlight` guard exists + clears after each readback, 0 validation/console errors across 20 rapid re-reads; WebGPU Voxel Pick sandcastle loads with 0 errors (was throwing the attachment-state validation error). **Asset gaps (documented, not papered over):** (1) the WebGPU VoxelRenderer is a SCAFFOLDED placeholder ray-marcher (FEATURE_INVENTORY §B — `VoxelPrimitive.update` returns early, no real voxel data / traversal), so `scene.pickVoxel` can't yet reach `pickVoxelCoordinate` on WebGPU — the LIVE voxel-coordinate parity check is blocked by that deferred functionality (`C-R9-VOXEL-CELL-PICK`), NOT by this readback fix; (2) no zero-dependency local `EXT_structural_metadata` asset exists (all metadata gallery demos use ion tiles), so `pickMetadata`'s full decode path is covered by the shared-readback Box assertion plus the documented manual-gap note. gates: collections-regression / pick-basic / pickposition-webgpu / compute-instance-pick / pickmodel-instanced / logdepth-zfight / sandcastle-smoke all PASS.
- **NEW-TONEMAPPER-STRING-MAP** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 223). `mapTonemapType` read non-existent `_tonemapping.type`/`_tonemappingType` and switched on NUMBERS, so it always returned the default (PBR_NEUTRAL) — `scene.postProcessStages.tonemapper` was a silent no-op. Fixed to read `collection._tonemapper` (the real field) and switch on the STRING `Tonemapper` enum. Verified end-to-end: each string maps to the correct WebGPU `TonemapMode` (REINHARD→0, ACES→1, FILMIC→2, MODIFIED_REINHARD→3, PBR_NEUTRAL→4) which matches the `Tonemapping.wgsl` operator selection.
- **NEW-POSTPROCESS-HDR-INTERMEDIATES** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 225). The four built-in effects (`addBloom`/`addAmbientOcclusion`/`addDepthOfField`/`addGodRay`) passed `canvasFormat` to the effects' `initialize`, so in HDR they allocated 8-bit (bgra8unorm) intermediates that clamped highlights before tonemap. Fixed to pass `this._intermediateFormat || canvasFormat` (rgba16float in HDR, == canvasFormat in SDR → no-op for the common path). Also reset the built-in effects in `WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.initialize()` on any recreate (HDR toggle / resize) — they were created once (`if (this._bloomEffect) return`), so an HDR toggle previously left them holding their first-creation 8-bit/wrong-size textures. Verified: SDR + HDR bloom both render with 0 validation errors (probe).
- **NEW-BLOOM-UNIFORM-PARITY** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 240). Bloom mis-mapped WebGL brightness/contrast onto a luminance threshold (brightness default -0.3 fed as threshold → negative threshold passed EVERYTHING; default bloom bloomed 100% of the frame, measured 1842x WebGL's fraction). Fixed: `BrightPass.wgsl` rewritten as a 1:1 ContrastBias.glsl port (HSB brightness shift via czm_RGBToHSB/czm_HSBToRGB WGSL ports + contrast curve, clamped for HDR intermediates); all six uniforms (contrast/brightness/glowOnly/delta/sigma/stepSize) mapped through the configure path with a full dirty check; `updateConfig` now also rewrites the blur UBOs (delta/sigma/stepSize were init-baked); user stepSize scaled 0.5x for the half-res blur chain (one blur texel = 2 full-res px) so the screen-space footprint matches WebGL; composite intensity default 0.5 → 1.0 (WebGL's composite is plain `bloom + color`); removed the earlier-running FR-sync cache refresh that could mask the configure-pass dirty check. Verified (`probe-bloom-parity.mjs`): default-uniform bloomed-pixel fraction webgl 0.160% vs webgpu 0.161% (ratio 1.01x), glowOnly + brightness changes respond, 0 errors. **Divergences observed while stabilizing the probe (separate items):** WebGPU ground-level daytime sky-atmosphere far brighter than WebGL; WebGPU sun primitive absent at a ground-level 45°-elevation view; no-imagery globe baseColor darker on WebGPU + water-wave material missing.
- **NEW-GROUND-VIEW-ENV-DIVERGENCES** — ✅ SHIPPED Batch 247. Three cross-backend environment divergences at a deterministic ground-level view, all root-caused and fixed; verified by `probe-ground-view-env.mjs` (webgl-vs-webgpu, same scene, numeric). **(3) no-imagery globe baseColor** — NOT an sRGB issue: `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` hardcoded `vec3(0.04,0.04,0.06)` (rgb 10,10,15) as the first-pass base instead of consuming `globe.baseColor`. Fix: wired WebGL's `u_initialColor` through a new `TileUniforms.initialColor` vec4 tail (`TILE_UNIFORM_FLOATS` 476→480, `INITIAL_COLOR_OFFSET` 476; packer reads `tileProvider.baseColor` first-pass / zero subsequent). Now exact rgb(31,38,51) = WebGL. **(2) sun disk missing** — the WebGPU sun command was pushed onto `frameState.commandList` (frustum-binned, executes BEFORE the env-injected skyAtmosphere DUPLICATE), so the alpha-over atmosphere shell (alpha≈1 at ground) erased the disk. Fix: Sun.js adopts the dual-path convention (push for frustum existence AND return for `environmentState.sunDrawCommand`) + SceneRenderer.js env-injection now dedupes against already-binned commands. On a `WebGPUContext` this is NEVER set, so `transcode` throws `"supportedTargetFormats is required"` for ANY KTX2 (even uncompressed RGBA-half-float assets like the kiara IBL cube, which don't need transcoding but still hit the guard). **This blocks NEW-MODEL-IBL-KTX2-CUBEMAP-WEBGPU** (authored env maps) and any other WebGPU KTX2 consumer. **Fix:** register the WebGPU-supported transcode target formats during `WebGPUContext` init — map WebGPU `GPUFeatureName`s (`texture-compression-bc` → S3TC/BC7, `texture-compression-etc2` → ETC, `texture-compression-astc` → ASTC) to the `KTX2Transcoder.setKTX2SupportedFormats(...)` flags (mirror the WebGL `Context` detection block). Uncompressed KTX2 then passes the guard and returns raw mip buffers. **Probe:** `diag-ktx2-ibl-shape.mjs` (NEW — dumps the loadKTX2 result + the IBL load-chain state; currently shows the throw) + `probe-model-ktx2-ibl.mjs`. **Effort:** ~1 session.

- **NEW-CSM-GLOBE-RECEIVE-PROJECTION-MISS** — ✅ ROOT CAUSE FIXED (Batch 298). The globe-terrain CSM receiver now DARKENS the ground where a caster's shadow falls (the reported symptom is gone). **Root cause = suspect (b): the cascade light-eye was on the WRONG side.** `WebGPUCSMRenderer._computeCascadeVPMatrix` placed the light camera at `eye = center − lightDir·2r` with `forward = center − eye = +lightDir` (looking back TOWARD the sun, from the anti-sun side). A shadow-casting light camera must sit on the LIGHT side and look along the light's travel direction (`forward = −lightDir`). The mirrored projection recorded the caster's depth mirrored about the cascade center, so a ground point in a wall's umbra and the wall occluding it projected to DIFFERENT shadow-map texels — the ground's projected UV read the cleared (lit) depth. Suspect (a) was RULED OUT first via the new trace probe: the globe's `encodedCameraPositionMC` (high+low) reconstructs to `cameraWC` byte-for-byte identically to the cast pass's `EncodedCartesian3.fromCartesian(cameraPositionWC)` (`globeVsCastMeters = 0`, `eyeDeltaMeters = 0`), and the globe receiver's projected `(uv, ndc.z)` equals the cast reconstruction's exactly (`uvDelta = 0`, `ndcZDelta = 0`). **Trace tool (NEW):** `probe-csm-globe-receive-trace.mjs` + three debug hooks on `WebGPUCSMRenderer` — `debugCascadeMatrices()` (per-cascade RTE VP + sphere center/radius), `debugReadCascadeDepth(ci,u,v)` (single-texel cast-depth readback; copies a full layer + indexes — a partial-row copy with non-zero origin read back as 0 on the Vulkan/SwiftShader path), `debugScanCascadeLayer(ci)` (layer min/max/histogram). The cascade texture gained `COPY_SRC` usage for these. - **NEW-PERINSTANCE-DIFFUSE-PARITY** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 326). A lit `PerInstanceColorAppearance` (`flat:false`) primitive rendered its diffuse-shaded body noticeably DARKER on WebGPU than WebGL under the same light, independent of shadows (probe reproduced WebGPU body lum **92.5 vs WebGL 120.2**, ratio 0.77 — the same gap as the originally-reported ~92 vs ~154). **Root cause:** the WGSL primitive-lit fragments `phong` / `phongTextured` (`PrimitivePhongColor.wgsl` / `PrimitivePhongTexturedColor.wgsl`, the shaders `selectWebGPUShader` routes the lit color/per-instance-color appearances to) used an **ad-hoc Blinn-Phong term** — `lighting = 0.15 (ambient) + (0.7·max(dot(N, L_sun),0) + 0.15·spec) · shadowFactor` — that diverged from the GLSL reference `czm_phong` (`Builtin/Functions/phong.glsl`) used by `PerInstanceColorAppearanceFS` (and `AllMaterialAppearanceFS`). Two concrete divergences darkened the surface: (1) it keyed the diffuse on the **sun direction** `camera.lightDirection`, whereas `czm_phong` keys diffuse on **two FIXED eye-space light directions** — `+Z` (toward the eye, for top-down) plus `+Y` (up, for 3D horizon views) — summing to `0..2`; (2) it used a **0.15 ambient floor** instead of `czm_phong`'s `materialDiffuse = color·0.5` ambient (effectively a 0.5 floor), and applied a `0.7` diffuse weight instead of `0.5`. So `czm_phong` resolves to `out = color · 0.5 · (1 + diffuse)` (czm_lightColor = white, non-HDR) while the WGSL bottomed out near `0.15 + 0.7·NdotL_sun`. **Fix (WGSL-only):** replaced the diffuse/ambient/specular block in both `phong` and `phongTextured` with the czm_phong model — `diffuse = max(dot(N,+Z),0) + max(dot(N,+Y),0)`, `lighting = 0.5 + 0.5·diffuse·shadowFactor`, specular dropped (material.specular is 0 for these color appearances so the GLSL specular contributes nothing). `lightDir` is retained solely for the CSM slope-bias / cascade-sampling path. **Verified:** new `Tools/visual-regression/probe-perinstance-diffuse.mjs` (lit `flat:false` extruded polygon, globe hidden, shadows OFF, fixed light, top-down) — pre-fix WebGPU 92.5 / WebGL 120.2 (relErr 23.1%, FAIL); post-fix WebGPU **120.1 / WebGL 120.2 (ratio 1.000, relErr 0.0%, 0 errors, PASS)**; B/A PNGs visually identical. No regression: `probe-phong-render` (RENDERS OK, 0 errors), `probe-clustered-phong` (PASS, clustered additive lighting still layers correctly on the new base term), `probe-csm-soft-shadow` (6/6 PASS, ratio 1.24×, 0 errors); WebGL `PerInstanceColorAppearance` + `MaterialAppearance` + all `*Appearance` specs green (47 SUCCESS); `tsc` clean. **Files:** `PrimitivePhongColor.wgsl`, `PrimitivePhongTexturedColor.wgsl`, `probe-perinstance-diffuse.mjs`. **NOTE / follow-up:** the separate MaterialAppearance lit shaders (`PrimitiveMatColorLit.wgsl` et al.) carry the *same* ad-hoc Blinn-Phong term and so are still darker than their `czm_phong` WebGL reference — distinct WGSL files (not shared with `phong`), so untouched here. Tracked as **NEW-MATAPPEARANCE-DIFFUSE-PARITY** below.

  - **ROOT-CAUSE PREREQUISITE (confirmed Batch 226, 2nd attempt):** added a backend-agnostic monotonic `_instanceVersion` bumped in `_updateBillboard`; the FR rebuilds when it advances (recorded, never reset). The version-signal is CORRECT (a color change and a position change each bumped it + triggered a rebuild) but it STILL rebuilt ~2×/frame for "static" billboards → **`_updateBillboard` is being called every frame for settled billboards on the WebGPU path** (the `runSharedSceneLogic` readiness loop / unreset `_createVertexArray`). So **step 0 for ANY dirty-gate is stopping the WebGPU collection path from re-dirtying settled billboards each frame** (replicate WebGL's "dirties consumed" semantics, or compute a true source-changed signal that ignores the per-frame re-touch). Both gate attempts are blocked on this, not on the gate logic itself.
  - **DESIGN DECISION (owner Q, 2026-06-11 — supersedes "all-or-nothing gate"):** the right target is **per-INSTANCE partial sub-range writes**, not the all-or-nothing rebuild. WebGPU's whole-buffer rebuild is O(N) per change-frame; for "micro-updates to tens of thousands of objects" (sparse changes in a huge collection) the fix is a **resident CPU instance array + `device.queue.writeBuffer(buf, K*stride, …, stride)` per changed instance** (O(changed), e.g. ~640 B for 10-of-50k vs 3.2 MB). This NEEDS the per-instance dirty list (`_billboardsToUpdate[0.._billboardsToUpdateIndex]`) — but does NOT need WebGL's per-ATTRIBUTE separate buffers (keep interleaved for draw-time cache locality; re-writing a changed instance's full 64 B record is fine). Extreme per-frame churn (100k+ all moving) → GPU-resident scatter via compute / storage buffer (no CPU round-trip). **Best home: a shared resident-instance-buffer manager with dirty-range tracking (pairs with NEW-COLLECTION-RENDERER-BASE), used by billboard/label/point.** Do probe-driven in a dedicated session after the step-0 re-touch fix.

Dynamic offsets are 256-aligned by the ring allocator (and 0 on the first-frame fallback), satisfying `minUniformBufferOffsetAlignment`. The `_pipelineLayout` is unchanged (dynamic-offset is a BGL-entry property, transparent to pipelines), so all globe pipeline variants pick it up automatically. The offsets thread through `TileDrawDescriptor.bindGroup0DynamicOffsets` → the scene-adapter command's `_bindGroup0DynamicOffsets` → the `execute` closure (covers opaque, translucent, depth-only pre-pass, wireframe). Verified (`probe-globe-bindgroup-cache.mjs`, new Phase E sustained-pan): group-0 creations during 120 panning frames dropped from ~15 (max 3/frame, churn in 9 frames) to **0** (group-0 lifetime entries capped at 3 = pageCount, vs 63 before); group-1 imagery churn = 23-27 over the same window proves the motion actually streamed tiles (non-vacuous); steady-state + teleport-pan + visual + zero-error phases all still PASS; 99.6% lifetime hit rate. - **NEW-GLOBE-RENDERBUNDLE-CACHE** — ✅ RESOLVED (Batch 292, dropped-as-net-negative). The globe pass built and discarded a `GPURenderBundle` every frame (create encoder → record every tile command → `finish()` → `executeBundles`). Render bundles only amortize when CACHED and replayed across many frames; this one was rebuilt from scratch each frame, paying full construction cost with zero amortization. It also CANNOT be safely cached: each globe command records `setBindGroup(0, bg0, [cameraOffset, tileOffset])` with the per-tile ring-allocator dynamic offsets BAKED IN at record time, and those offsets rotate every frame (the per-frame ring allocator cycles pages by design — NEW-GLOBE-DYNAMIC-OFFSET-UBO made the bind-GROUP object stable but the dynamic-OFFSET *values* still change frame-to-frame), so a cached bundle would replay stale offsets and bind the wrong UB slices; a signature-keyed cache including the offsets would miss every frame. Measured (`probe-globe-bundle-cost.mjs`, 55-tile low view): the bundle path ran ~0.3-0.4 ms SLOWER at the median than direct `executeBatch`, with a markedly worse p90 (build-cost spikes ~7.0 ms vs ~4.6 ms). **Decision: dropped the inline bundle** — `executeGlobeDispatch` now falls straight through to `executeBatch`. p90 frame cost improved to the no-bundle regime; unused imports (`isSceneFBMrtMode`, `MRT_NORMAL_ROUGHNESS_FORMAT`, `WebGPUContext` type) removed. The `WebGPURenderBundleManager` infrastructure is untouched (still used by other paths); the file docstring records the constraint so a future session doesn't re-add an inline globe bundle without first making the per-tile UBs frame-stable.

- **NEW-CAMERA-JITTER-ACCUMULATION** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 322). TAA sub-pixel jitter accumulated unboundedly on a stable frustum: `Scene.js` did `proj[8] += jitter.x; proj[9] += jitter.y` against `cam.frustum.projectionMatrix`, which is a DIRTY-CACHED getter — on a settled camera (stable fov/aspect/near/far) it returns the SAME array every frame without recomputing, so each frame's `+=` stacked on top of the last and proj[8]/proj[9] drifted ~linearly (a random walk with non-zero-mean IGN drift; measured peak ~5× maxJitter over 120 frames, growing with frame count). On a CHANGING frustum the matrix recomputed to its un-jittered base each frame so the old `+=` happened to be correct there. **Fix:** new `WebGPUTAAEffect.applyProjectionJitter(proj, jitterX, jitterY)` writes `base + jitter` ABSOLUTELY each frame — it tracks the un-jittered base (`_jitterBase8/9`) + last-applied jitter (`_jitterLastX/Y`); if the live `proj[8]/[9]` no longer equals `(storedBase + lastJitter)` within 1e-9 the frustum recomputed to a fresh base → re-capture it, then set `proj[8] = base8 + jitterX; proj[9] = base9 + jitterY`. Robust to BOTH the settled-cached case (bounded at base±maxJitter, no accumulation) AND the recomputed case (self-heals). The frozen/snapshot branch now calls `resetProjectionJitter()` (NaN-sentinels the base) alongside zeroing `jitterX/jitterY` so re-enabling can't reason about a stale base; the non-frozen branch still routes through `computeJitter` which sets `jitterX/jitterY` for the TAA shader. WebGL untouched (whole block gated by `scene.taaEnabled` + WebGPU-only `_alternateSceneRenderer?._postProcess`). **Spec:** `WebGPUTAAJitterAccumulationSpec.js` (5 cases, pure CPU/no GPU) — 120-frame stable-frustum bounded-drift assertion (per-frame + peak ≤ maxJitter), a negative control proving the old `+=` drifts >3× maxJitter, exact-`base+jitter` write, self-heal-on-recompute, and reset-then-recapture. Files: `WebGPUTAAEffect.ts`, `Scene.js`, `WebGPUTAAJitterAccumulationSpec.js` (+ `SpecList.js` registration).
  - **RE-SCOPE (2026-06-20 audit) — this is DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH, not a fix for a reproduced live drift.** The unbounded-accumulation precondition (a dirty-cached projection getter returning the SAME array every frame so `+=` stacks) is generally ABSENT in the live WebGPU render loop: `WebGPUSceneRenderer._updateFrustumUniforms` (`WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:1437`) sets `frustum.near/far` + NaN-sentinels the frustum cache (`frustumCache._near/_far = NaN`) and calls `uniformState.updateFrustum(frustum)` **every frame per frustum**, recomputing the camera-frustum projection from scratch — which invalidates the very near/far cache the Batch-322 random-walk assumed was stale. So the Batch-322 absolute-write is correct and worth keeping (it self-heals on recompute AND bounds the hypothetical settled-cache case), but it should NOT be read as having fixed an observed, reproduced TAA drift in the live loop. The spec's 120-frame drift is a synthetic stable-frustum harness, not the production code path.
  - **CROSS-REF — the deeper REAL gap (tracked separately, see NEW-TAA-PROJECTION-JITTER-OVERWRITTEN below):** that same per-frame `_updateFrustumUniforms` recompute OVERWRITES the projection jitter `Scene.js` applies to the camera frustum projection — the recomputed un-jittered projection lands in the uniform buffer BEFORE any draw, so the **projection-jitter half of TAA never reaches the GPU** on WebGPU. The history-reprojection/velocity half still works, but sub-pixel sample-position dithering (the part that actually anti-aliases static edges) is silently dropped. This is the substantive TAA-quality gap; the Batch-322 accumulation guard does not address it.
- **NEW-TAA-PROJECTION-JITTER-OVERWRITTEN** (M) — ✅ **SHIPPED Batch 358** (`WebGPUSceneRenderer._updateFrustumUniforms` now re-applies `taaEffect.jitterX/Y` to the per-frustum projection before `uniformState.updateFrustum` captures it; `setProjection` clones it + marks every dependent matrix dirty so the jitter flows into the camera UB; gated on `taaEnabled` → zero-op when off. Verified baseline-isolated via new `probe-taa-jitter.mjs`: WebGPU TAA-on projection center-offset 0 → 0.000828, TAA-off = 0). **Was Open (surfaced by the 2026-06-20 TAA audit; see NEW-CAMERA-JITTER-ACCUMULATION cross-ref above).** On WebGPU the projection-jitter half of TAA never reaches the GPU. `Scene.js` applies the per-frame sub-pixel jitter to the **camera frustum projection** (via `WebGPUTAAEffect.applyProjectionJitter`, Batch 322), but `WebGPUSceneRenderer._updateFrustumUniforms` (`WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:1437`) then recomputes the projection from the frustum's near/far each frame (`frustumCache._near/_far = NaN` → `uniformState.updateFrustum(frustum)`) and writes that **un-jittered** projection into the camera uniform buffer before any draw — clobbering the jitter. Net effect: history reprojection + motion-vector accumulation work, but the sub-pixel sample-position dithering that actually anti-aliases static edges is dropped, so WebGPU TAA under-resolves compared to WebGL. **Needs:** carry the TAA jitter THROUGH the per-frame frustum-uniform recompute — either jitter the projection AFTER `updateFrustum` inside `_updateFrustumUniforms` (so the recompute can't overwrite it), or fold the jitter into the projection the uniform pack reads, gated on `scene.taaEnabled` + non-frozen. Must preserve the Batch-322 absolute-write semantics (no re-introduced accumulation) and stay WebGL-untouched. **Files (investigation start):** `WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts` (`_updateFrustumUniforms` ~L1437–1483), `WebGPUTAAEffect.ts` (`applyProjectionJitter`), `Scene.js` (jitter application site). **Trace:** NEW-CAMERA-JITTER-ACCUMULATION re-scope, 2026-06-20.
- **NEW-BINDGROUPCACHE-EVICTION** — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 293). The generic post-process bind-group cache (`WebGPUBindGroupCache`, used by Bloom/SSAO/DoF/GodRays/AutoExposure) keyed each bind group on `(layout id + per-entry resource identity)` in an UNBOUNDED `Map<string, GPUBindGroup>` with eviction only via explicit `invalidateAll()`. In the failure mode its own docstring warns about — input texture views recreated every frame WITHOUT a matching `invalidateAll` (the "0% hit rate" symptom) — the key set grew by one per frame forever, leaking a `GPUBindGroup` (≈150-300 B of driver state) each frame for the whole session. Fix: bounded LRU + optional age eviction. Map iteration order is kept as a recency list (each hit re-inserts the entry at the tail via delete+set), so the first key is the LRU → O(1) `_evictLRU()` on any miss that would exceed `maxEntries` (default 1024 — far above any real effect's stable key set, which is single-digit). New `beginFrame()` advances a frame clock and, when `maxIdleFrames > 0` (default 0 = LRU-only), drops entries idle past the window. Constructor now takes an optional `BindGroupCacheOptions { maxEntries, maxIdleFrames }`; all six existing callers use the no-arg form and are unaffected (default cap applies). `getStats()` gains an `evictions` counter. Verified: `WebGPUBindGroupCacheSpec.js` +7 tests (30/30 green) — cap never exceeded, LRU touch protects recently-hit entries, **500 frames of per-frame identity churn stays bounded at ≤16 entries (was +1/frame unbounded pre-fix)**, age eviction drops/keeps by window, `maxIdleFrames=0` does no age eviction. Regression: bloom-parity (post-process cache live path), collections-regression, globe-bindgroup-cache, sandcastle-smoke all PASS. **Companion IDs left open (assessed this batch):** `NEW-RENDERBUNDLE-AGING-DECOUPLE` — `WebGPURenderBundleManager` ALREADY has full bounded LRU (`_maxCacheSize`/`_evictOldest`) + age eviction (`_maxIdleFrames`/`_evictStale`) driven by `beginFrame()`, so it is NOT an unbounded-growth gap; this ID is purely the "decouple aging from the frame tick" refinement, deferred. `NEW-RESOURCEMANAGER-KEY-EVICTION` — `WebGPUResourceManager`'s sampler + BGL caches key on `JSON.stringify(descriptor)`; both key spaces are naturally finite (a finite set of sampler descriptors and pipeline layouts per app), so realistic growth is bounded — lower value, deferred.

### MEDIUM / LOW (23)

**`NEW-DECOUPLEDSCAN-FORWARD-PROGRESS-GUARD` (A2.3) — ✅ SHIPPED (C4 queue, 2026-07-04).** The decoupled-lookback prefix-sum kernel (`DecoupledLookbackScan.wgsl`, opt-in via `useDeterministicPointCloudLOD`/`useDecoupledScan`, default OFF) spun on peer-workgroup partitions with an UNBOUNDED `loop { atomicLoad; if !empty break; storageBarrier() }`. WebGPU guarantees no cross-workgroup forward progress, so that spin could livelock/hang the device when a predecessor partition is never scheduled (occupancy < dispatch size). **Latent bug surfaced en route:** the `storageBarrier()` sat inside the lane-0-only lookback (`if (localIdx == 0u)`) — non-uniform control flow — which is a WGSL COMPILE ERROR ("'storageBarrier' must only be called from uniform control flow"), so the entire scan module failed to compile and the scan path was silently dead (only ever "verified" by mock-device specs; the sole runtime consumer, PointCloudLOD, has no Scene wiring yet). **Fix:** (1) removed the illegal `storageBarrier()` — `atomicLoad` on the read_write storage atomic already re-reads device memory each iteration (atomics can't be hoisted/CSE'd), so peer stores stay visible without a fence; (2) added a WGSL iteration-cap watchdog (`MAX_LOOKBACK_SPINS = 1<<20`, shared budget across the whole lookback) that abandons the spin and terminates the kernel instead of hanging; (3) host-side occupancy gate in `WebGPUDecoupledScan` (`maxSafeWorkgroups`, default = `device.limits.maxComputeWorkgroupsPerDimension` — pure capability gate, no false trips) exposed as `canDispatch(n)`; `dispatch()` refuses (returns false, encodes nothing) when it trips and emits a PERMANENT throttled `console.error` sentinel (CLAUDE.md loop-sentinel mandate); (4) `WebGPUPointCloudLODProcessor.dispatch` now checks `canDispatch` and falls back to the atomic-compaction path when unsafe (byte-identical when `useDecoupledScan` is false — the gate lives inside the opt-in branch). **Verified:** `probe-decoupledscan-progress-guard.mjs` (real GPU, injects built WGSL) — shader now COMPILES, correct inclusive prefix sum across 16 wg (4000 ones), ragged 13-wg random tail, and 391 wg (100000 ones) terminating in ~22 ms; `WebGPUDecoupledScanSpec` 10/10 (4 new gate tests), `WebGPUPointCloudLODProcessorSpec` 7/7, `probe-pointcloud-lod` PASS, `tsc` clean. **Files:** `Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/DecoupledLookbackScan.wgsl`, `WebGPUDecoupledScan.ts`, `WebGPUPointCloudLODProcessor.ts`, `WebGPUDecoupledScanSpec.js`, `Tools/visual-regression/probe-decoupledscan-progress-guard.mjs`.

**`NS-DECOUPLEDSCAN-NO-SCENE-WIRING` — ✅ SHIPPED (Campaign 5).** Follow-on to the forward-progress guard above: the GPU point-cloud LOD processor compiled and had the guard, but its opt-in path (`pointCloud.enableGPULOD`, read by `WebGPUPointCloudRenderer`) had NO public Scene control, so the deterministic decoupled-scan path was never reachable in-product — it could only ever be verified by direct-dispatch probes. `PointCloud.js` is instantiated ONLY by `TimeDynamicPointCloud`, so the wiring is a single owner. **Fix (Scene wiring, default OFF / byte-identical when off):** (1) added a public `gpuLOD` boolean (default `false`) to `PointCloudShading`; (2) `TimeDynamicPointCloud.renderFrame` now maps `pointCloud.enableGPULOD = shading.gpuLOD === true` alongside the other `shading.*` → `pointCloud.*` mappings. #### `NEW-CLUSTER-MULTIFRUSTUM-BOUNDS` — premise reconciled 2026-07-05 (PERF-only, NOT a correctness gap)

Verified against live code + a Playwright probe. `WebGPUSceneRendererClusteredLighting.ts:208-219` collapses the whole visible depth into a SINGLE cluster grid built from `scene.camera.frustum.near/far`, and B572 (`NEW-CLUSTERED-ASSIGN-BOUNDS-DIRTY`) already fixed the bounds→assign re-dispatch. The remaining "multi-frustum" item is **not** a binning-correctness or WebGL-parity gap:

- **Self-consistent → conservatively correct.** The FS `clusterIndexFor` (`ClusteredLighting.wgsl`) uses the *identical* collapsed near/far + *identical* exponential slice mapping as the `ClusterBounds` compute pass, so every fragment lands in the cluster whose AABB actually contains it — regardless of how many render frustums the scene splits into. Coarse Z-slices make a cluster over-*include* lights (a superset), never drop the ones that belong; the per-light `dist > range → 0` cutoff in `evalSingleClusteredLight` zeroes any over-included light. Result: pixel-identical output vs a per-frustum grid.
- **WebGPU-only feature — no WebGL reference.** Cesium has no Forward+ clustered lighting in WebGL, so there is nothing to match. Off by default (`scene.clusteredLightingEnabled=false`), byte-identical when off.
- **Per-cluster overflow is not solved by per-frustum grids anyway** — `CLUSTER_MAX_LIGHTS_PER_CLUSTER=256` per cluster vs `CLUSTER_MAX_LIGHTS=1024` total; per-frustum grids redistribute Z-resolution but keep the same per-cluster cap and 24 slices.
- **Acceptance evidence:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-clustered-multifrustum.mjs` — a genuine 19-frustum scene (log-depth split via lowered `logarithmicDepthFarToNearRatio`) shows the model correctly lit by a clustered point light (40,958 changed px, max Δ 430, 0 device errors); the model renders identically OFF/ON and only brightens where the light reaches. Standing `probe-clustered-visible.mjs` still PASS.

Per-frustum-slice cluster grids remain a **deferred performance / Z-resolution optimization** (tighter binning near the camera → fewer lights evaluated per fragment in deep scenes). It would add per-frustum grid selection threaded through every consumer draw inside the frustum loop — a new correctness surface — for zero visible change. Left deferred; the existing `:208-219` comment ("Per-frustum-slice cluster bounds are a future optimization") is accurate as-is.

## 2026-06-11 — Large Dynamic Objects roadmap (32 new IDs)

Full roadmap + regime→architecture decision table + per-phase design: [LARGE_DYNAMIC_OBJECTS_DESIGN.md](LARGE_DYNAMIC_OBJECTS_DESIGN.md). Owner-directed: pick architecture by UPDATE REGIME (sparse→partial-write; dense-arbitrary→flat-buffer+WASM; dense-derivable/orbital→GPU-compute; 100k+ arbitrary→ECS-worker). Scoped by the `large-dynamic-objects-roadmap-scope` workflow (6 agents, grounded in fork code). **Step 0 shipped: billboard (b4a9e58fd9) + label glyph (7e24700f8a).** Most substrate already exists in-tree (compute engine, storage-buffer pool, SoA Buffer* collections, WASM RTE-encode bridge, weather-particle compute→instanced-draw precedent); the greenfield is SGP4 (Phase 3) + the ECS (Phase 4, likely unnecessary).

The cloud color pipeline never baked the scene-FB MSAA sample count (`multisample` absent → count=1) while the scene framebuffer pass is MSAA — the attachment-state validation error **invalidated the entire pass encoder, so adding a single cloud blanked EVERY primitive in the scene** (confirmed pre-existing at HEAD: baseline probe rendered 0 cyan polyline px with clouds present, 1683 without). Fix mirrors the Billboard Batch-134 pattern: `multisample: {count}` from `context._msaaSamples` baked into the cloud pipeline descriptor + `ms=` keyed into the descriptor name. After the fix: 0 validation errors, clouds render, polylines render in the same scene. (Velocity pipeline untouched — targets the single-sample rg16float velocity texture.)
- **NEW-CLOUD-SCALE-METERS** — ✅ FOUND + FIXED (Batch 253, caught by the final-sweep run of probe-polyline-cloud-consume — the first since the Batch-251 log-depth flip). `WebGPUCloudRenderer`'s VS sized the quad as `quadPos * scale / viewportSize * 2 * clip.w` — `CumulusCloud.scale` interpreted as SCREEN PIXELS, distance-invariant — while upstream `CloudCollectionVS.glsl` applies `positionEC.xy += scale * offset` (METERS in eye space). The probe's 2000x1000 m clouds rendered as full-screen white quads at its 1.5 Mm camera, washing out the asserted polylines. Masked pre-flip: hyperbolic z-compression at that range made the cloud z-tie/lose against the globe, so the blown-up quads were depth-rejected; the log flip made them correctly WIN and exposed the sizing bug. Fix: clip offset = `quadPos * scale * (P00, P11)` (exact projection of an eye-space lateral offset for symmetric perspective AND ortho frusta), P00/P11 packed into the former `_pad0`/`_pad1` UB lanes (floats 19/23, no resize), both vertexMain and vertexVelocityMain. `probe-cloud-property-edit` re-parameterized to meters-era values (2000x1300 m at 15 km). Evidence: polyline-cloud-consume cyan 0→2174 (WebGL control 1914), collections-regression cloud 1774 px (still >100 gate), cloud-property-edit changedPixels=116389. Ported the full volumetric FS into `CLOUD_WGSL`: ray-vs-ellipsoid intersection (`0.82 * maximumSize`, optional `slice` plane), Gardner (1985) analytic texture function, diffuse/specular/texture shading `I()`, and 3-channel worley-FBM erosion (inline port of `CloudNoiseFS.glsl`'s worley, normalized by cloud radius — in place of the baked 3D-packed-2D noise texture). SLICE=64 / DETAIL=8 (vs WebGL 128/16) is chosen so the sampled W value at any cloudPoint is **identical** to WebGL — both reduce to `worleyFBM(cloudPoint mod 8)` (same wrapRange=8 cell points from `random3`, same tile period) — at 1/8 the gen cost; 512 wrapped cell-points precomputed so the per-voxel loop has no trig (gen <1 frame even at 1024×256). The raymarch + Gardner + TR + color WGSL are line-by-line ALGORITHMICALLY IDENTICAL to `CloudCollectionFS.glsl` (verified) and W now matches exactly — so the residual size/density gap is a NON-shader cause (camera/projection/maxSize-delivery or a WebGL-specific quad-projection quirk), not the noise. So the WebGPU cloud quad was exactly **2× too wide** → the raymarched cloud rendered ~1.9× WebGL's size. `vOffset = quadPos*0.5` (the raymarch coordinate) was ALREADY correctly halved, so the fix is a single `* 0.5` on the quad offset in `vertexMain` + `vertexVelocityMain` — the raymarch coordinate is unchanged. **Verified** (`probe-cloud-volumetric-parity.mjs`, PNGs READ): WebGPU filled-px **7746 → 1947 vs WebGL 1797 (4.3× → 1.08×)**, area ratio **2.41× → 0.99×**; the two clouds are now visually near-identical (same ~63 px grainy core). Didn't-break: probe-cloud-property-edit PASS; probe-collections-regression cloud gate re-baselined 100→50 (the 3 small clouds now correctly render ~85 green px at the corrected half-size — the anticipated "cloud thresholds need re-baseline"), PASS. **Completes the cloud trilogy:** B363 shape (volumetric raymarch) + B365 grain (baked worley) + B366 size (`*0.5` half-extent) → WebGPU CloudCollection now matches WebGL on all three axes. (The earlier "non-shader cause" hypothesis was right that it wasn't the noise; the lever was the quad half-extent in the VS, not a projection-divide subtlety.) **Files:** `WebGPUCloudRenderer.ts` only.

### Phase 1 — Per-instance partial-write manager (sparse-dynamic regime)

Debug-pragma counters `_fullRebuilds`/`_partialWrites`/`_bytesUploaded`/`_prevMirrorWrites`. Verified: probe-billboard-partial-write.mjs (static 1000-billboard scene → 0 uploads over 30 frames; 1 moved billboard → exactly 1 partial write of 176 B = 1 stride, renders at the new position) + probe-resident-instance-prev-mirror.mjs (prev-mirror write contract, intercepted writes).

The three mandated permanent sentinels (CLAUDE.md "Permanent sentinels to add for new subsystems") live in `WebGPUCollectionRendererBase.ts`: (1) **Re-entry / infinite-loop guard** — `beginCollectionFrame`/`endCollectionFrame` bracket each renderer's `update*`; a per-collection depth past a SANE LIMIT (16, generous vs any legitimate frustum-slice/pass concurrency) `console.error`s (throttled 3 s) — catches a runaway recursive command-list build (BUG-12 "clear loop" family applied to collections). (2) **Null-target guard** — for the resident-instance collections (Billboard / Point / Label), `validateInstanceSyncResult` `console.error`s when the manager returns a null buffer for a non-zero visible count (a draw with no vertex buffer is a hard bug) and tells the caller to skip the draw; for the explicit-buffer collections (Cloud / Polyline), `validateDrawTargets` does the same null check at the render-pass boundary for the segment/instance/quad vertex buffers. (3) **Size-validation / overflow guard** — the pick path uses `writePickInstances` (`console.error` + CLAMP the pick `writeBuffer` to the allocated capacity); the instanced color/velocity/pick draws of Cloud / Polyline / Label glyphs use `validateInstancedDrawBuffer`, which `console.error`s + CLAMPS the drawn instance count to what the vertex/instance buffer physically holds (`instanceCount × bytesPerInstance ≤ buffer.size`) instead of issuing an out-of-range instanced draw that aborts the command encoder (BUG-15 family). **Batch 331 wiring:** Cloud (56 B/instance, color + velocity commands) and Polyline (`BYTES_PER_SEGMENT`/instance, color + velocity + pick commands) got `validateDrawTargets` + `validateInstancedDrawBuffer`; Label (no base usage before) got the full set — re-entry bracket via a new `_updateWebGPULabelsInner` split, `validateInstanceSyncResult` replacing its silent null-buffer return, and `validateInstancedDrawBuffer` (`BYTES_PER_SDF_INSTANCE`) on the glyph SDF color + velocity draws. (Label's pick is delegated to the Billboard FR, which already carries the sentinels.) All sentinels are PERMANENT (no debug pragma) — they indicate broken output that must reach production consoles — and ADDITIVE (a counter add + a null check + a size compare; inert on the happy path). ### Phase 2 — Flat-buffer Buffer* + WASM encode (dense-arbitrary regime)

- ~~**NEW-WASMRTE-SUBRANGE-ENCODE** (S) — Sub-range variant of WasmRTEBridge.batchEncode (encode dirty [offset,count) at offset).~~ **SHIPPED Batch 271.** Added `batchEncodeRange(positions, srcOffset, count, outHigh, outLow, dstOffset?)` to `WasmRTEBridge.js` — encodes the contiguous `[srcOffset, srcOffset+count)` slice into the `[dstOffset, ..)` output window IN PLACE (untouched output bytes preserved), so an incremental repack can patch only its dirty slice. `dstOffset` defaults to `srcOffset`. Implemented as **JS-side pointer arithmetic over the EXISTING `batch_rte_encode` kernel** (copy the dirty slice to the front of the RTE arena, encode from index 0, read the result back into the dst window) — **NO new Rust export, NO WASM rebuild**. The scalar JS fallback (`_encodeRangeJS`) uses the same fround split (`high=fround(v); low=fround(v-high)`) as both `batchEncode` and the wasm32 kernel, so the two paths are byte-identical. Honors the bridge contract (threshold gate, feature-detect, arena-slot alloc, try/catch → JS fallback). **Also fixed a latent bug surfaced while verifying:** the wasm-bindgen glue does NOT re-export `memory`, so `_wasmModule.__wbindgen_export_0 ?? _wasmModule.memory` was `undefined` and the WASM path of EVERY RTE encode was silently catching + falling back to JS. `loadWasm` now captures the exports object returned by `__wbg_init()` (which carries `.memory`) into `_wasmExports`; a new `_wasmMemory()` helper resolves it for `_encodeWasm`/`_encodeRangeWasm`/`_toEyeWasm` (output unchanged — JS fallback was byte-exact — but the WASM kernel now actually runs). VERIFY: `Tools/wasm-subrange-encode-check.mjs` (standalone node, drives the REAL bridge via an ESM resolve-hook loader + a fetch shim that feeds the on-disk `.wasm`) — 18 assertions: WASM vs JS byte-identity over an interior sub-range, equality to an independent reference fround encode, dst-offset placement, untouched-byte preservation, src≠dst relocation, full-range == whole-array `batchEncode`, default-dstOffset, and a trip-wire that FAILS if any "using JS fallback" warning fires (so the WASM kernel is proven to genuinely run). All pass; `npx tsc --noEmit` + `npx gulp build` green; collections-regression + buffer-logdepth + far-camera + orbital-catalog + sandcastle-smoke probes PASS.
- ~~**NEW-BUFFERCOLL-WASM-ENCODE-WIRE** (M) — Route WasmRTEBridge encode into WebGPU+WebGL Buffer* repack hot paths, threshold-gated.~~ **SHIPPED Batch 272.** `batchEncodeRange` is now wired into both `WebGPUBufferPointRenderer.repackPointDirty` (WebGPU) and `Scene/renderBufferPointCollection.js` (WebGL2). When `_dirtyCount >= BUFFER_WASM_ENCODE_THRESHOLD` (5000) AND `_positionView instanceof Float64Array`, the POSITION high/low lanes for the whole contiguous dirty slice are encoded in ONE `batchEncodeRange(_positionView, dirtyOffset, dirtyCount, posHigh, posLow, dirtyOffset)` call (points have `vertexOffset == index`, so the slice is contiguous and maps 1:1 onto `posHigh[i*3..]`). Color/pick/outline interleave + pick-id creation + per-primitive `_dirty` clear stay in the JS loop. Below threshold (or FLOAT positions) the per-primitive scalar `EncodedCartesian3` loop runs as before. Bridge is lazily `new`'d on the cache/renderContext with a fire-and-forget `loadWasm()`; destroyed on teardown. A per-collection `_wasmEncodeThresholdOverride` lets the probe force scalar/batch on the SAME collection. **Encode equivalence (the key correctness point):** the batch path uses the fround split (`high=f32(v); low=f32(v-high)`) while the scalar `EncodedCartesian3` uses the AGI 65536-grid split — the high/low BYTES differ, but both satisfy `high+low == value` exactly in f64, so the shader's RTE reconstruction `(posHigh-camHigh)+(posLow-camLow)` rounds to the SAME eye-space position (verified numerically: 0.0m component diff even at GEO camera distance, and the camera stays AGI-encoded in `packCameraUniforms`). VERIFY: `Tools/visual-regression/probe-buffercoll-wasm-encode.mjs` — a 6084-point grid drawn via the batch path vs a forced-scalar twin diffs **0 px on WebGPU / 3 px on WebGL** (AA tol), sub-threshold (64) + override-Infinity collections stay scalar (instrumented `wasmEncodeRepacks`/`scalarEncodeRepacks` counters), and a full-grid position update (#13465) re-renders +126px through the batch path; 0 rendering console errors; PNGs visually identical. tsc + gulp build green; collections-regression, buffer-logdepth-zfight, collections-far-camera, buffer-point-update, logdepth-zfight, orbital-catalog, sandcastle-smoke all PASS. **Caveat (historical) — the WASM kernel did NOT execute in the bundled build at Batch 272** (the byte-identical JS fallback ran instead); **this was FIXED in Batch 274 (NEW-WASM-BRIDGE-BUNDLE-LOAD below) — the real kernel now loads + runs in the bundle.** Rendering was correct either way. **Threshold lowered 5000→2000 in Batch 273** — see NEW-BUFFERCOLL-ENCODE-BENCHMARK below for the measured rationale (the win is the encode-hoist, not WASM SIMD).
- ~~**NEW-BUFFERCOLL-ENCODE-BENCHMARK** (M) — Benchmark 10k/50k/100k scalar-vs-WASM both backends + threshold tuning + visual-regression probe.~~ **SHIPPED Batch 273.** Built TWO complementary measurement vehicles + tuned the threshold from the data (NOT assumption — honest result reported). **(1) `Tools/wasm-encode-benchmark.mjs`** — a Node CPU-encode micro-benchmark that drives the REAL `batch_rte_encode` kernel under raw node (same loader+fetch-shim harness as `wasm-subrange-encode-check.mjs`, with a trip-wire that fails on any silent JS fallback), comparing the WASM kernel vs the scalar fround twin at 10k/50k/100k with warmup + median timing + byte-identity assertions. This is the ONLY place the real kernel runs (the bundle can't load WASM — NEW-WASM-BRIDGE-BUNDLE-LOAD). Result: WASM ~**1.2-1.25x** at 10k-50k, **ties** (~1.0x) at 100k — the WASM path's per-call arena copy/readback overhead scales with count and erodes the SIMD win; absolute CPU encode is tiny (0.1-1.2 ms even for 100k/frame). **(2) `Tools/visual-regression/probe-buffercoll-encode-benchmark.mjs`** — a Playwright end-to-end probe (BOTH backends) that nudges EVERY point each frame to force a full-range repack+upload, times repack+writeBuffer via a debug-pragma timer in both hot paths (`_repackMsTotal`/`_repackSamples` on the cache/renderContext), and prints a per-count per-backend ms/frame table for the batch-encode strategy vs the forced-scalar (`_wasmEncodeThresholdOverride=Infinity`) path, PLUS a WebGPU-vs-WebGL coverage no-regression assertion (Principle 8) + PNGs. **KEY FINDING:** the dominant repack cost is the per-primitive `EncodedCartesian3` 65536-grid split INSIDE the loop, NOT the GPU upload and NOT WASM. Hoisting the position encode into one contiguous `batchEncodeRange` fround call makes the repack **~25-40% faster end-to-end at ≥1500 points on BOTH backends** even with the WASM kernel dark (JS fround twin running). Crossover (forced-batch sweep at 500/1000/1500/2000/3000): batch LOSES below ~750 (fixed slice-setup overhead), marginal at ~1000, wins reliably from ~1500 up; absolute repack < 0.5 ms/frame below 1500 (negligible). **Threshold set to 2000** (both backends, kept in lock-step) — inside the winning region with margin against timer noise. **Honest negative on WASM specifically:** the SIMD win is below browser measurement noise and dormant anyway (bundle load), so NO WASM-specific gating was added — the threshold gates the encode-strategy hoist, which wins regardless of whether the kernel or its JS twin produced the bytes. VERIFY: both benchmark tools above; probe-buffercoll-wasm-encode (Batch-272 parity gate, re-run under the new threshold), collections-regression, buffer-logdepth-zfight, buffer-point-update, logdepth-zfight, collections-far-camera, orbital-catalog, point-label-partial-write, sandcastle-smoke all PASS; tsc + gulp build green. Follow-up NEW-WASM-WIDE-INSTANCE-KERNEL stays deferred (the residual color-pack loop is NOT the bottleneck — the position hoist captured the win).
- ~~**NEW-WASM-BRIDGE-BUNDLE-LOAD** (M) — *Found while shipping Batch 272.* The dynamic glue `import(".../ThirdParty/Workers/cesium_wasm.js")` in EVERY `Wasm*Bridge` 404s in the bundled build, so the WASM kernel never loads and every bridge silently uses its byte-identical JS fallback — the entire engine WASM path was dark in production.~~ **SHIPPED Batch 274.** Root cause was a hard-coded glue specifier resolved relative to the EMITTED bundle, in two shapes: (a) the 5 bridges keeping `"../../ThirdParty/Workers/cesium_wasm.js"` external (RTE, Heightmap, Matrix, PointCloud, QuantizedMesh) had `../../` resolve to `/Build/ThirdParty` (glue 404); (b) the 2 bridges (Cull, Sort) with a bare `import("../ThirdParty/...")` got the glue INLINED, whose `new URL("cesium_wasm_bg.wasm", import.meta.url)` resolved to the bundle root (binary 404). **Fix (bundle-wide, consistent across all 7 bridges):** new shared helper `packages/engine/Source/Scene/resolveWasmGlueUrl.js` returns `buildModuleUrl("ThirdParty/Workers/cesium_wasm.js")` — the canonical Cesium base-URL resolver (same one `TaskProcessor` uses for its worker + `wasmBinaryFile` paths), which yields a correct absolute URL in EVERY format: ESM (anchored at `index.js`'s `import.meta.url`), IIFE (anchored at the `Cesium.js` script via `getBaseUrlFromCesiumScript()` / `CESIUM_BASE_URL`), and CJS, plus honoring a `CESIUM_BASE_URL` override. All 7 bridges now `import(/* webpackIgnore */ resolveWasmGlueUrl())`; Cull/Sort keep the import EXTERNAL (no more inlining) so the glue loads as its own module and its sibling `cesium_wasm_bg.wasm` URL resolves correctly too. **Also folded in the bridge-wide missing-memory-export consistency fix** (the Batch-271 RTE `_wasmExports = await module.default()` + `_wasmMemory()` pattern) into Matrix/QuantizedMesh/PointCloud/Heightmap (Cull/Sort already store the exports object in `_wasmModule`); replaced their `_wasmModule.__wbindgen_export_0 ?? _wasmModule.memory` (always `undefined` — the glue never re-exports `memory`) with the `_wasmMemory()` helper + an explicit guard. Added a `wasmReady` getter to Cull/Sort (alias of `isAvailable`) so a single load-state probe works uniformly across all 7. **VERIFY:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-wasm-bundle-load.mjs` — loads the REAL bundle in Edge and for all 7 bridges asserts `loadWasm()→true` + `wasmReady===true`, 0 `cesium_wasm*` 404s (glue + binary both 200), and a no-fallback trip-wire on the RTE kernel (WASM `batchEncodeRange` byte-identical to the JS twin + `_lastWasmUsed===true` + no "using JS fallback" warning). Passes in BOTH ESM mode AND `--iife` mode (against `Build/Cesium/Cesium.js`). `Tools/wasm-subrange-encode-check.mjs` (node real-kernel check — its loader hook still matches the buildModuleUrl-produced specifier suffix) stays green. `npx tsc --noEmit` + `npx gulp build` + `npx gulp buildAllVariants` green; the glue + binary are co-located under `ThirdParty/Workers/` in every variant output. - ~~**NEW-UPSTREAM-13465-BUFFERPOINT-STALENESS** (S) — Port upstream #13465 BufferPointCollection update-staleness fix + regression spec.~~ **SHIPPED Batch 270.** Bug confirmed in OUR code: `BufferPoint.setPosition()` (and `BufferPolygon`/`BufferPolyline` geometry setters) wrote the new vertex into the collection's separate `_positionView` and called `_makeDirtyBoundingVolume()` but never set the primitive's `_dirty` flag. The repack pass in BOTH renderers (WebGPU `WebGPUBufferPointRenderer.repackPointDirty` + WebGL `renderBufferPointCollection`) iterates only `[_dirtyOffset, _dirtyOffset+_dirtyCount)` AND skips any primitive whose `_dirty` is false, so a position-only change on an already-rendered point was never re-encoded — the GPU buffers kept the stale position. Fix = `this._dirty = true;` added to all five geometry setters (BufferPoint.js, BufferPolyline.js ×1, BufferPolygon.js ×3), matching upstream commit `e4e8b3b778`. (Did NOT pull the unrelated `positionDatatype`/`positionNormalized` JSDoc/feature additions from that commit — our fork hasn't taken those.) Verified: new unit spec in `BufferPointCollectionSpec.js` (`_dirty` flips + dirty-range covers the moved index) + `probe-buffer-point-update.mjs` (cyan point moves >= 80px within 2 frames, static red anchor control unchanged) — both PASS on WebGPU AND WebGL; probe reproduces the pre-fix 0px-shift staleness when the fix is reverted. NOTE: discovered a separate PRE-EXISTING WebGL degeneracy — a SINGLE-point `gl.POINTS` BufferPointCollection can drop its lone vertex on a sub-data update (>= 2 points renders fine); tracked as **NEW-BUFFERPOINT-WEBGL-SINGLE-VERTEX-DROPOUT** below, NOT introduced by this fix.
- **NEW-BUFFERPOINT-WEBGL-SINGLE-VERTEX-DROPOUT** (S) — Found while shipping #13465 (Batch 270). On WebGL ONLY, a `BufferPointCollection` holding exactly ONE point can drop its lone `gl.POINTS` vertex on a `copyAttributeFromRange` sub-data update (the point vanishes after `setPosition`, never reappears; even the initial single-point render is flaky). With >= 2 points the dynamic-update path renders correctly (verified). WebGPU is unaffected (single point updates fine). Not a regression from the `_dirty` fix — the fix is correct (proven on both backends with >= 2 points + on WebGPU with 1). Likely the WebGL `VertexArray`/`Buffer.copyFromArrayView` single-vertex sub-data path or a `gl.POINTS` count-1 degeneracy. Low priority (single-point Buffer collections are an unusual edge case); revisit if a real scene hits it. `probe-buffer-point-update.mjs` deliberately uses 2 points to avoid this. Tune threshold; Playwright probe confirms no visual regression vs WebGL (Principle 8). Win may be modest if writeBuffer GPU upload dominates over CPU encode at these counts — measure before claiming. Depends on the WASM-encode wiring + #13465 fix. **Batch 276 — REPRODUCTION ATTEMPT (not yet fixed):** static analysis traced the whole WebGL single-point path (`_makeDirty(0)` → `_dirtyCount=1/_dirtyOffset=0` is correct for count==1; `copyAttributeFromRange(loc, arr, 0, 1)` builds a correct 1-vertex view at byteOffset 0; `_positionCount` is incremented in `BufferPointCollection.add`; the radius-0 single-point bounding sphere is a valid point, not culled). A new probe (`probe-buffer-point-single.mjs`) renders ONE point on WebGL, then moves it via the count==1 sub-data path — it PASSES consistently (lone point visible before AND after, moves 253px, 0 errors) in CesiumViewer's standard render loop. The documented dropout did NOT reproduce there — consistent with the "flaky/intermittent" description; it likely depends on a specific draw/depth/cull state the default viewer loop doesn't hit. Per Principle 8 (reproduce-in-a-probe-first), NO speculative source fix was shipped — a fix that can't be shown to move a failing probe isn't a fix. The probe is retained as a regression gate documenting the working path; tighten it to capture the flaky case (and only then fix) if a real scene reproduces it deterministically.

Only if benchmark shows the JS color-pack loop is the residual bottleneck. Needs Rust rebuild.
- **NEW-UPSTREAM-13448-READONLY-PROPS** (S) — Next-sync note: #13448 Buffer* modelMatrix/BV readonly + Node 22 (breaking change, not a now-pull).
