## NEW-GBUFFER-MRT-INTEGRATION — Always-on G-buffer + MRT (Slice 5c-B follow-ups) — PRODUCER side largely SHIPPED; consumer integration is the residual

**Status (doc-synced Batch 175, after the triage workflow + a slot-1-emitter grep):** The original "slot 1 currently stays at sentinel `(0,0,0,1)` because no fragment shader emits `@location(1)` yet" claim is STALE — **176 WGSL shaders now emit `@location(1)` normalRoughness**: the globe (`GlobeTerrain.wgsl` `makeFragOutput`), Model PBR (`ModelPBRComplete.wgsl` `FragOutput`, every return path — verified clean in the Batch 143 NEW-GLTF-PIPELINE-SHAPE-AUDIT Item 3), the full Primitive Lit-material family (`PrimitiveMat*Lit.wgsl`, `PhongLighting.wgsl`, `PBRMetallicRoughness.wgsl`), classification (`ShadowVolumeAppearance.wgsl`), and `FlexibleGeometry.wgsl`. So the **producer side is broadly shipped** — the G-buffer slot 1 carries real per-fragment normals + roughness across the major draw paths, not a sentinel.

**Residual (the part that's genuinely open):** the *consumer* integration. AO already consumes `normalRoughnessTexture`. The remaining downstream consumers (clustered/Forward+ lighting, SSR, contact shadows, NPR, TAA normal-disocclusion) are the open follow-ups below — the clustered-lighting consumer in particular is gated on the `maxBindGroups = 4` platform ceiling (it needs another bind group the Model/globe layouts already fully use), which is the real architectural blocker, NOT the producer emit. Also note the legacy compute producer `GBufferNormalsFromDepth.wgsl` / `dispatchGBufferNormalsFromDepth` is now largely redundant given the render-pass emit, but is LEFT IN PLACE (Principle 7 — it's the fallback for draw paths that don't emit slot 1, e.g. depth-only / sentinel-normal debug returns; retiring it needs a per-path audit, tracked as a follow-up, not done here).

**Architecture refresher:**

- `GBufferFramebuffer.js` allocates paired single-sample + MSAA textures (`rgba16float`, packed `(normalEC.xyz, roughness)`). MSAA companion auto-resolves into the single-sample texture at end-of-pass.
- The single-sample texture has `STORAGE_BINDING | TEXTURE_BINDING | COPY_DST | RENDER_ATTACHMENT` usage — it serves as the storage-bindable target for the legacy compute producer (`GBufferNormalsFromDepth.wgsl`) AND as the resolve target for the MRT render-pass writes (when shaders emit `@location(1)`).
- The MSAA companion (`RENDER_ATTACHMENT` only, since multisampled textures cannot have `STORAGE_BINDING`) is the actual render-pass attachment when `scene.msaaSamples > 1`.
- `WebGPUSceneRendererPassRedirect.ts` appends the MRT slot-1 attachment when `isSceneFBMrtMode()` returns true (currently always true post-Batch-116).
- Consumers (AO is the only one today) read `gBufferFramebuffer.normalRoughnessTexture` — the single-sample resolved view.

### Producer-side follow-ups (Batches 117+)

#### NEW-GBUFFER-MRT-GLOBE-EMIT — Globe shader emits @location(1)

Wire `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` to emit `(normalEC.xyz, roughness)` at `@location(1)` and flip the globe pipeline slot 1 from `null` → `{format: "rgba16float", writeMask: 0xf}`. This is the natural next batch.

**Scope:**

- `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` has 4 fragment entry points (`fragmentMain` + 3 debug variants). Each one ends with `return color;` (or similar). They all need to become `return FragOutput(color, normalRoughness)` where `FragOutput` is a new struct with both locations.
- Globe `normalEC` is already computed inside `fragmentMain` for lighting; the debug variants don't compute one but can emit `(0,0,0,1)` sentinel.
- Globe roughness today is a hardcoded value via the IBL path. For the G-buffer pack, use a constant `0.5` placeholder; refine in a follow-up when material-aware roughness lands.
- Pipeline change: 1-line flip in `WebGPUGlobeSurfacePipelines.ts:buildPipelineDescriptor` — slot 1 goes from `null` to the rgba16float-writeMask-0xf shape. The bisect in Batch 116 already verified that this slot shape works as long as the shader emits the matching location.
- Verification: `probe-mrt-validation.mjs` to confirm zero pipeline-cache errors after the flip. Then a normal-overlay probe to confirm slot 1 has real data instead of the sentinel clear.

**Effort:** 1 batch (~half-day). Risk: shader return-rewrap mismatch (the patcher mistake from the failed Sub-C dry-run). Mitigation: edit each return path by hand, no automated patcher.

#### NEW-GBUFFER-MRT-PRIMITIVE-EMIT — Lit Mat primitives emit @location(1)

Same conversion as the globe but for each of the ~30 primitive renderers that produce per-fragment material normals (Lit Box/Sphere/Polygon/Wall/Corridor/Frustum + glTF Models with normal maps + 3D Tiles B3DM/I3DM/PNTS lit variants). Their pipelines already declare slot 1 as a placeholder (writeMask=0) via Phase 1's `makeSceneFBTargets` helper; bumping to a real write target needs:

- A `FragOutput` struct in each shader (or a shared helper module).
- Per-renderer pipeline target flip via `emitsGBuffer: true` option.
- The G-buffer normal should be the FINAL material normal (post-normal-map, post-anisotropy), not the geometric `v_normalEC`. This is the entire point of Slice 5c-B over the compute-from-depth producer.

**Status:** Partially shipped.

- ✅ **EllipsoidPrimitive** — Batch 118. Analytical ray-traced eye-space normal at slot 1.
- ✅ **glTF Models** (`Model.js` via `WebGPUModelPipelineCache`) — Batch 119. Post-normal-map N + real material roughness. Three return paths covered: main-lit (real N + roughness), unlit early-out (geometric normal + 0.5 placeholder), clipping edge band (geometric normal + 0.5 placeholder).
- ✅ **3D Tiles B3DM / I3DM / TILE_GLTF** — same as glTF Models. They share the `Model.js` → `WebGPUModelPipelineCache` pipeline; Batch 119's conversion automatically covers them. Verified via `Model.js:3516` (`ModelType.TILE_B3DM`) → same `createColorPipeline` call site.
- ⬜ **Lit Mat geometry primitives** (Box, Sphere, Polygon, Wall, Corridor, Frustum, etc.) — not yet converted. These go through `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js` and the `PrimitiveMatLit*.wgsl` family. The Lit Mat shaders compute a per-fragment normal in eye-space already (the lighting eval needs it); conversion is the same pattern as Model (FragOutput struct + rewrap returns + `emitsGBuffer: true`).
- ⬜ **3D Tiles PNTS lit variants** — points don't have surface normals in a meaningful per-fragment sense; SHOULD stay at writeMask=0 placeholder.

**Effort:** ~1 day per Lit Mat cluster (Box/Sphere/etc. typically share a shader family).

**Risk:** per-shader normal-extraction details (some shaders compute `czm_inverseViewRotation * worldNormal` late; others have eye-space normals already). Audit each before converting.

#### NEW-GBUFFER-MRT-COMPUTE-PRODUCER-RETIRE — Decision: keep or retire `GBufferNormalsFromDepth.wgsl`?

The legacy compute producer derives normals from depth via central differences. Now that MRT writes are wired:

- For pixels touched by an MRT-emitting pipeline, the MRT write wins (overwrites the compute output if both fire).
- For pixels touched ONLY by 1-target pipelines (sky, debug overlays, OIT accumulation that doesn't write through), the slot-1 attachment stays at the sentinel `(0,0,0,1)`.
- Today the compute producer runs every frame and writes EVERY pixel (with sentinel for sky/discontinuities). After Slice 5c-B Phase 2 is complete, it's redundant for the pixels covered by MRT-emitting shaders.

Two options:

1. **Retire the compute producer entirely.** Cleaner but requires every primitive that needs G-buffer normals to emit @location(1). Sky/non-emitting primitives leave the sentinel value, consumers handle via the fallback path (AO already does this — `lenSq > 0.01` check before using the G-buffer normal).
2. **Keep the compute producer as a fallback that runs BEFORE the MRT render pass.** It populates the sentinel pixels with depth-derived normals; the MRT pass then overwrites them. Doubles per-frame work for the overlap region but simplifies consumer logic (always sees a real-ish normal everywhere).

Punt this decision until at least 50% of primitives are emitting @location(1) — until then, option 1 leaves too many pixels at the sentinel and option 2 is the only viable path.

### Consumer-side follow-ups

The G-buffer is now always allocated (Sub-B, Batch 115b) so any consumer can read `gBufferFramebuffer.normalRoughnessTexture` without checking the deferred-lighting flag. Today only AO uses it. Candidates that should:

#### NEW-GBUFFER-CONSUMER-SSR — Screen-space reflections

SSR's primary input is per-pixel normal + roughness. `WebGPUSSREffect.ts` currently builds its own per-pixel normal via depth derivatives (same approximation AO used to use). Switch it to read the G-buffer normal-roughness texture and pull roughness from `.w` instead of hardcoding.

**Effort:** ~2 hours. Risk: SSR runs in the post-process pipeline, after the scene FB pass — the G-buffer texture is already in its resolved (single-sample) state at that point, so the bind is straightforward.

#### NEW-GBUFFER-CONSUMER-CLUSTERED-LIGHTING — Forward-clustered light pass

Forward-clustered lighting (currently a research-stage SCAFFOLDED feature) needs per-pixel normal for the diffuse + specular evaluation. With the G-buffer always available, the clustered pass can read it instead of re-deriving from depth (which would dramatically improve quality at silhouettes).

**Effort:** Multi-day, depends on Slice 5d (clustered lighting Phase 1) landing first.

**Sub-batch plan:** See [SLICE_5D_PLAN_CLUSTERED_LIGHTING.md](SLICE_5D_PLAN_CLUSTERED_LIGHTING.md) (Batch 137, 2026-05-25) for the 5-sub-batch sequence: KHR_lights_punctual loader → LightCollection → cluster bounds compute → light-cluster assignment compute → Forward+ fragment consumer. Effort estimate 6-8 days total.

**Status update (2026-05-26):** Steps 1-4 SHIPPED (Batches 134-148). Step 5 SCAFFOLDED across Batches 149-151 (FS chunk + dispatcher + SceneRenderer per-frame hook). Batch 152 attempted to wire the Model PBR consumer via a new `@group(4)` BGL but hit a platform ceiling — `Tools/visual-regression/probe-device-limits.mjs` confirmed Chromium-on-Windows caps `maxBindGroups` at 4 (both D3D12 + Vulkan backends), so the @group(4) approach is dead-on-arrival. Reverted cleanly to infrastructure-only; Batch 153 will merge the 5 clustered-lighting bindings into the existing group 3 (effects) BGL. See the Batch 152/153 entries in the slice plan for full scope + verification steps.

**Reference implementation:** [toji/webgpu-clustered-shading](https://github.com/toji/webgpu-clustered-shading) — Brandon Jones's (Google WebGPU lead) canonical Forward+ on WebGPU example. Directly portable pieces:

- **Cluster bounds compute shader** — assigns each cluster (typically 16×9×24 grid in view-space) an AABB. Runs once per resize, cached in a storage buffer keyed by `(viewport, frustum near/far, projection)`. Cesium-side hook: invalidate the cache when `WebGPUSceneRendererEnsureResources` bumps `_scenePipelineFormatGeneration` or when scene FB dimensions change.
- **Light-cluster assignment compute shader** — per-frame dispatch, one thread per cluster, walks the active-light list (KHR_lights_punctual when that lands) and emits two storage buffers: a per-cluster count + the global indirection list. Cesium-side hook: light list comes from `frameState.lights` (currently sun-only; KHR_lights_punctual would populate the array).
- **Forward+ fragment evaluation** — fragment reads its own cluster index from `gl_FragCoord.xy` + linear depth, then iterates that cluster's lights. With G-buffer normal already in slot 1, the fragment can use `textureLoad(gBufferNormalTexture, ...)` instead of re-deriving — exactly the integration this entry tracks.

**What to NOT directly port from the reference:**

- The example uses a single-world-space scene with a fixed camera; Cesium needs RTE precision so cluster-bounds compute must consume eye-space inputs (or RTE-encoded world space). The `encodedCameraHigh`/`encodedCameraLow` pattern in `CameraUniforms` is the bridge.
- The example's light culling is per-frame regardless of camera motion; Cesium's `RenderScheduler` already has per-frame dirty tracking that should gate the assignment dispatch when the camera + light positions haven't changed.
- Toji uses a hand-rolled glTF loader; Cesium has its own (`Model.js`) — the light extraction needs to plug into Cesium's KHR_lights_punctual loader (which itself needs to be built).

Both pieces (KHR_lights_punctual loader + this consumer) should land in the same Slice 5d arc — there's no point shipping clustered shading with no lights to cluster.

#### NEW-GBUFFER-CONSUMER-CONTACT-SHADOWS — Screen-space contact shadows

Sun-direction marching from a starting position + normal, sampled against the depth buffer. The starting normal comes from the G-buffer; the depth comes from the existing depth attachment. No new producer needed.

**Effort:** ~1 day for a basic implementation (no PCF, no soft contact). Quality improvement on close-range geometry (foliage occlusion, ground-truth ambient occlusion for grounded objects) is significant.

#### NEW-GBUFFER-CONSUMER-NPR-OUTLINES — Normal-discontinuity edges

Reads the G-buffer + depth to detect edges where adjacent pixels have divergent normals (silhouettes, hard creases) and draws an outline. Cheap post-process pass; no new bind groups beyond what the depth + G-buffer textures already provide. Useful for technical / engineering / CAD-style globe presentations.

**Effort:** ~half-day. Risk: visual taste — strong outlines clash with the photorealistic terrain default; needs an opt-in property on `scene`.

#### NEW-GBUFFER-CONSUMER-TAA-DISOCCLUSION — TAA history reproject

TAA's disocclusion mask is currently velocity-based. Adding G-buffer normal comparison (reject history pixels whose normal differs from the current frame's by more than a threshold) reduces ghosting at moving silhouettes. Small quality improvement, not a blocker.

**Effort:** ~half-day in `WebGPUTAAEffect.ts`. Risk: tuning the normal-divergence threshold — too tight and you lose history at every frame; too loose and ghosting persists.

### Cross-cutting concerns

- **Pipeline cache invalidation:** when `setSceneFBMrtMode(false)` is called (no current trigger, but possible if a future "low-memory mode" wants to drop the G-buffer), all cached pipelines must be invalidated — they were built with 2-target descriptors and would no longer match the 1-attachment pass. `WebGPURenderPipelineCache.clear()` exists; the gate just needs to fire.
- **Format negotiation:** `MRT_NORMAL_ROUGHNESS_FORMAT` is currently hardcoded to `rgba16float`. If a future device-tier check decides `rg16float` is enough (encode normal as oct-encoded `vec2`, drop roughness or pack into compute uniforms), update the format in `WebGPUSceneFBTargetHelpers.ts` AND match it in every emitter shader.
- **MSAA + storage interaction:** `_textureMSAA` (the render attachment) and `_texture` (the resolve target with `STORAGE_BINDING`) are different textures. Anything that writes to the G-buffer through the storage path (the compute producer today) writes to `_texture` directly; anything that reads as a sampler reads `_texture` too. The MSAA half is only the render-pass attachment. This is fine but worth remembering when adding new producers.

### Probe for this work

`probe-mrt-validation.mjs` (Batch 116) covers the four-cell AO×deferred matrix with WebGPU error capture (`device.onuncapturederror` + `device.lost` + categorized `console.error`). Re-run after every MRT change to confirm no new pipeline-cache errors. For each Producer-side conversion, also add a `probe-gbuffer-slot1-content.mjs` follow-up that samples the G-buffer texture and confirms slot 1 has non-sentinel values where the converted primitive draws.

## ~~NEW-ENV-EFFECTS-DEPTH-WIRING~~ — RESOLVED (Batches 127-129) — `context._depthStencilView` now assigned

**Status (doc-synced Batch 172, confirmed by triage workflow + grep):** RESOLVED.
The root cause was `context._depthStencilView` never being assigned, so every
environmental effect early-returned. It is now assigned in
`WebGPUSceneRendererEnsureResources.ts:221` (`_ctxWithDepth._depthStencilView = …`,
including the MSAA-resolve path), so `executeEnvironmentalEffects` no longer
skips on a null depth view. NOTE: a consumer can still be visually inert for
OTHER reasons (an effect's own feature flag off, or a downstream G-buffer
producer not wired — see NEW-GBUFFER-MRT-INTEGRATION) — but the specific
"depth view never assigned" blocker this entry tracked is gone. The original
body below is retained for archaeology.

**Original status:** Open. Surfaced during Batch 125 NPR-visibility investigation (2026-05-25).

**Affected features:** `WebGPUSceneRendererEnvironmentalEffects.executeEnvironmentalEffects` and every effect it dispatches:

- Procedural Clouds (`globe.showProceduralClouds`)
- Screen-Space Reflections (`scene._enableSSR`)
- Weather Particles (`scene._enableWeather`)
- Volumetric Fog (`frameState.atmosphericConditions.volumetricFog.enabled`)
- NPR Outlines (`scene._enableNPROutlines`, Batch 123)

**Symptom:** None of these effects produce visible output in any test scene. All silently skip.

**Root cause:** `WebGPUSceneRendererEnvironmentalEffects.ts:55-62` has:

```ts
const colorView = context._sceneColorView ?? context.currentTextureView;
const depthView = context._depthStencilView;
const outputView = context.currentTextureView;
if (!colorView || !depthView || !outputView) {
  return;
}
```

`context._depthStencilView` is declared on `WebGPUContext.ts:387` as `public _depthStencilView: GPUTextureView | null = null;` and is **never reassigned anywhere in the renderer** (verified via repo-wide grep on 2026-05-25). The only assignments to a similarly-named field are on `WebGPUEdgeFramebuffer._depthStencilView` (different class).

So `depthView` is always undefined → early return → the entire env-effects chain has been a no-op since this gate was added (commit history pending).

**False-positive in Batch 122 SSR verification:** the Batch 122 commit message claimed "B vs C = 0.000% — SSR reads same G-buffer regardless of deferredLighting flag." But SSR was never actually running — both B and C cells just rendered the baseline scene without SSR contribution. The 0% diff was trivially true (same no-op output) and didn't verify the G-buffer wiring.

**Secondary problem:** even if `_depthStencilView` is wired, the env effects currently write to `outputView = context.currentTextureView` (canvas swap chain). After they run, `_runPostProcessing` blits the scene FB color to the canvas, overwriting any env-effect output. So fixing the depth wiring alone isn't enough — the target chain also needs to be reordered or the env effects need to write back to scene FB color.

**Tertiary problem:** scene FB depth is MSAA when `scene.msaaSamples > 1` (default 4), and `_sceneFramebuffer.depthSampleableView` is null in that case (per L1953 comment in `WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts`). So even wiring `_depthStencilView = _sceneFramebuffer.depthSampleableView` doesn't help MSAA scenes. Env effects need either a multisampled-depth path (`texture_depth_multisampled_2d` + `textureLoad(.., 0)`) or a resolve step.

**Multi-batch fix outline:**

1. **Wire `context._depthStencilView` to the scene FB depth view.** Single-sample case: `_sceneFramebuffer.depthSampleableView`. MSAA case: either resolve depth to a single-sample texture each frame OR teach every env-effect shader the multisampled-depth path. Easier: resolve (one extra render pass per frame, fixed cost).
2. **Reorder env effects to AFTER post-process** so their canvas writes survive. Attempted in Batch 125 but the depth issue masked the result (env effects still skipped due to null depthView).
3. **OR: re-route env effects to write back to scene FB color** via a ping-pong intermediate buffer. Preserves the linear-HDR pipeline through tonemap/FXAA. Heavier — needs a new intermediate scene-color texture.

**Verification when fixed:** `probe-npr-outlines.mjs` with `nprNormalThreshold=-1` should produce a SOLID MAGENTA canvas over geometry (current behavior: terrain renders unchanged, NPR is invisible). `probe-ssr-consumer.mjs` should show A-vs-B (SSR off vs on) >> noise floor on a scene with reflective surfaces.

**Effort:** 1-2 days. Risk: high — touches the post-process + env-effects ordering that hasn't been fully exercised since the bug landed.

**Status (doc-synced Batch 172):** All 6 audit items resolved — heading struck. The body had a self-contradictory stale "Items 4 + 5 still open" line (corrected below); the authoritative state is the Batch 143/144/145 resolution summarized here. All 6 items VERIFIED CLEAN / FIXED.

- Item 4 (KHR extension factor probes) VERIFIED CLEAN in Batch 145 (2026-05-26). 7 synthetic test assets (clearcoat / specular / anisotropy / iridescence / sheen / volume+transmission / transmission+ior) all load + render with 0 device errors, and the JS pack offsets match the WGSL struct field offsets verified at runtime via `model._webgpuCache.primitives[].materialData` introspection. The KHR FS code paths (Batches 105-107) work end-to-end on WebGPU as of this verification.

Velocity-pipeline MSAA mismatch (Item 1) fixed opportunistically in Batch 143 as a dormant-bug cleanup — Model doesn't emit velocity commands yet so it was inert, but the pipeline-shape mismatch is gone.

**Batch 143 audit findings (Model PBR pipeline shape):**

- ✅ Item 1 (MSAA): `createPipeline` (color), `createClassificationPipeline` correctly thread `sampleCount` from `context._msaaSamples` into `multisample: { count }`. Pick pipelines correctly omit `multisample` (pick FBO is single-sample). One dormant mismatch found in `createVelocityPipeline` (multisample=sampleCount while velocityTexture is sampleCount=1) and fixed in Batch 143 to align with collection renderers' velocity-pipeline pattern from Batch 134. Currently inert — Model primitives don't tag `.velocityCommand` so the velocity pass short-circuits (verified by `probe-model-taa-msaa.mjs` reporting 0/79 velocity commands on a TAA+MSAA+animated-model scene).
- ✅ Item 2 (BGL visibility): all Model BGLs audited. Camera UBO `VERTEX_FRAGMENT` (correct — VS reads MVP, FS reads camera position). Material UBO at group 1 binding 0 also `VERTEX_FRAGMENT` (correct — VS reads modelMatrix, FS reads PBR factors). All instance-group bindings (joint matrices, morph deltas, instance transforms) correctly `VERTEX`-only. All texture + sampler bindings correctly `FRAGMENT`-only. LightUniforms `FRAGMENT`-only (correct — no VS uses light data). No mis-declarations found.
- ✅ Item 3 (MRT slot 1): the lit color pipeline uses `makeSceneFBTargets(..., { emitsGBuffer: true })` which produces `[scene, {rgba16float, writeMask: 0xf}]`. ModelPBRComplete's FragOutput emits `@location(1) normalRoughness` from every path (lit PBR with perturbed normal at L2706, unlit early-out with geomNormalEC at L1952, clipping-edge early-out with geomNormalEC at L1859) so the shader emit matches the descriptor. Classification correctly drops `emitsGBuffer` and uses placeholder slot 1 with writeMask=0.
- ✅ Item 6 (Pick FBO parity): 4 pick descriptor variants (`createPickPipeline`, `createPickHoverPipeline`, `createPickPrecisePass1Pipeline`, `createPickPrecisePass2Pipeline`) all correctly use single-target `[{format: presentationFormat}]` with NO `multisample` block, matching the single-sample pick FBO. The depth pre-pass variant uses `writeMask: 0` to suppress color while keeping depth/stencil writes.

**Status (CORRECTED Batch 172):** ~~Items 4 + 5 still open~~ — STALE; both are resolved (Item 4 Batch 145, Item 5 Batch 144 — see the resolution summary at the top of this entry). Original status text below for reference only.

Surfaced at the end of Batch 141 (2026-05-26) when the Model PBR audit completed the data-side review and called out the pipeline-side as not yet covered.

**What's already done (Batches 138-141):** Data-side of the Model PBR pipeline is byte-correct across MaterialUniforms (768 B / 192 floats), CameraUniforms, LightUniforms + per-light PunctualLight records, MorphWeightsUniforms, SHUniforms. One real bug fixed in FeatureIdUniforms (featurePickEnabled was at wrong slot, silent per-feature pick failure on batch-tabled tilesets).

**What's NOT covered:**

1. **MSAA sample-count parity across pipeline variants.** Bug Pattern A from Batch 134 (collection renderers' missing `multisample: { count }`) was found in 6 collection-renderer files. The Model PBR pipeline cache (`WebGPUModelPipelineCache.js`) builds ~20+ variants based on MODEL_HAS_* defines (FLAG_HAS_NORMAL_TEXTURE, FLAG_USE_SPECULAR_GLOSSINESS, FLAG_HAS_CLEARCOAT, FLAG_HAS_TRANSMISSION, FLAG_HAS_INSTANCING, FLAG_HAS_SKINNING, FLAG_HAS_MORPH_TARGETS, FLAG_HAS_FEATURE_ID_TEXTURE, FLAG_HAS_FEATURE_ID_ATTRIBUTE, FLAG_HAS_BATCH_TABLE, FLAG_HAS_VERTEX_COLORS, FLAG_IS_DOUBLE_SIDED, FLAG_IS_UNLIT, FLAG_ALPHA_MODE_MASK, FLAG_ALPHA_MODE_BLEND, FLAG_HAS_SPECULAR, FLAG_HAS_ANISOTROPY, FLAG_HAS_IRIDESCENCE, FLAG_HAS_SHEEN, FLAG_HAS_VOLUME). Each variant goes through its own descriptor build — verify all of them pass `multisample: sampleCount > 1 ? { count: sampleCount } : undefined` consistently. Pick + velocity variants need to be checked too (Batch 134 found Ellipsoid pick had inherited multisample state incorrectly, separate from color).

2. **BGL visibility parity (Bug Pattern B from Batch 134).** Look for bind group layout entries declared `visibility: GPUShaderStage.FRAGMENT` only where the corresponding `@group(X) @binding(Y)` is also consumed by the vertex shader. The Model pipeline has 7 bind groups (camera, material, skinning, morph, instancing, feature-id, effects) and most have entries read by BOTH stages — easy place for FRAGMENT-only mis-declarations to hide.

3. **MRT slot 1 G-buffer target.** Per Batches 119-121 the Model pipelines should be emitting `@location(1) normalRoughness` for the always-on G-buffer. Verify every MODEL_HAS_* variant's pipeline descriptor includes `targets[1]` with the right format (`rgba16float`) and write mask (`0xf` since Model emits the perturbed normal). The pick variant should have `writeMask: 0` for slot 1 since pick doesn't emit G-buffer. Recently Batch 132 found MaterialAppearance had a separate pipeline path that missed multisample — same risk class.

4. **KHR extension factor paths in the FS.** The Batch 141 probe (`probe-model-pbr-audit.mjs`) loaded 5 generic glTF assets but none of them carry KHR_materials_clearcoat / specular / anisotropy / iridescence / sheen / volume / transmission extensions. The shader has gates on `materialFlags` for each — those code paths haven't been exercised end-to-end on WebGPU since their introduction (Batches 105-107). Need an explicit probe per extension with a representative test asset (Khronos has reference assets for each KHR_materials_* extension at github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF-Sample-Assets).

5. **CesiumMan startup race.** Probe-model-pbr-audit.mjs surfaced 2 device errors loading CesiumMan ("Recording in CommandEncoder which is locked while RenderPassEncoder is open") during a tile/model concurrent-load race. Not reproducible with a simpler 600-frame steady-state probe in `probe-cesium-man-debug.mjs`. Could be:
   - Skinning matrix upload happening via `encoder.copyBufferToBuffer` while scene pass is open (would explain the timing)
   - Tile loader's `copyTextureToTexture` racing with the model's first frame
   - A loader async-init that registers a per-frame callback before the renderer is fully set up

   The probe needs to add finer-grained instrumentation (callstack capture on `onuncapturederror`, or a wrap of `encoder.*` methods to log who's calling while a pass is open) to localize the source.

6. **Pick FBO descriptor parity.** Pick pipelines target the pick FBO (single-sample, single-target). Verify Model pick pipelines correctly drop `multisample` and `targets[1]` from their descriptors. Batch 118 found Ellipsoid's pick descriptor inherited multisample state from the parent color descriptor — Model's pick path uses a separate descriptor builder so it could have its own version of the same bug.

**Probes to add:**

- `probe-model-pipeline-variants.mjs` — exhaustively enumerate Model pipeline variants (Cartesian product of MODEL_HAS_* defines truncated to common combinations) and assert each pipeline creates without errors. Include MSAA on/off matrix.
- `probe-model-khr-clearcoat.mjs` — load Khronos's `ClearCoatTest.glb` (or similar reference asset) and verify the FS clearcoat code path produces a visible specular sheen.
- `probe-model-khr-*` — similar per-extension probes.

**Effort:** Multi-batch arc. Step 1 (MSAA + BGL audit) is ~half a day per variant family. Step 4 (KHR ext probes) is ~half a day per extension if a test asset is on hand.

**When to do this:** When clustered lighting (Slice 5d) lands or stalls, OR if a user reports broken rendering for a KHR_materials_* asset. Until then the existing audit (data-side correctness + 5-asset smoke) covers the most common shipping scenarios.

## NEW-VEGETATION-SYSTEM — Planetary vegetation epic (trees / grass / rocks, globe + 3D Tiles, dual-backend) — FUTURE / unbuilt

**Status:** FUTURE — design complete, **zero code shipped** (investigation/design only, 2026-06-05). This is a scope flag + pointer; the full design (feasibility, gap analysis, 4-stage LOD, foliage PBR, 3D-Tiles spec analysis, perf-feature usage, biome/ecoregion data layer) is canonical in **[VEGETATION_SYSTEM_DESIGN.md](VEGETATION_SYSTEM_DESIGN.md)** — do not duplicate detail here.

**What:** Ultra-performant planetary vegetation on the globe + draped on 3D Tiles, WebGPU-first with a degraded-but-correct WebGL2 fallback. Six independently-shippable slices (each must ship a Playwright probe per CLAUDE.md Principle 8):

- **V1 — Scatter foundation:** `Scene/VegetationLayer.js` + `VegetationScatterCollection` + `FeatureRendererKey.VEGETATION_SCATTER` + `WebGPUVegetationScatterRenderer.ts` + `Shaders/WebGPU/Compute/VegetationScatter.wgsl` (density/biome map → RTE instance buffer); WebGL2 CPU-worker twin writing the identical layout (deterministic seeded PRNG, never `Math.random()`).
- **V2 — 4-stage mesh-LOD chain + GPU LOD select:** the central new artifact — no per-Model mesh-LOD chain exists today (`Scene/Model/Model.js` has only `distanceDisplayCondition`, a binary cull). Reuse `WebGPUGPUCuller` + `WebGPUIndirectDrawManager`; CPU per-instance tiering on WebGL2. **Decision point:** add a GPU-cull gate to the `Pass.CESIUM_3D_TILE` path (currently bypasses `gpuCullCommands()`) vs dispatch scatter through `Pass.OPAQUE` to inherit the existing gate.
- **V3 — Octahedral impostor bake + sample** (resolves `FEAT-GAP-07`): offline + lazy-RTT atlas; portable octahedral FS sampling; stochastic-dither L0↔L1 cross-fade (`csm_stochasticDither.wgsl`, shipped).
- **V4 — `VegetationPBR` shader pair:** new `ShaderDefine` bits + flag bits 26–30 (wind, two-sided leaf translucency, alpha-to-coverage, canopy AO, impostor sampling) in WGSL + GLSL lockstep.
- **V5 — Grass + rocks profiles:** grass chain (blades → density imposter → detail-albedo); rocks/sparse-arid parameter profile (no wind, full-octahedron impostor, Hi-Z occlusion).
- **V6 (optional) — optimization:** GPU-sort consumer wiring, render-bundle caching for static L2/L3 tiles, per-instance picking + `Cesium3DTileStyle` species coloring.

**3D-Tiles authoring / extension idea:** explicit instances ride entirely on ratified/in-flight standards (`EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing` + `EXT_structural_metadata` + `EXT_instance_features` + `3DTILES_metadata` + `3DTILES_implicit_tiling`) with **zero new loader** — the recommended ingest for real datasets (OSM `natural=tree`, Global Forest Watch). The spec has **no** vegetation/biome/scatter semantics and **no** metadata-driven auto-LOD/impostor/HLOD generation (those are author-baked-explicit or viewer-side). A fork-local `3DTILES_vegetation_scatter` / `_CESIUMWEBGPU_vegetation_scatter` convention (`VEG_BIOME` / `VEG_ECOREGION` / `VEG_SPECIES` / `VEG_DENSITY_SCALE` semantics + density/biome KTX2 rasters) is proposed for procedural fill — fork-local first, upstream only after deterministic seeded scatter is proven.

**Biome/ecoregion data dependency (asset-prep, not engine work):** three-layer model (biome/climate + ecoregion + landcover) keying a species palette per `(biome × ecoregion × landcover)`. Recommended permissive stack: Köppen-Geiger v3 + RESOLVE Ecoregions 2017 + ESA WorldCover 2021 (all **CC-BY-4.0** — note: no MIT-licensed geospatial data exists; CC-BY/CC0/public-domain is the field norm). Auto-sample (pre-rasterized KTX2 → O(1) lookup) + manual GeoJSON/tileset override with strict precedence (explicit > manual > tileset > global).

**WebGL2 / WebGPU split:** the recurring deficit is WebGL2 has no compute, no GPU-driven indirect-arg generation, no per-point LOD (`Context.js:1107`). Every GPU-driven stage (scatter, cull, LOD-select) needs a maintained CPU twin. The portable subset (impostor sampling, HLOD proxies, wind, dither/A2C, terrain-albedo bake) is large enough that WebGL2 still gets a correct, shippable experience — just CPU-bounded scatter and tile-granular (not per-instance) LOD.

**Related existing inventory entries** (this epic consolidates them): `FEAT-GAP-07` (impostors, §D.2), `FEAT-SURVEY-43` (grass/foliage material + vegetation instancing, §D.7), `BACKLOG-§9` (subsurface scattering, §D.7). Refraction-MRT for physically-correct leaf transmission is unbuilt (ties to `BACKLOG-§9`); no runtime mesh-merge tool (L2 HLOD clumps baked offline); `Scene/PropertyTexture.js` shader-wiring gap blocks per-texel density maps (workaround: plain control texture).

**Prerequisites:** none hard-blocking V1 (the consumer half — instancing, metadata, depth-draping, terrain sampling, RTE, stochastic dither — already exists). V4 refraction defers to `BACKLOG-§9`. **Effort:** multi-slice epic, each slice independently shippable. **Trace:** `migration_doc/VEGETATION_SYSTEM_DESIGN.md` (canonical design, §1–§9 + 3D-Tiles spec section + LOD-A..C perf-feature section + BIOME-A..E data-layer section).

### Build / lifecycle pillar (origin: PRINCIPAL_ENGINEER_REVIEW_2026_04_16.md)

- **BUILD-LIFECYCLE-3C-VIEW-BINDGROUP-CACHE** (§3c) — Per-frame `createView()` / `createBindGroup()` without a cache in two hot paths: `WebGPUPickFramebuffer.ts` (`createView()` in `begin()` every frame) and `WebGPUMipmapGenerator.ts` (`createBindGroup()` per mip level). Silent memory accretion in long sessions. NOT the same as C-R11 (which covered post-process + per-tile EffectsBindGroup caches). Fix: cache views on the texture wrapper (rebuild on resize), cache mipmap bind groups keyed on `(texture, mipLevel)`. **Status unverified, lifted from PRINCIPAL_ENGINEER_REVIEW_2026_04_16.md §3c on archive.**
- **BUILD-LIFECYCLE-3D-DEVICE-LOSS-PROMISE** (§3d) — Device-lost recovery (`WebGPUDeviceLossRecovery._attemptRecovery()`) is `async` and its promise is not stored on the context; `destroy()` does not await/abort an in-flight recovery → recovered device can become an unowned-but-alive latent leak, and detached writes can crash. Fix: store the recovery promise on the context; `destroy()` awaits it or aborts via `AbortSignal`. **Status unverified, lifted from PRINCIPAL_ENGINEER_REVIEW_2026_04_16.md §3d on archive.**
- **BUILD-VARIANT-PLUGIN-SPEC** (§5b) — `scripts/bundleVariantPlugin.js`, the variant stubs, and the variant build tasks ship with zero specs (a regex edit could redirect the wrong files and still build green). The plugin itself is BUILD-VAR-1 (BACKLOG, SHIPPED) but its **spec** is not tracked anywhere. Fix: `scripts/__tests__/bundleVariantPlugin.spec.js` mocking esbuild `onResolve`, asserting the right stub per variant × path. **Status unverified, lifted from PRINCIPAL_ENGINEER_REVIEW_2026_04_16.md §5b on archive.**
- **WEBGPU-SPEC-BACKFILL** (§5c) — 20 of 22 major WebGPU modules (~8,850+ LOC: `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands`, `WebGPUAutoUniforms`, `WebGPUModelRenderer`, `WebGPUPrimitiveShaders`, `WebGPUCubeMapPanoramaRenderer`, `WebGPUPolylineRenderer`, `WebGPUSkyAtmosphereRenderer`, `WGSLShaderBuilder`, `WebGPUEnvironmentRenderer`, …) have zero specs. #1 quality risk per the build/lifecycle pillar. Fix: no new module without a spec; backfill top-5-by-LOC. **Status unverified, lifted from PRINCIPAL_ENGINEER_REVIEW_2026_04_16.md §5c on archive.**
- **PRAGMA-STRIP-LINT** (§6e) — No post-build lint verifies that every `console.log`/`console.warn` in bundled output sits inside a pragma-debug region; a developer can add an un-wrapped diagnostic and the stripper silently misses it (§6b proved this happens). ### Data-pipeline pillar (origin: PRINCIPAL_ENGINEER_REVIEW_DATA_PIPELINE_2026_04_16.md)

- **DP-H7** — Polyline `followSurface` / `arcType: GEODESIC` silently straight-lines on WebGPU. ✅ **SHIPPED (Batch 328, 2026-06-20) — VERIFIED-WORKING + RE-ATTRIBUTED (no rendering-code change needed; the stated root cause was wrong).** The 2026-05-30 framing ("WebGPU emits one GPU segment per adjacent position pair, no geodesic subdivision … needs CPU-side subdivision … zero `arcType`/`generateArc` hits in `Source/Renderer/WebGPU/`") mis-diagnosed the architecture. The geodesic/rhumb subdivision is **CPU-side and backend-neutral** by design — it runs in `Core/PolylineGeometry.createGeometry` (line ~406, `PolylinePipeline.generateCartesianArc`) and `DataSources/PolylineGeometryUpdater.update` (line ~719) BEFORE any renderer sees the positions, so the *correct* state is zero `arcType` references in the renderer. Probe-confirmed (`Tools/visual-regression/probe-polyline-geodesic.mjs`): (1) geodesic subdivision is CPU-side and backend-neutral (qualitatively confirmed — the same `PolylineGeometry.createGeometry` subdivision feeds BOTH backends; the committed probe's vertex-count figure was a miscount — it reported ~19.67 from a stray `/3` where the true subdivided count is ~59 — and has been removed); (2) the `PolylineCollection` path (`WebGPUPolylineRenderer`, the path DP-H7 explicitly named) renders the geodesic **CURVE identically on WebGPU and WebGL** — a 60N lon±90 great-circle arcs up over the pole, bowing **16 px** from a straight line between its endpoints and sitting **17 px** above a red straight-chord reference, with WebGPU↔WebGL diff **0.10 %** (16 vs 16 bow, 17 vs 17 sep — pixel-identical). So the geodesic does NOT straight-line through the Earth on the `Polyline`/`PolylineCollection` path; DP-H7's reproduction is not reproducible.
  - **What the investigation DID surface (the real, distinct gap):** the **appearance-based polyline PRIMITIVE path** — `PolylineColorAppearance` / `PolylineMaterialAppearance` over a `PolylineGeometry` `Primitive` — renders **NOTHING on WebGPU regardless of `arcType`** (an `arcType: NONE` straight 2-point primitive also renders 0 px on WebGPU — the qualitative conclusion holds, but the committed probe builds ZERO `Primitive`/`Appearance` objects, so the earlier "0 vs 5124 cyan px" measurement was unbacked and has been removed). Root cause is unrelated to geodesics: there is **no WGSL port** of `Shaders/PolylineCommon` + `Shaders/Appearances/PolylineColorAppearanceVS` / `PolylineMaterialAppearanceVS` (the screen-space line-width-expansion vertex path), and `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js` has no handling for the polyline appearance / its `prevPosition`/`nextPosition`/`expandAndWidth` attributes. This is a substantial missing-feature renderer (a new WGSL appearance-shader + vertex-expansion path), NOT a "route the subdivided positions" fix. **Tracked as the next concrete polyline-parity work item below (NEW-POLYLINE-APPEARANCE-PRIMITIVE-WEBGPU).**

It BUILDS, the pick command + pipeline are created (`probe-polyline-appearance-pick.mjs`: `pickCmds=1`, `hasPickPipeline=true`, correct `pickIdColor`), the color render is unregressed (cyan=19035) and there are 0 device errors — but **`scene.pick` still returns undefined** (WebGL reference picks fine: hits=285). **ROOT CAUSE:** the polyline VS does VIEWPORT-DEPENDENT screen-space ribbon expansion (`csm_getPolylineWindowCoordinates` uses `projection` → `viewportTransformation`/`viewportOrthographic` computed from the MAIN canvas `drawingBufferWidth/Height`), but `scene.pick` renders through a NARROW PICK FRUSTUM. At pick time `updateWebGPUPickCommandUniforms` writes the pick-frustum `projection` while the viewport transforms stay main-canvas-sized → the ribbon lands in the WRONG place in the pick FBO → readback misses it. The GEOMETRY pick works because it uses a single viewport-INDEPENDENT `mvpRelativeToEye`; the polyline's multi-stage screen-space math does not compose with the pick frustum. **FIX PATH (fresh context):** make the polyline pick's viewport transforms consistent with the pick frustum — either (i) thread the pick FBO's effective viewport dims into `writeRTEUniformsPolyline` when writing a polyline PICK command (so `viewportTransformation`/`viewportOrthographic` match the pick projection), or (ii) render polyline pick commands with the main (full-canvas) frustum into a full-canvas pick target rather than the narrow pick frustum. The reproduction harness `probe-polyline-appearance-pick.mjs` (samples ON-LINE pixels, NOT the zig-zag centroid) is committed + RED, ready to gate the fix.   - **(c) LOG-DEPTH — ✅ SHIPPED Batch 381 (C2-13 / 376c, 2026-06-24).** The 6 polyline appearance/material shaders wrote HYPERBOLIC `@builtin(frag_depth)` while the WebGPU globe writes LOGARITHMIC depth (`scene.logarithmicDepthBuffer` defaults TRUE) → a surface-height appearance polyline z-fought/sank into the globe at a far camera. **Fix:** added the csm log-depth recipe to `PolylineColorAppearance.wgsl` + the 5 `PolylineMat{Color,Dash,Glow,Arrow,Outline}.wgsl` (all share a byte-identical VS): a `logDepth: vec4` lane in the 512B `CameraUniforms` (floats 92-95: near, far, factor, reserved), a `//>>ifdef LOG_DEPTH` `v_logDepth` varying, the VS `csm_vertexLogDepth(output.position, near)` + `csm_updatePositionDepth` block (works because after `viewportOrthographic * positionWC` the clip-w equals the eye-space distance — bottom row `[0,0,0,1]` × the clip-w-rehomogenized `positionWC`, mirroring WebGL's `czm_vertexLogDepth()` post-ortho), and a `FragOutput` struct writing `csm_writeLogDepth(v_logDepth, camera.logDepth.z)`. The 3 helpers live (gated) in the shared `csm_polylineCommon.wgsl` chunk. JS: `writeRTEUniformsPolyline` calls `writeLogDepthTail(ud, 92, …)`; both `createPolylineAppearanceCommands` + `createPolylineMaterialAppearanceCommands` flip `ShaderDefine.LOG_DEPTH` via `isWebGPULogDepthActive` + a `cache.logDepthEnabled` rebuild trigger. The camera BGL was ALREADY `VERTEX | FRAGMENT` (no BGL fix needed, unlike C2-7). **Verified:** `probe-polyline-appearance-primitive.mjs` (cyan 12584≡12584 vs WebGL) + `probe-polyline-material-primitive.mjs` (Dash 0.999 / Glow 1.000) confirm no-regression with LOG_DEPTH active + all 6 shaders compile; `probe-polyline-appearance-logdepth.mjs` (NEW — globe ON, h=0 lines, FAR oblique 6000km camera) GREEN: WebGPU cyan 1447 vs WebGL 1464 (0.988), magenta 532/531 (1.002), `logDepthEnabled===true` on both caches, 0 NEW device errors (AtmosphereLUT filtered). PNGs READ: cyan + magenta lines rest cleanly on the globe surface, pixel-identical to WebGL — no z-fight/occlusion. **Files:** the 6 `Polyline*.wgsl`, `csm_polylineCommon.wgsl`, `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js`, `probe-polyline-appearance-logdepth.mjs`. **Defines=0 (log-depth OFF) is byte-identical to the pre-376c path** (the `//>>else` of every block emits nothing).

  - **(d) TEXTURED Image MATERIAL — ✅ SHIPPED Batch 383 (C2-14 / 376d, 2026-06-24).** `selectPolylineMaterialShader` routed `Image`/`DiffuseMap` → `polylineMatColor` (FS returns `material.color`, no texture group) → a textured polyline rendered NOTHING on WebGPU (probe: WebGL red@x290/blue@x733 along a red|blue split texture; WebGPU red=0/blue=0). **Fix:** new `PolylineMatImage.wgsl` (clone of `PolylineMatColor` VS + a `@group(2)` sampler+texture + MaterialUniforms `{repeat, color}` matching `PrimitiveMatImageFlat`; FS samples `textureSampleLevel(.., 0.0)` — explicit mip 0, since a thin polyline ribbon's implicit-derivative LOD picks a degenerate high mip and the small texture vanishes); `selectPolylineMaterialShader` routes `Image` → `polylineMatImage` with `needsTexture:true` (scoped to `Image`; `DiffuseMap`'s different fabric `{diffuse, alpha, image, repeat}` is a follow-up); `createPolylineMaterialPipeline(needsTexture)` builds a 3-binding texture BGL at group 2 (NO effects group — the polyline material FS never reads effects) so `ensureMaterialTextureBindGroup` (the surface-material helper) reuses cleanly; the builder calls it + binds `[camera, material, texture]`. **Two non-obvious bugs the probe caught:** (1) `_refreshPrimitiveEffectsSlot` swaps the shared effects BG into `bindGroups[last]` every frame — which for the textured variant is the TEXTURE → clobbered it → blank; gated with a `_noEffectsSlot` flag. (2) The command is built ONCE, before the async Image decodes, so the texture bound a placeholder/empty texture and never refreshed (`_imageSources.image` is `undefined` until load); added a per-frame `ensureMaterialTextureBindGroup` refresh in the polyline update hook (keys on image identity → rebuilds exactly once on decode, then early-returns). **Verified:** `probe-polyline-image-material.mjs` (NEW) — WebGPU now **pixel-identical to WebGL** (red 8780@x290, blue 8780@x733), PNG READ (red→blue split along the line); non-textured materials unregressed (Dash 0.999 / Glow 1.000 / all 2D modes 1.000). **Original gap (context):** A `Primitive` built over `PolylineGeometry` with `PolylineColorAppearance` or `PolylineMaterialAppearance` renders nothing on WebGPU (any `arcType`, including `NONE`). The `PolylineCollection`/`Polyline` runtime path works (renders curves identically to WebGL — see DP-H7), but the appearance-based primitive path is unimplemented: `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js` only handles `LINES`/`LINE_STRIP`/`LINE_LOOP` (geometry-outline line-lists) and has no path for the polyline appearances, which expand a TRIANGLES strip in the VS using `PolylineCommon`'s screen-space width math over the `prevPosition`/`nextPosition`/`expandAndWidth` vertex attributes. **Needs:** a WGSL port of `PolylineCommon` + `PolylineColorAppearanceVS` / `PolylineMaterialAppearanceVS` and the matching attribute/uniform wiring in `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js` (RTE high/low encoding of the subdivided positions; the polyline geometry already supplies subdivided `arcType` positions CPU-side). **Probe:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-polyline-geodesic.mjs` records the gap (PolylineCollection path PASSES; the appearance-primitive case is the documented residual). **Files:** new `Shaders/WebGPU/.../Polyline*.wgsl`, `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js`, `Scene/PolylineColorAppearance.js`/`PolylineMaterialAppearance.js` (VS plumbing). **Trace:** Batch 328 DP-H7 finding above. (COLOR slice shipped Batch 343 — see the status at the top of this entry.)
- **NEW-WEBGPU-UNIFORMSTATE-VIEWPORT** (S–M) — ✅ **SHIPPED (Batch 368, item 371).** Seeded `this._uniformState.viewport = {x:0, y:0, width:drawingBufferWidth, height:drawingBufferHeight}` once per frame in `WebGPUContext.beginFrame` (after `_ensureDepthTexture`, before `_beginDefaultRenderPass`). The setter only reads x/y/width/height, so a plain object literal suffices (no `BoundingRectangle` import). ORDERING: `Scene.render()` calls `Matrix4.setDepthRangeType("webgpu")` before `beginFrame`, so the lazy `cleanViewport` ortho z-mapping uses the WebGPU 0..1 branch. The canonical `uniformState.viewportOrthographic`/`viewportTransformation` getters are now correct (the per-renderer `drawingBufferWidth/Height` fallbacks in `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands`/GroundPolyline/etc. are LEFT in place — retiring them is a follow-up). **Verified** (`probe-uniformstate-viewport-371.mjs`, NEW): WebGPU `viewportTransformation` is now NON-identity = `[512,0,0,0, 0,384,0,0, 0,0,0.5,0, 512,384,0.5,1]` (1024×768) and **matches WebGL within 1e-3** (was IDENTITY — the WebGL-vs-WebGPU match IS the baseline isolation), `viewport`==canvas, the screen-space polyline ribbon still renders (cyan 12588, PNG READ — clean full-width zig-zag), 0 console errors. **Files:** `WebGPUContext.ts`.\n  - **ORIGINAL:** `UniformState.viewport` is only ever seeded by the WebGL `RenderState.applyViewport` path (`gl.viewport`); the WebGPU render path never set it, so `uniformState.viewportOrthographic` / `viewportTransformation` stayed at IDENTITY on WebGPU. Any screen-space WebGPU shader needing window coordinates must therefore build these matrices MANUALLY from `context.drawingBufferWidth/Height` — the polyline appearance primitive (Batch 343 `writeRTEUniformsPolyline`) + the Billboard / BufferPolyline collections already do this. **Proper fix:** seed `uniformState.viewport` (the render-pass viewport rect) in the WebGPU render-pass setup so the `viewportOrthographic` / `viewportTransformation` getters work for ALL screen-space WebGPU shaders, then drop the per-shader manual builds. **Files:** the WebGPU render-pass setup, `UniformState.js`. **Trace:** Batch 343 polyline color slice (the IDENTITY viewport re-collapsed the polyline to 0px on the first build before the manual workaround).
- **DP-H18** — `depthFailAppearance` — **✅ DONE (color-appearance slice, C2-23 / Batch 390, 2026-06-24).** `createWebGPUCommands` now emits a depth-fail twin command after each main color command: new `PrimitiveDepthFailColor.wgsl` (flat RTE-color VS reusing the main vertex buffer; FS returns the per-instance `depthFailColor` from a 16-byte material UB) + a `depthCompare:'greater'` / `depthWriteEnabled:false` pipeline with `cullMode:'none'` (so a closed volume's back faces show through as the depth-fail color, matching WebGL). Per-instance `depthFailColor` read CPU-side from the batch table like `color`. Verified: `probe-depthfail-appearance.mjs` (blue box, red depthFail, grey occluder, both backends) — WebGPU red 40176 == WebGL red 40176, grey parity 1.00, GREEN, PNG read.
- **NEW-WEBGPU-DEPTHFAIL-MATERIAL** — **✅ DONE (material-appearance slice, Batch 419, 2026-06-26).** Mirrors the color twin in `createWebGPUMaterialCommands`: when a primitive's MAIN appearance has a material (MaterialAppearance / Entity polygon-box `depthFailMaterial` / GroundPrimitive) AND `_depthFailAppearance` carries a material, a depthFail TWIN material command is emitted after each main material command. The twin reuses the SAME material shader the main path would select for the depthFail material (via `selectMaterialShader(depthFailMaterial, …)` — Color/Stripe/Grid/etc., so the occluded region shows the real depthFail appearance, not a flat color), bound into a dedicated `df*` sub-cache pipeline that differs from the main material pipeline ONLY in depth state + cull: `depthCompare:'greater'` + `depthWriteEnabled:false`, and `cullMode` **DERIVED FROM THE DEPTHFAIL APPEARANCE** (not hardcoded). WebGL's depthFail render state IS `_depthFailAppearance.getRenderState()` with only `depthTest.func → GREATER` (`PrimitiveCommandHelpers.createRenderStates` line 65), so the cull comes from the depthFail appearance's own `closed` flag via `Appearance.getDefaultRenderState`: `closed:true` → back-face cull (depthFail shows only where genuinely occluded — the un-occluded main pass survives), explicit `cull.enabled:false` → none, non-closed default → none (the back face shows through as the canonical x-ray look). Same `closedAndCulled` shape the main material pipeline uses. (An initial pass hardcoded `cullMode:'none'`, mirroring a stale doc description — that made WebGPU ignore the depthFail appearance's cull and DIVERGE from WebGL for a `closed:true` depthFail appearance: WebGL went all-blue/red-0 while WebGPU stayed full-red. Fixed in the same batch; cull state is tracked in the pipeline signature so it rebuilds on change.) FULL mirror — not partial: own RTE vertex buffer (the df shader's flat/lit layout may differ from the main shader's, so reusing the main VB across a stride mismatch is unsafe — dedicated VB built per geometry), own camera UB (sized to df isLit), own material UB from `depthFailMaterial._uniformBuffer.gpuData`, and own texture bind group (textured df fabrics like Image route through `ensureMaterialTextureBindGroup` reused via a DF field-key set, no forked copy). The twin command is tagged with the real `mat*`/`pbr*` df shader type so the existing per-frame `updateWebGPUMaterialCommandUniforms` dispatch (`st.startsWith("mat")` in `PrimitiveCommandHelpers`) keeps its camera + material UBs current and refreshes the effects slot (with `_noEffectsSlot` set for textured df variants to avoid clobbering the texture). `Primitive.update` now also calls `this._depthFailMaterial.update(context)` so the df material's `_uniformBuffer.gpuData` is populated/refreshed (backend-neutral, no-op for the color slice). **Verified** (`probe-depthfail-material.mjs`, two configs, both backends, PNGs read): config A (depthFail NON-closed, cull none) WebGPU red **40176** == WebGL red **40176** (the depthFail MATERIAL x-rays the occluded box, grey parity 1.00); config B (depthFail CLOSED, cull back) WebGPU red **0** == WebGL red **0**, blue **40698** ≈ WebGL **40699** (cull honored — pins the cull-derivation fix), 0 device errors, GREEN. **Files:** `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.js` (df sub-cache + `createMaterialDepthFailPipeline` with depthFail-appearance cull derivation + twin emit + `ensureMaterialTextureBindGroup` field-key generalization), `Primitive.js` (`_depthFailMaterial.update`), `probe-depthfail-material.mjs`. The color slice (Batch 390) path is untouched.
- **DP-H35** — glTF morph-target NORMAL deltas dropped: `WebGPUModelMorphTargets.js` `packMorphTargetDeltas` packed only `positionData`; morph-animated normals stayed on the rest pose while positions deformed (WebGL morphs them via `MorphTargetsStageVS.getMorphedNormal`). ✅ **SHIPPED (Batch 329, 2026-06-20).** **Fix:** the morph storage buffer now interleaves, per vertex per target, a `[positionDelta, normalDelta]` vec4 PAIR (`FLOATS_PER_VERTEX_PER_TARGET = 8`). `packMorphTargetDeltas` writes the POSITION delta at `dstIdx` and the NORMAL delta at `dstIdx+4` (zero when the target has no NORMAL accessor — a no-op, matching WebGL). `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl` reads the pair via `base = (t*vertexCount + vid) * 2u` → `posDelta = morphDeltas[base]`, `nrmDelta = morphDeltas[base + 1u]`, accumulates `normalMC += nrmDelta * w`, then re-normalizes (guarded for a near-zero result). The TAA prev-frame morph block steps the same `*2u` stride and reads only `[base]` (position) — prev-frame velocity unchanged. **Lockstep kept byte-consistent:** CPU `FLOATS_PER_VERTEX_PER_TARGET = 8` ↔ WGSL `*2u` vec4 stride (8 floats = 2×vec4). Position-morph path and WebGL morph untouched. **Decisive isolation finding (this is why the first probe verdict was misleading):** AnimatedMorphCube **target 0 carries a ZERO NORMAL delta** (decoded accessor maxAbs = 0.0 — it translates faces without reorienting them); only **target 1** has the real NORMAL delta (maxAbs 0.705). A controlled normal-ON/OFF build A/B at the **target-1** morph (identical silhouette) gave WebGPU lit mean **65.3 (normals ON) vs 98.6 (OFF)** — a 33-unit shading swing attributable solely to the normal morph, proving the path works. An earlier `[1,0]` (target-0) probe weight could never show a normal effect regardless of the fix. **Probe:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-morph-normals.mjs` (now weights **target 1**, `[0,1]`) asserts: (1) cross-backend silhouette/lit-pixel-count parity (position morph unchanged: 0.01%); (2) WebGPU within-backend rest→morphed luma ratio ×1.22 sits well below the frozen-normal reference ×1.84 (= normals re-shade); (3) cross-backend ratio gap 8.4% (BRDF gray gap divided out). PASS for the right reason; flipping normals OFF makes it FAIL (ratio ×1.84, gap 38.3%) — not a tautology. **Files:** `packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUModelMorphTargets.js`, `packages/engine/Source/Shaders/WebGPU/Model/ModelPBRComplete.wgsl`, `Tools/visual-regression/probe-morph-normals.mjs`.

  - **OPEN — root-caused (2026-06-21, this investigation). NOT a KHR_materials_specular F0/factor/tint bug; it is a deeper diffuse-IBL prefilter-energy mismatch (SH vs irradiance-cubemap). - **NEW-MODEL-MORPH-TANGENT-DELTAS** (S, FUTURE — surfaced Batch 329 DP-H35, 2026-06-20) — Batch 329 (`7af0334417`) shipped glTF morph-target **NORMAL** deltas on WebGPU (DP-H35) but did **not** also morph the **TANGENT** attribute: `WebGPUModelMorphTargets.js` interleaves only `[positionDelta, normalDelta]` per vertex per target, so a morphed normal-mapped model keeps its rest-pose tangent frame while the surface deforms (WebGL morphs it via `MorphTargetsStageVS.getMorphedTangent`). **Benign for textureless / non-normal-mapped assets** (no tangent consumed → no visible error, which is why it was deferred), but **needed for normal-mapped morphed models** where the bitangent (and thus the tangent-space normal) drifts as the mesh deforms. **Fix path (small follow-up, mirrors the NORMAL work):** widen the per-vertex-per-target morph element from a 2-vec4 `[pos, nrm]` pair to a 3-vec4 `[pos, nrm, tan]` triple (`FLOATS_PER_VERTEX_PER_TARGET 8 → 12`, WGSL stride `*2u → *3u`), pack the TANGENT delta (zero when the target has no TANGENT accessor — no-op), and accumulate `tangentMC += tanDelta * w` + re-orthonormalize in `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl`. Keep the CPU↔WGSL lockstep byte-consistent (the same triple-consistency discipline DP-H35/DP-H36 call out). **Files:** `WebGPUModelMorphTargets.js`, `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl`, extend `probe-morph-normals.mjs` with a normal-mapped-morph-target asset assertion. **Trace:** Batch 329 DP-H35.
- **DP-H36** — glTF instance translation not split for RTE: `WebGPUModelInstancing.js` wrote the translation column as raw f32. At ECEF magnitudes > 2²² sub-meter precision is lost; instanced 3D-Tiles content (i3dm) placed up to ~1 m off its true position vs WebGL's RTE path. ✅ **SHIPPED (Batch 325, 2026-06-19).** Root cause: the per-instance storage element was a single `mat4x4<f32>` whose column 3 (translation) was the large-magnitude term. In `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl` the instance matrix multiplied the local vertex position BEFORE the RTE camera subtract — `(instMat * pos)` produced an Earth-scale model-space position stored back into `positionMC: vec3<f32>`, so the sub-meter bits were gone before `positionMC - encodedCameraMC` could cancel them. **Fix:** widened the per-instance storage element to a 24-float / 96-byte `InstanceTransform { linear: mat4x4, translationHigh: vec4, translationLow: vec4 }`. The CPU (`WebGPUModelInstancing.js`) now splits the translation column via `EncodedCartesian3.encode` (zeroing the linear matrix's col3); the WGSL applies only the linear 3×3 to the (small-magnitude) local position and folds the translation into the RTE subtract: `rte = (translationHigh - camHigh) + (translationLow - camLow) + positionMC`. Non-instanced path is byte-identical (high/low default to zero → original `pos - camHigh - camLow`). **Lockstep triple kept consistent:** CPU pack width `FLOATS_PER_INSTANCE = 24` ↔ GPU storage buffer stride (auto from `byteLength`) + default-buffer size 64→96 bytes in `WebGPUModelPipelineCache.js` ↔ WGSL `InstanceTransform` struct (96 bytes). The shadow-cast `modelInstancedSB` variant in `WebGPUShadowMapRenderer.js` (shared by the single-shadow-map + CSM cast paths) was updated to read the same struct (recombining the translation in model space; the depth-only pass tolerates the residual, and TAA prev-frame instancing similarly recombines). Matrix-instancing (full 4×3) and vec3-translation instancing converge on the same column-3 translation, so both are covered. **WebGL instancing untouched** (`InstancingPipelineStage` unchanged; Instancing/I3dmLoader specs green). **Probe:** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-i3dm-instance-jitter.mjs` loads `InstancedWithBatchTable` (i3dm, lon −75.61 / lat 40.04) on both backends with a stationary camera + hidden globe; asserts WebGPU A↔B pixel-stability (0.00%) and WebGPU-vs-WebGL placement match (0.19%, AA-edge noise only). PNGs read: instances render at identical screen positions on both backends.

- **DP-H47** — `czm_atmosphere*` auto-uniform suite entirely absent from `csm_*`; atmosphere-sensitive renderers (SkyAtmosphere, GroundAtmosphere, VolumetricFog) each hand-roll their own pull from `frameState.atmosphericConditions`, producing inconsistency between renderers. **CONFIRMED REAL + SCOPED (Batch 304) — NOT a bug-bash-sized fix; documented scope (per Phase-12 "add the shared suite OR document scope").** The WebGL side defines a full `czm_atmosphere*` auto-uniform set in `Renderer/AutomaticUniforms.js` (`czm_atmosphereHsbShift`, `czm_atmosphereLightIntensity`, `czm_atmosphereRayleighCoefficient`, `czm_atmosphereRayleighScaleHeight`, `czm_atmosphereMieCoefficient`, `czm_atmosphereMieScaleHeight`, `czm_atmosphereMieAnisotropy`, `czm_atmosphereDynamicLighting`) sourced from `UniformState`. On WebGPU there is no shared `csm_atmosphere*` block: `WebGPUSkyAtmosphereRenderer.js` (lines ~334/451/466/743–787/822–856), `WebGPUProceduralCloudRenderer.ts`, the globe ground-atmosphere path in `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts`, and `ModelAtmosphereStage.wgsl` each independently re-read `frameState.atmosphericConditions` / the `skyAtmosphere` object and pack their own per-renderer uniform layouts with their own DEFAULT_* fallbacks — so a custom `scene.atmosphere.rayleighCoefficient` (etc.) can land in one renderer's packing and be silently defaulted in another. **Why it is not a bug-bash fix:** closing it requires a NEW shared atmosphere uniform-block contract (a `csm_atmosphere*` suite mirroring the WebGL auto-uniform set) plus a single CPU pack path off `UniformState`, plus rewiring EVERY atmosphere-consuming WGSL renderer's bind groups to that block and deleting their hand-rolled packings — a multi-renderer uniform-architecture change, not a localized edit. Doing it partially (one renderer adopts the suite, others keep hand-rolling) would create exactly the partial-implementation/scaffolding debt Principle 7 warns against. **Tracked as the next concrete atmosphere-consistency work item** (Principle 9): build `csm_atmosphere*` as a real shared block + UniformState pack, migrate SkyAtmosphere → ProceduralClouds → GlobeGroundAtmosphere → ModelAtmosphereStage to it in one arc. Until then the renderers remain consistent in PRACTICE only because they share the same `DEFAULT_*` constants and the common case leaves `atmosphericConditions` at defaults.
  - **RE-VERIFIED + SHARPENED 2026-07-04 (campaign Q24, premise CONFIRMED REAL — not stale; no code shipped, honest defer).** Live-code audit found the entry's own closing claim ("consistent in PRACTICE only because they share the same `DEFAULT_*` constants") is **FACTUALLY WRONG** — the per-renderer defaults **materially diverge**, which turns DP-H47 from a uniform-plumbing swap into a **visual re-tuning epic**:
    - `WebGPUSkyAtmosphereRenderer.js:86-98` uses `rayleighCoefficient.z = 22.4e-6`, `rayleighScaleHeight = 8500`, `mieScaleHeight = 1200`, `mieAnisotropy = 0.758`, and `lightIntensity` default `50.0` (`skyAtmosphere.atmosphereLightIntensity || 50.0`, line 544). These are a **different atmosphere model** (precomputed-scattering/Bruneton-style LUT tuning), NOT the canonical `Scene/Atmosphere.js` defaults.
    - Canonical `Scene/Atmosphere.js` (= what WebGL `czm_atmosphere*` sources): `rayleighCoefficient.z = 28.4e-6`, `rayleighScaleHeight = 10000`, `mieScaleHeight = 3200`, `mieAnisotropy = 0.9`, `lightIntensity = 10.0`. `WebGPUDynamicEnvironmentMapManager.ts:1001-1006` (the Model/IBL sky-fill path) already reads `frameState.atmosphere.*` with THESE canonical fallbacks — so **Sky and Model already disagree at defaults**, before any user override. Unifying Sky onto the canonical suite is therefore **NOT byte-identical**: it visibly changes the tuned, visually-verified WebGPU sky and demands a full sky-look re-verification against WebGL (a re-tune, not a plumb).
    - **Clouds are NOT a scattering consumer:** `WebGPUProceduralCloudRenderer.ts` has **0** references to rayleigh/mie/`frameState.atmosphere` — it reads only the cloud-specific `atmosphericConditions.clouds` path. The "four renderers" framing overcounts the `czm_atmosphere*` **scattering** suite; the genuine scattering/HSB consumers are **Sky + Model(DynEnvMap) + the ground HSB-shift path** (`GlobeFS.glsl` HSB applied to ground color; ground *scattering* is deliberately sourced from `globe.atmosphere*`/`tileProvider.*`, a WebGL-parity distinction — see `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts:506-548`, comment lines 516-522).
    - **Ground shaders under active churn:** the ground-atmosphere shaders (`GlobeFS.glsl`, `GlobeTerrain.wgsl`) are being modified batch-over-batch by adjacent campaign work; the ground-HSB leg of DP-H47 should land only after they settle, to avoid rebasing a shared-uniform change onto a moving target.
    - **SKY leg is ALREADY WebGL-faithful — do NOT wire `scene.atmosphere.*` into the sky (verified 2026-07-04, campaign Q24R, premiseStale).** The proposed "increment 1" (route the WebGPU SkyAtmosphere scattering coefficients through `scene.atmosphere.*` to "match WebGL responsiveness") rests on a MISREAD of the WebGL sky. Empirically (`Tools/visual-regression/probe-sky-atmosphere-coeffs.mjs`, both backends, PNGs read) AND by code: the WebGL SKY is driven ONLY by the SkyAtmosphere INSTANCE coefficients (`u_atmosphereRayleighCoefficient`, bound in `Scene/SkyAtmosphere.js:258` → consumed by `AtmosphereCommon.glsl computeScattering`); it does **NOT** read `scene.atmosphere.rayleighCoefficient` (`czm_atmosphere*` drives only the GROUND path + the Model/IBL sky-fill via `ComputeRadianceMapFS.glsl czm_computeScattering`). WebGPU's `WebGPUSkyAtmosphereRenderer.packUniforms` (line ~960) ALREADY reads the same `skyAtmosphere.atmosphereRayleighCoefficient`, so the sky-coefficient parity is closed at BOTH defaults and overrides: reversing the Rayleigh coefficient (blue→red-heavy) via the instance property REVERSES the sky identically on both backends (WebGL |dR|+|dB|=202.8, WebGPU=202.3; default cross-backend Δ=1.3), while a `scene.atmosphere.rayleighCoefficient` override moves NEITHER backend's sky (both 0.0). Wiring `scene.atmosphere.*` into the WebGPU sky would make it DIVERGE from WebGL, not converge — so increment-1-as-scoped is a REGRESSION and was NOT shipped. NOTE this also refines the DP-H47 "inconsistency between WebGPU renderers" framing: WebGPU's sky-reads-instance / model-IBL-reads-`scene.atmosphere` split MIRRORS WebGL's identical sky/model split, so it is WebGL-faithful, not a parity bug. The genuinely open DP-H47 work is the WebGPU-internal *consistency* nicety (a shared resolver so a user who sets BOTH `scene.atmosphere.*` and the instance props gets coherent cross-renderer behavior) + the default-constant re-tune — both still deferred per the arc above. Regression guard: `probe-sky-atmosphere-coeffs.mjs`.

This is the load-bearing consistency fix and is byte-identical-off. (2) Migrate Sky + Model(DynEnvMap) CPU packing to the resolver (CPU-only, no bind-group/WGSL change, low risk, verifiable via a `probe-atmosphere-custom-params.mjs` that sets `scene.atmosphere.rayleighCoefficient` and asserts BOTH the WebGPU sky AND the model-IBL react + converge toward WebGL). (4) Ground HSB + clouds are out of the scattering suite; track ground-HSB parity as its own item once the ground shaders settle. **Do NOT attempt (1)-(4) as one autonomous pass** — the default-divergence + in-flux ground shaders make a single-pass 4-renderer convergence unverifiable.

### Scene-mode morph (3D ⇄ Columbus ⇄ 2D transition) pillar (origin: webgpu-morph-review audit, 2026-06-07)

Multi-agent audit of the WebGPU morph (transition) animation. Two confirmed P1s were fixed (Batch 216): the globe MORPHING `mesh.center` double-count (terrain splayed apart for the whole transition) and the ground-polyline `morphTime` typo. Remaining confirmed findings are deferred here.

- **MORPH-EXAG-SKIRTS** — ✅ **SHIPPED (Batch 362, 2026-06-23).** Vertical exaggeration was DROPPED during MORPHING and COLUMBUS_VIEW on WebGPU: `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` gated the exaggeration position-offset on `camera.sceneMode > 2.5` (SCENE3D only) AND fed the planar (CV/morph) legs RAW height, so CV/morph terrain rendered flat and a morph would pop between an exaggerated 3D leg and a flat planar leg. **Root cause of the Batch-216 skirt-wall failure (now understood + avoided):** the naive ungate exaggerated `length(position3D) − radius` (the GEOMETRIC height). Skirt vertices carry a REDUCED height ATTRIBUTE (`heightSample −= skirtHeight`, `HeightmapTessellator.js:399`), and their geometric position is extruded down — exaggerating the geometric length pushed skirts into tall visible vertical WALLS. **Fix:** mirror WebGL (`GlobeVS.glsl:245-258`) EXACTLY — exaggerate the vertex HEIGHT ATTRIBUTE (`resolvedHeight`): `newHeight = (resolvedHeight − rel)*exag + rel` (clamped to `−radius`); feed `newHeight` to the planar `computePlanarPosition` (which uses height as the projected X axis) for CV + the morph planar leg; offset the 3D position along the geodetic ellipsoid normal by `(newHeight − resolvedHeight)` for SCENE3D + the morph 3D leg (un-gated from `sceneMode > 2.5` so all modes exaggerate consistently — no morph pop). `resolvedHeight` is now computed from the RAW (un-exaggerated) position so exaggeration can't feed back into its own input. Because the exaggerated skirt's height is the ATTRIBUTE-based value, the (taller) skirt quad still points DOWN below the surface and stays occluded by the adjacent tile exactly as in WebGL — clean peaks, no walls. **Verified probe-first** (`probe-exaggeration-cv.mjs`, EXAG=10 Himalayas): WebGPU CV went from FLAT (no relief) to a full exaggerated peak field matching the WebGL reference, zero shattered walls. Didn't-break: SCENE3D exaggeration unchanged (NEW `probe-exaggeration-3d.mjs`, PNGs read — the attribute-vs-length offset diff is sub-meter for non-skirt terrain; baseline-isolated to confirm the pre-existing blue water streaks are NOT introduced by this change); normal globe (exaggeration == 1.0) byte-identical (camera-track meanDiff 1.557% == baseline; `planarHeight == resolvedHeight` and `exaggeratedPosition == position` when exag == 1.0). Files: `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` only. **Surfaced a separate pre-existing issue (NEW-WEBGPU-EXAG-WATER-STREAKS below).**
- **NEW-WEBGPU-EXAG-WATER-STREAKS** — ✅ **STALE-RESOLVED (Q12, 2026-07-04) — closed by Q10 (Batch 541, NEW-GLOBE-DAYTIME-OCEAN-BRIGHTNESS).** The Batch 379 diagnosis had LOCALIZED this to a globe-FS water-fragment colour/saturation divergence (atmosphere OFF: WebGL lakes grey-bright ~0 blue-streak px vs WebGPU lakes saturated dark-blue 2452 px @ meanRGB(18,17,123) — the blue lived in the water fragment itself, independent of atmosphere + LOD). Q10 rewrote exactly that path in `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` `computeEnhancedOcean`: the highlight taper now uses `tile.groundAtmosphereControl.y` (WebGL's atmosphere lightingFade) instead of the day/night `dayFade`, and `tsPerturbationRatio` derives from the distance-faded tangent normal `normalize(vec3(waveN.xy * waveIntensityFade, waveN.z)).z`. That desaturated the over-blue exaggerated-lake water to match WebGL. **Re-verified probe-first (2026-07-04, premise-verify-first):** `diag-exag-water-streaks-2x2.mjs` now reports WebGPU tracking WebGL exactly — atmosphere OFF **both 0 blue-streak px** (was 2452 on WebGPU), atmosphere ON both ~3500 px @ meanRGB≈(59,93,131). NEW deterministic `Tools/visual-regression/probe-exag-water-streaks.mjs` (pinned clock via the Q7 determinism kit) locks it in with a core guard (webgpu-off blue px ≤ 300) + cross-backend parity (meanB |Δ|≤15, px ratio 0.7–1.4) — PASS. All 4 PNGs read: same muted turquoise glacial lakes on both backends, no WebGPU-only streaks. No shader/code change this task (the fix landed in Q10). *Original entry retained below for history.* **[HISTORICAL] Confirmed PRE-EXISTING + NOT caused by MORPH-EXAG-SKIRTS (Batch 362):** baseline-isolated — the streaks appear in WebGPU SCENE3D exaggeration BOTH before and after the Batch-362 planar-exaggeration fix (the fix is the only `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` change and was stashed/rebuilt/re-probed; the streaks were present in the stashed/pre-fix build). The exaggeration merely AMPLIFIES the existing water/ocean-color parity gap by deepening valleys (more water surface visible). Likely the globe FS ocean/water-tint or water-mask path tinting low-altitude/water fragments brighter blue than WebGL's `czm_phong` + water-mask composite. **Open — separate water-rendering parity item; probe: probe-exaggeration-3d.mjs (READ the PNGs — WebGPU shows blue streaks WebGL lacks).**
  - **DIAGNOSED Batch 379 (C2-6) — root cause LOCALIZED + two hypotheses RULED OUT.** New `Tools/visual-regression/diag-exag-water-streaks-2x2.mjs` captures the 2×2 {webgl,webgpu}×{atmo-on,atmo-off} at the Himalaya EXAG=10 repro view (lon 86.9, lat 27.0, h 250km) + dumps per-backend rendered tile levels + a bright-blue-streak pixel metric. Decisive results (READ all 4 PNGs):

    - **NOT (only) atmosphere:** with atmosphere OFF on both, WebGL lakes go grey-bright `meanRGB(167,176,198)` with ~0 blue-streak px (12), but **WebGPU lakes STAY saturated dark-blue `meanRGB(18,17,123)` (2452 px)** — atmosphere on/off barely changes WebGPU (2503→2452). WebGL's blue at atmo-on (3635 px) is the atmosphere drape, which it correctly drops at atmo-off; WebGPU has no such atmosphere dependence because the blue is in the WATER FRAGMENT itself.
    - **CONCLUSION:** WebGPU's globe FS colors the glacial-lake water-body fragments vivid saturated blue (+ darker surrounding terrain) where WebGL renders them muted/desaturated — a **globe-FS water-fragment color/saturation divergence**, independent of atmosphere + LOD. `computeEnhancedOcean` additive highlights were already ruled out (Batch 365). **NEXT STEP (the fix):** use `CesiumDebug.globeFragmentDebug(name)` to isolate which stage produces the blue — candidates in `GlobeTerrain.wgsl`: `computeWaterColor` (line ~2050, water-mask-gated), the per-layer imagery saturation chain (`adjustColor` line ~1605 / ~1833-1844), or the DP-H24 globe hue/sat/brightness shift (line ~270) — then match the WebGL `GlobeFS.glsl` water/imagery path term-for-term. **Effort:** ~1 session (now that it's localized).
  - **INVESTIGATION 2026-06-23 (Batch 365 attempt) — root cause NARROWED, the two obvious suspects RULED OUT, DEFERRED as a deeper globe-lighting/water-fragment parity item.** Two decisive isolations: **(1) NOT `computeEnhancedOcean`** — zeroing its entire `oceanContribution` (`var color = baseColor + oceanContribution * 0.0;`, rebuilt + reprobed) left the blue streaks UNCHANGED, so the water-color/highlight function (diffuseHighlight / nonDiffuseHighlight / specular / foam) is NOT the source. (A first attempt — fading `tsPerturbationRatio` by the WebGL `waveFade(70000,1000000,dist)` distance curve, mirroring GlobeFS.glsl:816-817 — also did nothing, consistent with this.) **(2) NOT fog / ground-atmosphere / sky-atmosphere** — `diag-exag-water-streaks-source.mjs` captured WebGPU with `scene.fog.enabled=false` + `globe.showGroundAtmosphere=false` + `skyAtmosphere.show=false` (no rebuild); the blue streaks PERSIST. So it is NOT the atmosphere/fog blend either. **Remaining cause:** the streaks are the **base Bing imagery** of the glacial lakes (which ARE turquoise in the aerial) surviving on WebGPU where WebGL renders them muted/dark — i.e. a globe **lighting / material water-fragment** parity gap. WebGL feeds `materialInput.waterMask = mask` into its `czm_phong` material composite (GlobeFS.glsl:515) and its lighting coefficients differ from the WGSL (the GlobeTerrain.wgsl lighting block is a documented "INTENTIONAL ALGORITHMIC REWRITE … coefficients are different … WGSL adds a terminator glow"). The likely fix is in the WGSL **lighting/ambient** path (or a missing water-mask darkening of the material), NOT the ocean-color or atmosphere paths the heading originally guessed. **Next step:** isolate the WGSL globe lighting block (ambient floor + Lambert coefficients + any water-mask material term) vs WebGL `czm_phong` + `materialInput.waterMask` for water fragments; this is its own focused globe-lighting batch (broad blast radius — touches all globe shading), not a water-color tweak. **Diagnostics kept:** `diag-exag-water-streaks-source.mjs` (atmosphere-off isolation). Pre-existing, non-default (only visible at extreme EXAG over glacial-lake terrain); LOW priority.
- ~~**MORPH-POLYLINE-COLLECTION-2D**~~ — **SHIPPED 2026-06-13 (Phase 3 Slice 4, PLAN_2DCV_MORPH_BATCHES Batch 3).** `PolylineCollection` now renders at the correct map location in steady SCENE2D, COLUMBUS_VIEW, and through MORPHING on WebGPU. Implemented in `WebGPUPolylineRenderer.js` ONLY (WGSL byte-identical — no new attributes, no GPU morph branch). Three coupled fixes: **(1) scene-mode-projected position encoding** — the segment + pick builders now encode each endpoint via `SceneTransforms.computeActualEllipsoidPosition` (identity in SCENE3D → byte-identical; `(proj.z, proj.x, proj.y)` in CV; `(0, proj.x, proj.y)` in 2D; CPU-side per-vertex `morphTime` lerp in MORPHING — the same `.zxy` swizzle + manual lerp WebGL's `PolylineVS.glsl:39-65` does on the GPU). The existing mode-aware `mvpRelativeToEye` (built from `uniformState.view/projection`) then projects them correctly in every mode. The WGSL pipeline previously hardcoded `less-equal` + depth-write, so the CV polyline z-fought the co-planar map surface and rendered as a truncated wedge; a new `noDepthTest` pipeline variant (`always` + no depth-write, keyed into the pipeline cache alongside `defines`) matches WebGL. **Verified probe-first** (`probe-collections-2dcv-morph.mjs`): polyline cyan went 2D 6→1764px (ratio 0.96 vs WebGL), CV 0→1425px (0.89), 3D unchanged at 0.96; crop screenshots confirm full-length uniform-width lines visually identical to WebGL in both 2D and CV. SCENE3D stays byte-identical. All standing gates green (polyline-cloud-consume, collections-regression, far-camera, TAA, orbital-catalog, pickposition, upstream-regression, sandcastle-smoke). **Phase-3-continuation queue (NOT regressions; explicitly deferred):** the antimeridian (IDL) segment split (WebGL `intersectsIDL` / `_segments` — punted per the plan, low-impact for non-IDL-crossing lines); mid-morph polyline velocity/motion-vectors during a perspective↔ortho flip (`MORPH-TAA-PREVVP` — the velocity prev-VP is still 3D while prev positions are projected, harmless until TAA is on mid-morph and only for the base color material); and the remaining morph backlog (`MORPH-EXAG-SKIRTS`, `MORPH-MODEL-PROJECT2D`, `MORPH-PICK`).
