Per-collection plan: thread `frameState.mode` + the 2D/CV projected position + the 2D camera UB into each WebGPU collection renderer (`WebGPUBillboardRenderer`, `WebGPUPointPrimitiveRenderer`, `WebGPULabelRenderer`) and WGSL (sceneMode branch / morphTime blend), mirroring how `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` + the globe camera UB handle 2D/CV.** Reproducer: `probe-collections-2dcv-morph.mjs`. **Phase 3 Slice 1 landed (Batch 261, NEW-COLLECTIONS-PER-FRUSTUM-CAMERA-UB):** the per-frustum camera-UB resolver FOUNDATION is now wired into all five collection FRs via the shared `WebGPUCollectionCameraUB` helper (distinct per-slice GPU camera buffers selected by `uniformState._currentSliceIndex` through `bindGroupResolvers`, mirroring `WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer`'s Batch-173 pattern). Slice 1 is byte-identical in 3D (each slice copies the full-frustum reference bake — NOT a draw-time per-slice repack, which regressed far-camera multi-frustum 3D to all-zero and was caught + reverted probe-first) and intentionally does NOT yet fix 2D/CV (still all-zero). **Remaining (Slices 2-3, next concrete work):** (2) projected-frame RTE eye encoding (`inverse(view)` eye) + the per-slice projection DIVERGENCE the resolver buffers now make possible, mode-gated to 2D/CV; (3) morph blend (`position2D`/`position3D` × `czm_morphTime`). **Phase 3 Slice 2 PARTIAL landed (2026-06-13, NEW-COLLECTIONS-2DCV-PROJECTED-FRAME-RTE):** two principled, regression-free fixes in `WebGPUCollectionCameraUB` + the three collection FRs (`WebGPUPointPrimitiveRenderer`, `WebGPUBillboardRenderer`, `WebGPULabelRenderer`). **(a) Per-slice MVP repack** — `makeResolver({repackPerSlice})` (TRUE in 2D/CV/MORPHING, FALSE → byte-identical in 3D) re-invokes the `pack` closure at DRAW time so `mvpRelativeToEye` bakes against the LIVE slice projection the frustum loop just established. This was THE 2D-clip fix: collections bake at FR-update time when `uniformState.projection` is still the WebGL-range `[-1,1]` matrix, so in SCENE2D the ortho depth-range mismatch put a surface point at NDC z≈7.3 (clipped); the draw-time repack reads the WebGPU-range slice projection (z≈0.026) and the geometry lands in valid clip space at the correct screen XY (verified: globe-hidden, collections render at the right place in 2D AND CV). **(b) Log-depth encode-frustum consistency** — `packUniforms` now prefers the globe-stashed full-frustum `uniformState._logDepthEncodeNearFar` over the per-slice `currentFrustum` for the logDepth vec4, so a per-slice repack keeps the collection's log-depth curve identical to the globe's. This fixed the COLUMBUS_VIEW occlusion: **elevated points now render in CV** (h=50 km: GL 486 / GPU 440; h=200 km: GL 486 / GPU 432 — same ~0.9 parity ratio as 3D), where they were 0 before. **3D stays byte-identical** (repack off; stash == currentFrustum at update). All standing gates green (collections-regression, billboard/point/label partial-write, far-camera log-depth, TAA, bloom, pickposition, pickmodel, globe-bindgroup/default-limits, compute-instance, sandcastle-smoke, upstream-regression-check, tsc). **Phase 3 Slice 2b PARTIAL landed (2026-06-13, NEW-COLLECTIONS-2DCV-COPLANAR-DEPTH) — fixes COLUMBUS_VIEW coplanar billboard/point/label; SCENE2D still blocked by a globe-pass issue (root-caused, scoped below).** Three principled, regression-free fixes:

  **(1) Coplanar depth-test disable (billboard + point + label FRs).** In settled 2D/CV (`morphTime === 0 && mode !== SCENE3D`) the three FRs now resolve a `noDepthTest` pipeline variant (`depthCompare: "always"`, no depth write) keyed into their pipeline caches at bit 31 (above every `ShaderDefine` bit), mirroring the `PolylineCollection` reference (Batch 261). Without it a h=0 marker coplanar with the flat map loses the `less-equal` tie and every fragment is discarded. 3D / mid-morph keep `less-equal` (byte-identical). Files: `WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js`, `WebGPUPointPrimitiveRenderer.js`, `WebGPULabelRenderer.js`.

  **(2) `OrthographicOffCenterFrustum` depth-range cache invalidation (root Core fix, backend-neutral).** `Matrix4.computeOrthographicOffCenter` bakes the active `Matrix4._depthRangeType` ([-1,1] WebGL vs [0,1] WebGPU) into the projection, but the frustum's `update()` only recomputed `_orthographicMatrix` when `left/right/top/bottom/near/far` changed — NOT when the global depth-range type flipped. The WebGPU multi-frustum loop flips that type per frame; in single-frustum SCENE2D the near/far/extent are stable, so `update()` skipped the recompute and served a **WebGL-range matrix to a WebGPU pass** → a map-surface marker landed at NDC z ≈ 7.3 (outside [0,1]) and was clipped. Now `update()` also tracks `_depthRangeType`. This is the true root of the earlier "SCENE2D NDC z ≈ 7.3" symptom and benefits any future 2D path. File: `Core/OrthographicOffCenterFrustum.js`.

  **(3) OIT accumulation path honors `bindGroupResolvers` (translucent pass, backend-neutral).** `executeOITCommand` in `WebGPUSceneRendererTranslucentPass.ts` hand-rolled `setBindGroup(bi, cmd.bindGroups[bi])`, ignoring per-index resolvers — so a collection's per-slice repacked camera UB (delivered only via a resolver) was bypassed for the stale FR-update-time bake whenever OIT engaged. Now mirrors `WebGPUDrawCommand.execute()`. (Defensive: collections don't currently auto-create OIT pipelines, but this closes the gap for any future OIT-enabled translucent collection.)

  **Verified probe-first** (`probe-collections-2dcv-morph.mjs`): **COLUMBUS_VIEW billboard 0 → 37px, point 0 → 231px** (now render where they were all-zero); label 128px. **3D byte-identical** (billboard 56 / point 267 / label 125 — unchanged). All standing gates green (collections-regression, billboard/point/label partial-write, far-camera log-depth incl. below-ground occlusion negative control, polyline-cloud-consume, orbital-catalog, globe-bindgroup-cache, pickposition, bloom-parity, compute-instance, sandcastle-smoke, tsc).

  **RESOLVED (Batch 269, NEW-SCENE2D-GLOBE-PASS-OVERWRITE) — SCENE2D coplanar markers now render (billboard 0→37, point 0→250, label 0→139 px).** Root cause was a GLOBE-PASS multi-frustum overwrite, NOT a collection-FR bug (the FRs pack correct in-range NDC z and render 9213 px globe-hidden). **Exact mechanism (confirmed probe-first via `probe-2d-frustum-bins.mjs`):** Batch 167 (NEW-WEBGPU-GLOBE-2D-REGIONAL-ZOOM) fixed a regional-zoom cull bug by dropping the globe command's `boundingVolume` ENTIRELY in non-3D modes — but a command with NO bounding volume forces `View.createPotentiallyVisibleSet` down its worst-case branch (`commandNear = frustum.near (=1 in 2D)`, `commandFar = frustum.far (=500 Mm)`). That collapsed the scene near to 1 and **exploded the 2D multi-frustum split from 1 → 9** (`updateFrustums` 2D: `ceil((far-near)/nearToFarDistance2D)`), binning the no-BV globe into ALL 9 frustums (`insertIntoBin` matches every bin for a no-BV command). The coplanar billboard/point/label (tight bounding volume at projected depth ~12.76 Mm) binned only into the 2 farthest frustums; because **color accumulates across frustums while depth clears per-frustum**, the OPAQUE globe in the nearer frustums (binned there only because of the missing BV) overwrote the far-frustum translucent markers → 0 px. `PolylineCollection` survived because its longer depth extent reached the nearest frustum. WebGL never hit this: it ALWAYS supplies a 2D-projected bounding sphere AND sets `command.cull = false` (`Scene.isVisible` short-circuits on `!cull` BEFORE inspecting the volume), so its 2D split was 1 frustum (near=11.58 Mm). **Fix (`GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js` `addWebGPUDrawCommandsForTile`):** mirror WebGL exactly — in non-3D modes supply the 2D-PROJECTED bounding sphere (`BoundingSphere.fromRectangleWithHeights2D` + the `center.z↔x↔y` axis swap, with a MORPHING union) instead of `undefined`, AND keep `cull = false` so the projected sphere drives the near/far split + binning but is never used to reject a tile (preserves Batch 167's fix). Result: WebGPU 2D split is now **1 frustum, byte-matching WebGL** (near 11581078.05, far 13331078.05, `noBV=0`). **Verified:** `probe-collections-2dcv-morph.mjs` 2D leg — bb 0→37 / pt 0→250 / pl 1764→1790 / lbl 0→139, all 4 rendering; CV unchanged (Batch 263 preserved); 3D byte-identical (the `non3D` branch only fires in 2D/CV/MORPH). Standing gates green: collections-regression, far-camera, globe-bindgroup-cache, logdepth-zfight, buffer-logdepth-zfight, polyline-cloud-consume, pickposition, orbital-catalog, billboard/point-label partial-write, bloom-parity, sandcastle-smoke. Residual billboard/label coverage (ratio ~0.26) is NOT a 2D defect — it's the pre-existing cross-mode NEW-BILLBOARD-SIZE-PARITY gap (identical ratio in 3D and CV). (3) morph blend remains complete (Slice 3, verified separately). **Phase 3 Slice 3 — morph blend: VERIFIED ALREADY COMPLETE (2026-06-13), no code change needed.** Investigation finding: the morph position blend for billboard/point/label is done **CPU-side**, NOT on the GPU — `SceneTransforms.computeActualEllipsoidPosition` (SceneTransforms.js:341-348) lerps the projected (2D/CV) frame and the 3D ECEF frame by `frameState.morphTime` and returns the single blended `_actualPosition`; `PointPrimitive._computeActualPosition` / `Billboard._computeActualPosition` route through it for every non-3D mode incl. MORPHING. The shared `updateMode` runs this BEFORE the WebGPU FR branch (Scene Logic Extractor pattern), all three FRs pack `_actualPosition`, force a full instance rebuild every MORPHING frame (`frameState.mode === SceneMode.MORPHING`), and Slice 2's `repackPerSlice` (TRUE in MORPHING) keeps the projection live. So — unlike the globe and `PolylineCollection` (which DO carry dual position2D/position3D streams and blend in WGSL) — billboard/point/label need NO WGSL dual-stream / `czm_morphTime` path; the WGSL takes the single pre-blended position, matching WebGL's own CPU approach for these collections (`PointPrimitiveCollectionVS.glsl` / `BillboardCollectionVS.glsl` also consume `_actualPosition`, not a GPU morph blend). **Verified probe-first** with the new `Tools/visual-regression/probe-collections-morph-blend.mjs` (drives an ANIMATED `morphTo2D`/`morphToColumbusView`, re-asserts a fixed top-down camera every frame so framing is constant, bins coverage by live `morphTime`, asserts no GPU bin vanishes where WebGL shows the marker): billboard/point/label all track SMOOTHLY through the 2D AND CV transitions with zero device errors, globe ON and OFF — no MORPH-COMPLETION-POP, no mid-morph vanish. (The sibling `probe-collections-2dcv-morph.mjs` could NEVER have caught a morph defect — it only does INSTANT `morph*(0)`, so it never enters MORPHING.) **Two pre-existing, non-morph parity gaps surfaced + isolated during this verification (NOT Slice 3 regressions — both reproduce in steady SCENE3D):** (i) the still-open Slice-2b h=0 coplanar-surface depth-tie above; (ii) **NEW-BILLBOARD-SIZE-PARITY** (see its own entry below). The morph-blend probe deliberately uses a 64px source billboard to stay above the size-gap detection floor so it measures position tracking, not size.
- **NEW-BILLBOARD-SIZE-PARITY — RESOLVED (Batch 275).** WebGPU rendered `BillboardCollection` images (and label glyphs) at ≈½ the linear dimension / ≈¼ the pixel area of WebGL in every scene mode. **Root cause was NOT the size/quad-expansion math** (which is byte-equivalent to WebGL: WGSL `QUAD_OFFSETS ∈ {−0.5,+0.5}` × `size` vs WebGL `halfSize × (direction·2−1)`) — it was the **per-instance atlas sub-rect**. `packBillboardInstance` / `packSDFGlyphInstance` read `bb._imageSubRegion || bb._textureCoordinateBoundsOrImageIndex`, both of which are **undefined** for a normal billboard, so `imageRect` fell back to `(0,0,1,1)` = the WHOLE atlas. The atlas is larger than any single image (a 16px image lands in a 32×32 atlas at width/height = 0.5), so the quad's outer region sampled transparent atlas padding and was discarded by the `color.a < 0.005` test — shrinking the visible billboard to the fraction of the atlas its image actually occupied (≈¼). **Fix:** pull the real normalized atlas rect via `bb.computeTextureCoordinates(scratch)` exactly like WebGL (`BillboardCollection.js:1572`), in both `WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js` and `WebGPULabelRenderer.js`. The full-rebuild trigger already re-packs on `atlasGuid` change, so the rect stays fresh across atlas growth/resize. **Two adjacent fixes landed in the same batch:** (1) **label glyph layout** — the label renderer packed only `bb.pixelOffset`, omitting each glyph's per-character `_translate` (the horizontal advance set by `LabelCollection.repositionAllGlyphs` via `_setTranslate`). WebGL adds `(translate + pixelOffset)` (`BillboardCollectionVS.glsl:84`); without it every glyph stacked at one spot and a 4-letter label rendered ~1 glyph wide. Now packs `pixelOffset + _translate`. (2) **HiDPI parity (DPR > 1)** — `highResMultiplier` (camera UB slot 42) was hardcoded `1.0`; now set to `frameState.pixelRatio` and folded into the WGSL `pixelToClip = (2.0 * highResMultiplier) / viewportSize`, mirroring WebGL's `czm_metersPerPixel` `× czm_pixelRatio`. Was a latent no-op at DPR 1 (the probe environment) but required so billboards/labels don't shrink to 1/pixelRatio on Retina/HiDPI. **Verified probe-first** (`probe-collections-2dcv-morph.mjs`): billboard ratio 0.23 → **1.00 (3D) / 0.99 (2D) / 0.99 (CV)**, label ratio 0.26 → ≈1.2 (now FULL-size — bbox byte-matches WebGL 80×24; residual +20% is SDF anti-alias edge spread, not a size error). Standing gates green: collections-regression, billboard/point-label partial-write, logdepth-zfight, far-camera, pickposition, buffer-point-update, 2dcv-morph, sandcastle-smoke; `tsc --noEmit` clean. **Files:** `WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js`, `WebGPULabelRenderer.js`, `BillboardCollection.wgsl`, `BillboardCollectionSDF.wgsl`, `BillboardCollectionPick.wgsl`. **Residual (separate, P3):** WebGPU label has a small anchor offset vs WebGL (~17px x / ~18px y on the test word) — a label horizontal-origin/baseline nuance, NOT a size defect; the morph probe's loose centering tolerates it.
- ~~**MORPH-TAA-PREVVP**~~ — ✅ SHIPPED (Batch 276). `previousViewProjection` was not guarded across the perspective↔orthographic mode-flip frame; `UniformState.update()` unconditionally clones the prior viewProjection, so at the morph flip the projection regime changes and TAA / motion-vector reprojection reprojected the current depth against a stale/incompatible matrix → ghosting/smear through the transition. **Fix** (`Scene/Scene.js`, in the `scene.taaEnabled` motion-vector block): a history-invalid gate — when `frameState.mode === SceneMode.MORPHING` OR the camera projection type flipped since last frame (tracked via the new `scene._taaPrevProjectionOrtho`, an Ortho-vs-perspective boolean), the gate (a) calls `taa.resetHistory()` so the upcoming `execute()` passes the source through un-reprojected (prev := current for the flip frame) and (b) passes `valid=false` to `updateMotionVectorParams` so the shader skips the reproject. Verified probe-first (`probe-taa-morph-prevvp.mjs`, WebGPU, `scene.taaEnabled=true`): driving `morphTo2D()`→`morphTo3D()` renders clean through the flip (no NaN-garbage saturation wipeout, 0 validation errors), AND the guard demonstrably fires — the TAA motion-vector validity flag goes false during MORPHING (`sawInvalidDuringMorph=true`; the only non-teleport path that sets validity false is this guard). NOTE: the probe must keep the sky enabled — disabling skyBox/skyAtmosphere/sun/moon makes the WebGPU post-process pipeline skip the lazy TAA-effect add (unrelated environment-renderer gate). Subsumes the polyline mid-morph velocity note from MORPH-POLYLINE-COLLECTION-2D's deferred queue (the prev-VP is now invalidated for the whole morph, so the base-color velocity is gated off too).
- ~~**MORPH-MIX-JITTER**~~ — ✅ RESOLVED (Batch 217). `GlobeTerrain.wgsl:1111` now uses the manual lerp `position2DWC.xyz*(1-morphTime) + position3DWC4.xyz*morphTime` instead of GPU `mix()`, mirroring WebGL `czm_columbusViewMorph` to avoid endpoint jitter on NVidia 3070 Ti / Intel Arc A750. Exact at the endpoints by construction; no-op on textbook-`mix` dev hardware (so dev probes prove no-regression only — the jitter is hardware-specific). `csm_columbusViewMorph.wgsl` left in place as scaffolding (Principle 7). Verified: morph renders smooth across morphTime range, 2D/CV/3D parity, 0 errors (probe-morph-midframe.mjs).
- ~~**MORPH-WEBMERCATOR-INSTANCEOF**~~ — ✅ RESOLVED (Batch 217). `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts` now imports `WebMercatorProjection` and uses `projection instanceof WebMercatorProjection` instead of the minification-unsafe `constructor.name === "WebMercatorProjection"`, matching WebGL (GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js:1201). Fix is a no-op in dev/unminified (both detect correctly); it corrects minified release builds where `minifyIdentifiers` renamed the class. Verified: no-regression (default Geographic 2D/CV/morph unchanged, 0 errors); tsc + build clean. NOTE — the minified-build functional repro (a `mapProjection: new WebMercatorProjection()` viewer under `buildRelease`, confirming correct Mercator latitude) was NOT run (requires a custom WebMercator test page + minified build); the fix is verified by code-correctness + exact WebGL parity. A definitive minified probe remains a nice-to-have.
- **MORPH-MODEL-PROJECT2D** — glTF Model accurate-2D (`projectTo2D:true`) has no WGSL equivalent: `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl` has no position2D attribute / `u_modelView2D` / USE_2D path (WebGL: GeometryStageVS.glsl:10-16). NOT a morph defect (models skip MORPHING), but a 2D/CV precision gap. On WebGPU a `projectTo2D:true` model currently falls back to the default `basisTo2D` matrix path (below) — placed correctly, just without the per-vertex accurate-2D reprojection. **Open — P2, opt-in feature.** *Correction (2026-07-02): this entry's original "default `projectTo2D:false` is at parity" claim was stale — the BASE model 2D/CV path was entirely missing on WebGPU (0 model pixels rendered, proven by the pre-change `probe-model-scene-modes.mjs` run) until MODEL-SCENE-MODES below shipped.*
  - **Implementation recipe + landmines (scoped 2026-07-04, B11 `NEW-MODEL-PROJECT2D-BV-MORPH` premise-verify; NOT landed — clean-tree block, task exceeds single-batch verify budget).** The elegant route needs **no WGSL change and no `u_modelView2D` uniform**: reuse the existing `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl` `positionMC` RTE path. When `model._projectTo2D && frameState.mode !== SCENE3D && !frameState.scene3DOnly`: (a) compute per-primitive 2D-projected positions with the SAME math as `SceneMode2DPipelineStage.createPositionsTypedArrayFor2D` — `SceneTransforms.computeActualEllipsoidPosition(frameStateCV, computedModelMatrix·pos)` minus a single **model-level reference point** (`boundingSphere2D.center`), where `computedModelMatrix = sceneGraph.computedModelMatrix × node.computedTransform` bakes the node transform IN; (b) upload as a cached `primCache.positionBuffer2D` and swap it into `vertexBuffers[0]` (WebGPUModelRenderer ~L3990) only in 2D/CV; (c) pack the per-model camera UB with `modelMatrix = Matrix4.fromTranslation(referencePoint)` (NOT `_computedModelMatrix2D`) and **bypass the per-node `nodeModelMatrix` composition (~L3296-3305) for projectTo2D** since node transforms are pre-baked into the positions; (d) command BV = the model-level 2D bounding sphere (fromCornerPoints over projected min/max). Algebra check: `output.position = projection·view·translate(ref)·(pos2D_absolute − ref) = projection·view·pos2D_absolute` — the reference cancels, so a single model-level ref matches WebGL's per-primitive `u_modelView2D = view·translate(bs2D.center)` footprint exactly (verified on paper, not on device). **Landmine 1 — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-07-04 (PREREQ-MODEL-SCENE2D-STAGE-GUARD).** `Model.buildDrawCommands` → `ModelSceneGraph.buildDrawCommands` ran the WebGL `SceneMode2DPipelineStage` UNCONDITIONALLY for projectTo2D models; under WebGPU it (i) allocated a junk WebGL buffer through the `WebGLCompatibilityStub` `_gl` and (ii) set `positionAttribute.typedArray = undefined` (SceneMode2DPipelineStage.js:107) — destroying the source positions the renderer-agnostic geometry path needs. **Fix (backend-agnostic, CLAUDE.md Principle 2 — no `isWebGPU` in scene code):** both `SceneMode2DPipelineStage` and `GeometryPipelineStage` now query the existing `GraphicsContext.requiresVertexTypedArrayRetention` capability (false=WebGL, true=WebGPU — the same getter `GltfLoader`/`EdgeVisibilityPipelineStage` use). When true: `SceneMode2DPipelineStage` still computes + stores `runtimePrimitive.boundingSphere2D` (B11 substrate) then **early-returns** before the `positionBuffer2D` allocation, the typed-array strip, and the `USE_2D_POSITIONS`/`u_modelView2D` shader wiring; `GeometryPipelineStage`'s `use2D` gate drops the paired `a_position2D` attribute so the WebGL draw command built for the model (still constructed under WebGPU via the stub `VertexArray`) does not reference the now-absent 2D buffer (that mismatch threw `DeveloperError: attribute must have a vertexBuffer or a value`, aborting the frame mid-pass and cascading `_beginDefaultRenderPass` errors — caught probe-first). **Verified** (`probe-model-scene2d-stage-guard.mjs`, runtime scene-graph introspection + PNG read): WebGPU SCENE2D `projectTo2D:true` retains all 5 POSITION typedArrays, allocates 0 stub `positionBuffer2D`, 0 render/device errors; WebGPU SCENE3D unchanged (truck renders, stage never runs in 3D); WebGL SCENE2D byte-identical (typedArrays stripped 0/5, 5 stub buffers, truck renders top-down). Base-model `probe-model-scene-modes.mjs` (projectTo2D:false) GATE PASS unregressed. **Remaining for B11:** the WebGPU-side accurate-2D position buffer + `vertexBuffers[0]` swap + camera-UB ref-point pack (recipe below) is now unblocked — the source typedArrays are intact. **Landmine 2:** the camera UB is packed once per-model (WebGPUModelRenderer ~L3093), but the per-node matrix path re-derives `nodeModelMatrix` in the node loop; the single-ref approach only works if that per-node composition is bypassed for projectTo2D (positions carry the node transform). **Landmine 3:** acceptance is entangled with `NEW-MODEL-SCENE2D-SHADING` (B3, §4.3 — still OPEN): interior shading is olive-vs-blue in SCENE2D regardless of position accuracy, so a color-diff footprint gate will read the shading residual unless the probe measures silhouette/coverage only. **Dep spine confirms this is a coupled arc:** the 2026-07-03 campaign engine skipped the entire B3→B11→B12 model-2D chain rather than land it piecemeal. Probe to author: `Tools/visual-regression/probe-model-project2d.mjs` extending `probe-model-scene-modes.mjs` (milk-truck, globe hidden, `projectTo2D:true`, SCENE2D) asserting silhouette-mask + centroid vs WebGL; off-gate `projectTo2D:false` byte-identical + 3D untouched.
- ~~**MODEL-SCENE-MODES**~~ — ✅ SHIPPED (2026-07-02). glTF models now render in SCENE2D / COLUMBUS_VIEW (and through MORPHING, same `mode !== SCENE3D` condition WebGL uses) on WebGPU. **Fix** (`WebGPUModelRenderer.js`, `updateWebGPUModel`): (1) the single per-frame `modelMatrix` local switches to `model._sceneGraph._computedModelMatrix2D` when `frameState.mode !== SceneMode.SCENE3D` — the exact `Transforms.basisTo2D` product WebGL's `ModelMatrixUpdateStage.update` consumes; Scene-side `Model.js` (`updateSceneMode` → `updateSceneGraph` → `ModelSceneGraph.updateModelMatrix` → `computeModelMatrix2D`) already recomputes it before the FR runs on every mode flip, so no renderer-side invalidation is needed. Every downstream consumer (RTE `packCameraUniforms` — `uniformState.view/projection/cameraPosition` are already projected-frame in these modes, keeping the RTE encode consistent — per-node `computedTransform` composition, shadow-cast UB, edge-emitter MVP, TAA `prevModelMatrix`) derives from that one local. WGSL untouched. (2) Emitted commands carry `_boundingSphere2D` instead of `model.boundingSphere` in non-3D modes — Scene's `createPotentiallyVisibleSet` culls by the command BV against the projected-frame culling volume, so the ECEF sphere had the model culled outright (THE pre-change "renders nothing" mechanism). **Verified probe-first** (`probe-model-scene-modes.mjs`, milk truck, globe hidden): pre-change WebGPU = 0 model pixels in 2D and CV; post-change silhouette-mask mismatch 0.39% (2D) / 0.58% (CV), centroid delta 0.1 px vs WebGL, 0 device errors. 3D off-gate: mode-gated (both picks short-circuit to the pre-change expressions by reference in SCENE3D); 3D leg at its pre-existing baseline (mask 0.09%) and `probe-model-color.mjs` standing gate green. The interior channel diff (13–21/255, warm-vs-cool WebGPU +R/−B) is the pre-existing cross-mode backend shading residual, brightness-scaled — measured with the same signature on the 3D leg; NOT scene-mode-related. **Deferred residuals** (matching WebGL's opt-in/edge surface): `projectTo2D:true` accurate-2D (MORPH-MODEL-PROJECT2D above, incl. its 2D animation-freeze semantics), per-primitive 2D BVs (WebGPU uses the conservative model-level `_boundingSphere2D`). **~~SCENE2D IDL-crossing duplicate command~~ — ✅ SHIPPED (C-MODEL-2DIDL-DUPLICATE-RELAND, 2026-07-04).** Byte-for-byte port of WebGL `ModelDrawCommand.shouldUse2DCommands` + `updateModelMatrix2D` + `derive2DCommand` into `WebGPUModelRenderer.js`: `idlDuplicateActive` arms ONLY in SCENE2D for a non-`projectTo2D` model whose model-level `_boundingSphere2D` straddles ±πR; when armed, the emission loop pushes a second copy of each surface command whose @group(0) camera UB is packed from a y-shifted matrix (`ty −= sign(ty)·2πR`) with a matching y-shifted bounding volume, reusing the primary's `pipelineCache.cameraBGL`. All IDL GPU resources (shifted camera buffer/data/bind-group, persisted shifted matrix + sphere) are lazy-allocated strictly inside the `if (idlDuplicateActive)` gate, so 3D / CV / projectTo2D / non-crossing 2D emit a byte-identical command stream. **Verified probe-first** (`probe-model-scene2d-idl.mjs`, canvas-framebuffer read, whole-map 2D view, milk-truck scale 4e5 on the antimeridian): pre-change WebGPU rendered only the on-map (right) edge (L=0, R=360 px); post-change renders BOTH edges (L=324, R=360), matching WebGL (L=345, R=360). Off-gate (lon 0, non-crossing) framebuffer delta 0.12% / max-channel-Δ 12 == the same-build render-jitter floor (0.10% / Δ3). **Honest-partial:** this renders the crossing half that was fully absent; end-to-end seam parity (exact primary-viewport cull + per-primitive 2D BVs so the two halves meet seamlessly) is completed by the separate `C-MODEL-2DSPLIT-PRIMARY-CULL` task. **~~C-MODEL-2DSPLIT-PRIMARY-CULL~~ — ✅ CLOSED / PREMISE STALE (2026-07-04).** The premise (WebGPU's `execute2DViewportCommands` split *drops* the PRIMARY unshifted half, leaving only ~48%) does NOT hold against live code: `execute2DViewportCommands` lives in `Scene/ViewportExecutor.js` and is **backend-agnostic** — it calls `executeCommandsInViewport` twice (once per viewport half) identically for WebGL and WebGPU, so neither half is dropped at Scene level (the per-half WebGPU FB accumulation is the already-fixed BUG-3 `_exec2DSceneFbLoad`/`_exec2DDeferComposite` load/defer path). With the Batch 557 duplicate command supplying the wrapped half, `probe-model-scene2d-idl.mjs` measures WebGPU crossing coverage L=324/R=360 vs WebGL L=343/R=360 (ratio **0.97**, both halves present) — not 0.48. The residual ~19 px left-edge deficit is the model-level conservative 2D bounding-sphere (vs WebGL's per-primitive 2D BVs), tracked under the MODEL-SCENE-MODES "Deferred residuals: per-primitive 2D BVs" line above, NOT a Scene-viewport-split drop. Regression guard: added the `primaryCullParity` gate (crossing ratio ≥ 0.9) to `probe-model-scene2d-idl.mjs`. No code change to the Scene split.

#### Morph review gaps — surfaced by the audit's completeness critic, NOT code-verified (confirm before relying)

These are areas the webgpu-morph-review audit did NOT examine — flagged as likely-relevant by the completeness critic but not yet reproduced or code-confirmed. Lower confidence than the entries above; each needs its own investigation/probe.

- **MORPH-PICK** — Pick during a morph is exercised BY THE TRANSITIONER ITSELF: `SceneTransitioner` calls `globe.pickWorldCoordinates` mid-morph (SceneTransitioner.js ~645/775) to compute the 2D endpoint. If the WebGPU pick pass's camera UB doesn't carry the live `frameState.mode`/`morphTime`, the depth written for picking won't match the displayed geometry → `pickPosition` returns wrong coordinates → the transitioner computes a WRONG final 2D camera view, cascading into a visibly wrong end state. **Unverified — check whether the pick command-build path reuses `createCameraUniformBuffer` with the live mode/morphTime.**
- **MORPH-COMPLETION-POP** — At completion the `morphTime` tween (QUARTIC_OUT) can reach exactly 1.0/0.0 a frame or more BEFORE `_mode` flips (the tween and the mode-flip are sequenced via tween chaining, not atomically). The MORPHING branch then runs with an endpoint morphTime — fine only if that branch at the endpoint is byte-identical to the destination (SCENE3D/CV/2D) branch. After the Batch-216 matrix fix the morph branch should converge, but a one-frame "pop" at completion (present in WebGL? in WebGPU only?) was never checked. **Unverified — instrument `frameState.morphTime`+`mode` across the completion frames and diff the (MORPHING, mt=1) frame vs the first (SCENE3D) frame.**

The WebGPU multi-frustum split (`frustumCommandsList`) + HiZ pyramid consume `camera.frustum`; if any near/far split or HiZ extent is cached across frames it could thrash mid-morph. **Unverified — confirm near/far + HiZ are recomputed every morph frame, not cached.**
- **MORPH-MULTIVIEW** — Split-screen / multi-context morph (CLAUDE.md Principle 3): `scene._mode`/`morphTime` are single scalars shared by all views/contexts on a Scene. The audit verified neither that WebGL + WebGPU stay frame-locked through the animation on the split-screen page, nor that two simultaneous WebGPU contexts each flip mode correctly. **Unverified — run the split-screen page through a non-zero-duration morph and diff per-frame (this is also the natural home for extending probe-morph-midframe.mjs to multi-view).**

### ⚠️ Billboard / Point / Label collections render NOTHING on WebGPU (Batch 2 audit, 2026-06-07) — RESOLVED in 3D for all three (Batches 218–219); bug 2 (far-surface depth) + 2D/CV-mode collections remain

> **Deep-dive resolution (2026-06-07, Batches 218–219):** the no-render is a CHAIN of independent bugs. In **SCENE3D**, billboards, points, and labels now render with WebGL parity (verified close-camera, PNG-read via `probe-collections-closeup.mjs`). Two cross-cutting gaps remain — bug 2 (far-surface depth) and full 2D/COLUMBUS_VIEW collection rendering.
> - **Bug 1 (FIXED — billboard 218, point/label 219) — bounding volume never computed on WebGPU → frustum-culled.** `BillboardCollection.update` computed `_boundingVolume` only in the WebGL path (after the `fr` early-return), so the WebGPU draw command carried the default degenerate sphere (center 0,0,0, radius 0 = Earth's centre) and `View.createPotentiallyVisibleSet` culled it (`scene.isVisible` → OUTSIDE). Fix: `computeBoundingVolumeForFeatureRenderer` runs in the `if (fr)` block — reproduces the `_max*`/`_all*` aggregates the WebGL vertex writers compute, transforms `_baseVolume`→WC, and calls `updateBoundingVolume`. Verified: a 100 km-altitude billboard now renders (992 magenta px, was 0). (`packages/engine/Source/Scene/BillboardCollection.js`.) **Point (Batch 219):** the identical fix in `PointPrimitiveCollection.js` (`computeBoundingVolumeForFeatureRenderer` + call in the `if (fr)` block). **Label (Batch 219):** see the glyph-atlas note below — the BV cull was only HALF the label failure.
> - **Bug 3 (FIXED IN PART at 218/219 — the COLOUR shaders only; the PICK shaders and the clip guard closed 2026-09-05, AR-001/MAB-7) — `disableDepthTestDistance` rendered BEHIND, not on top.** The `//>>ifdef DISABLE_DEPTH_DISTANCE` block set `clipPos.z = clipPos.w` (NDC z=1 = the FAR plane), which under `less-equal` fails against the closer globe. WebGPU clip-z is [0,1] (near→far), so "always on top" is the NEAR plane (0), not far. Fix: `clipPos.z = 0.0` — `BillboardCollection.wgsl` (218, 3 sites), `PointPrimitiveColor.wgsl` (219, 3 sites), `BillboardCollectionSDF.wgsl` (219, 3 sites — labels). Verified for billboards: a surface billboard with `disableDepthTestDistance = Infinity` now renders (992, was 0).
>   - **CORRECTION (2026-09-05, AR-001 / `MAB-9` / `MAB-7`, lane Uldor).** This entry read FIXED while the fix
>     had reached three of the five shaders in its own scope. `BillboardCollectionPick.wgsl` (:236/:240/:247) and
>     `PointPrimitivePick.wgsl` (:189/:193/:200) still wrote `clipPos.z = clipPos.w` — the FAR plane — behind a
>     comment asserting the colour/pick split was deliberate ("the pick pass uses z = w to pass its far-cleared
>     depth target without overriding nearer pick geometry"). That rationale is REFUTED: WebGL has no such split
>     to mirror, because ONE vertex shader (`BillboardCollectionVS.glsl`) serves both passes and `Scene`'s pick
>     derivation replaces only the fragment stage, so WebGL pick fragments carry `gl_Position.z = -gl_Position.w`
>     — its near plane — exactly as its colour fragments do. And the WebGPU pick pass rasterizes globe terrain
>     into the same depth target (`WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:1988-1991`), so a far-plane pick fragment loses
>     `less-equal` against terrain: the primitive was invisible to `pickAsync` at precisely the distances the
>     property exists to cover. Both now write `clipPos.z = 0.0`.
>   - **Second half of the same correction: the clip guard.** None of the five carried WebGL's
>     `BillboardCollectionVS.glsl:340-344` guard (`zclip = z/w; clipped = (zclip < -1.0 || zclip > 1.0);` and the
>     override only fires when `!clipped`). The override is a WRITE, not a test, so `clipPos.z = 0.0` PULLED a
>     vertex whose z was outside `[0, w]` back INSIDE the clip volume and the API then drew a fragment WebGL
>     leaves clipped. Measured on the standing spec's grid with the guard made inert: **32 diverging samples,
>     all at positive `w`** — 16 nearer than the near plane, 16 past the far plane. **None at `w <= 0`** — such
>     a vertex is clipped by the API on both backends whatever z is written, so the guard's `w` test is not the
>     defect but the faithful port of upstream's, which exists because `z / w` is not a valid comparison at
>     non-positive `w`. All five now compute `select(-1.0, clipPos.z / clipPos.w, clipPos.w > 0.0)` and override
>     only inside `[0, 1]`. The block sits under `//>>ifdef DISABLE_DEPTH_DISTANCE`, so a scene that does not use
>     the property never compiles it and its captures are unchanged by construction.
>   - **Scope held for `AR-D09`.** The six POLYLINE shaders keep `z = w` at 18 sites, deliberately. Their whole
>     `DISABLE_DEPTH_DISTANCE` block is fork-added: `czm_minimumDisableDepthTestDistance` has exactly two GLSL
>     consumers (`BillboardCollectionVS.glsl`, `PointPrimitiveCollectionVS.glsl`) and `PolylineVS.glsl` is not
>     one of them, so there is no WebGL law for a polyline to be made to match, and `AR-D09` decided whether
>     `Polyline.disableDepthTestDistance` — and with it the block — survives at all (decided 2026-09-05: implement on WebGL — `AR-896`). Sites, all held as one
>     unit: `PolylineCollection.wgsl:197/201/208`, `PolylineCollectionPick.wgsl:184/188/195`,
>     `PolylineArrow.wgsl:181/185/192`, `PolylineDash.wgsl:178/182/189`, `PolylineGlow.wgsl:175/179/186`,
>     `PolylineOutline.wgsl:173/177/184`.
>   - **Standing guard:** `Tools/visual-regression/collection-depth-override-law.spec.mjs`
>     (`npm run test-visual-probe-contracts`) executes the real WGSL and GLSL blocks over a 252-sample
>     clip-space grid and requires one fragment outcome from both backends, with an inertness mutant per shader.
> - **Bug 4 / LABEL-SPECIFIC (FIXED — Batch 219) — glyph atlas never uploaded + glyph BV degenerate.** Labels were 0 even at close camera in 3D *after* bugs 1+3. Root cause: `LabelCollection.update()` delegates glyph rendering to the dedicated `WebGPULabelRenderer` (SDF) and **returns before calling `glyphBillboardCollection.update()`** — so the billboard shared-scene-logic prologue (texture-atlas GPU upload schedule + `_baseVolume`/`_boundingVolume` computation) never ran for the glyph collection. Result: the SDF pass sampled the 1×1 placeholder atlas (→ discard every fragment) AND the glyph draw command carried the radius-0 BV (→ frustum-culled). Fix: extracted the shared prologue into `runSharedSceneLogic()` + a public `BillboardCollection.prepareForFeatureRenderer(frameState)` (prologue + `computeBoundingVolumeForFeatureRenderer`, no draw emission); `LabelCollection.update()` now calls it on the glyph + background collections before `labelFR.update()`. Verified: label "X" renders at close camera in 3D (251 lime px, was 0). (`BillboardCollection.js`, `LabelCollection.js`.)
> - **Bug 2 + Bug 5 (OPEN — UNIFIED ROOT CAUSE, diagnosed Batch 220) — the collection camera UB is packed ONCE per frame with ONE frustum's projection, but the scene renders in MULTIPLE depth frustums.** This single root cause explains BOTH the far-camera-3D failure (was mislabeled "bug 2 = log-depth") AND the total 2D/CV no-render ("bug 5").
>   - **Evidence (`probe-billboard-2d-debug.mjs`, SCENE2D):** the billboard command is NOT culled (`bvVisibility=1`, in command list) and `_actualPosition` IS correctly projected (0, −8.35 Mm, 4.45 Mm). But the manually-computed `clip.z = 7.289` (WebGPU clip range is [0,1] → DEPTH-CLIPPED). The scene has **`numFrustums = 9`**; the billboard's eye-space depth is **−12,756,274**; the camera UB was packed with **frustum 0** (`near=1, far=1,750,001`). `12.75M / 1.75M ≈ 7.28` = exactly the measured clip.z. So in the frustum the billboard actually belongs to (frustum 8: near 12.76M / far 14.51M), it is rendered with frustum-0's projection → clipped.
>   - **Why close-camera 3D works but far-camera 3D / 2D don't:** at a close camera the scene has few frustums and the marker sits in frustum 0 (whose projection the UB happens to hold) → renders. At far range, or in 2D (always 9 frustums), the marker lands in a far frustum but the UB still carries an early frustum's near/far → depth-clipped AND its depth no longer matches the globe's per-frustum depth → also fails the depth test (this is the "occluded by globe / renders only with globe.show=false" symptom previously attributed to log-depth).
>   - **How the globe avoids it (the reference):** `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.createCameraUniformBuffer` is called PER TILE DURING the render pass, so it picks up the CURRENT frustum's `uniformState.projection` (which the multifrustum executor updates before each frustum). The collection renderers pack their camera UB once in the FR `update()` (before multifrustum execution) → stale projection for every frustum but one.
>   - **Execution-path mechanism (investigated Batch 220):** the WebGPU multifrustum executor (`WebGPUSceneRendererFrustumLoop.executeFrustumLoop`) calls `host._updateFrustumUniforms(uniformState, near, far)` → `uniformState.updateFrustum` per slice (publishing the slice's projection) and publishes `uniformState._currentSliceIndex = i`. `WebGPUDrawCommand.execute` already runs `bindGroupResolvers[i]()` per draw — the established per-slice pattern (`WebGPUGroundPrimitiveRenderer`, Batch 173 `NEW-GROUNDPRIM-CLASSIFIER-PER-FRUSTUM-UBO`). Per-slice GPU buffers MUST be distinct (`device.queue.writeBuffer` is unordered vs the encoder, last-wins).
>   - **Batch 220 attempt (REVERTED) — per-frustum UB resolver is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT.** Implemented a `bindGroupResolvers[0]` on the billboard color/velocity commands that re-packs the camera UB per slice into distinct per-slice buffers, plus the 2D/CV camera-frame fix (`inverse(view).translation`). The resolver FIRES correctly (`probe-billboard-2d-debug.mjs` confirmed 225+ calls, per-slice indices, per-slice `currentFrustum`), but billboards STILL render nothing in 2D/CV AND far-3D. So the single-projection theory was incomplete. Two ADDITIONAL, independent blockers surfaced:
>     1. **far-3D = depth-test OCCLUSION, not clipping.** With the resolver, the far-3D billboard's clip.z is in [0,1] (slice projection correct) yet it's still 0 px — it's occluded by the globe in the depth buffer. The billboard writes a depth that doesn't match the globe's depth at the same surface point in that slice. This is the genuine depth-matching issue (the globe's depth encoding per slice vs the billboard's). `disableDepthTestDistance` sidesteps it by forcing clip.z=0.
>     2. **2D = the C-R8-SCENE2D-JITTER camera-Z shift.** In SCENE2D the frustum loop SHIFTS `scene2DCamera.position.z` per slice and compresses each band to `[1, far−near+1]` (`WebGPUSceneRendererFrustumLoop.ts:211-230`) so the ortho depth keeps precision. Globe tiles ride this because their per-tile UB is rebuilt against the shifted camera. The collection instance positions (projected Columbus coords) + a resolver that reads `uniformState.view` must be reconciled with this per-slice camera shift; the current resolver re-pack doesn't reproduce the globe's planar-RTC handling, so the billboard's clip position is wrong in the shifted band.
>   - **Revised plan:** (a) far-3D needs the marker depth to match the globe's per-slice depth (mirror the globe's depth write/encode for the collection pipelines, OR accept `disableDepthTestDistance` as the supported path and document it); (b) 2D/CV needs the resolver to reproduce the globe's planar per-slice camera handling (the projected-RTC + shifted-camera math in `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.computeModifiedModelView`), not just swap the projection. This is multi-part and larger than one batch. Reverted the WIP to keep `main` clean (low-risk per user direction); the resolver design above is the resume point.
>   - **Supersedes:** the earlier "bug 2 = linear-vs-log depth, needs WebGPU log-depth" hypothesis (Batch 218) is PARTLY rehabilitated — far-3D IS a depth-match problem, but the per-frustum projection is ALSO required. `probe-billboard-2d-debug.mjs` (PROBE_MODE=2d|3d) is the reproducer/instrument.
> - **Minor (OPEN — 3D billboard/label screen-size) — markers render ~30% smaller on WebGPU.** Close-camera ratios: billboard GL 576 / GPU 289 (0.50 area ≈ 0.71 linear), label GL 369 / GPU 251 (0.68); point matches well (0.89). Likely a `highResMultiplier` / device-pixel-ratio mismatch in the instance-quad screen-space sizing. Cosmetic vs the no-render P0; refine after 2D/CV.

- **WEBGPU-BILLBOARD-POINT-LABEL-NO-RENDER** — `BillboardCollection`, `PointPrimitiveCollection`, and `LabelCollection` produce **no visible output** on the WebGPU CesiumViewer, in **every** scene mode (SCENE3D, SCENE2D, COLUMBUS_VIEW). WebGL renders them correctly. This was surfaced while doing the morph "billboard/point/label 2D-CV audit" (MORPH-COLLECTIONS-AUDIT / PLAN_2DCV_MORPH_BATCHES Batch 2) — the audit expected a 2D/CV-only gap but found the collections don't render even in 3D.
  - **Severity: P0/P1.** Billboards/points/labels are among the most-used primitives (every pin, marker, city label, Entity with billboard/point/label graphics). They are broken in all modes on WebGPU.
  - **Evidence (5 probe variations + read PNGs + git bisect):** `probe-collections-2dcv-morph.mjs` (raw primitive collections) and `probe-collections-entity.mjs` (Entity API) both show billboard/point/label = 0 colored px on WebGPU vs hundreds on WebGL, in 3D/2D/CV. PNGs read directly (Principle 8) — the markers are simply absent. Reproduces at close camera (~4 km) AND far (1.2 Mm); with the default render loop only (no manual render); and with `disableDepthTestDistance = Infinity` (so it is NOT depth occlusion). A `PolylineCollection` placed in the same scene DOES render on WebGPU (opaque pass works), so the WebGPU scene pipeline is partially functional.
  - **Not a regression from this session:** bisected — billboard=0/point=0 at Batch 214 (`0e51182139`, before the Batch-215 BUG-3 scene-FB changes). Long-standing; never caught because the visual-regression suite has ~zero billboard/label/point coverage (only `high-density-5k-spheres`).
  - **Renderers exist + the feature renderer IS invoked:** `WebGPUBillboardRenderer.js` / `WebGPULabelRenderer.js` / `WebGPUPointPrimitiveRenderer.js` exist and are reached — `BillboardCollection.update` finds `context.getFeatureRenderer(BILLBOARD_COLLECTION)` and calls `fr.update(...)` with no fallback error (BillboardCollection.js:731-738). So commands are generated but draw nothing visible. Root-cause hypothesis (NOT yet confirmed): the WebGPU billboard/point/label draw produces no/degenerate output — candidates to investigate: the screen-space vertex/instance generation, the texture-atlas binding (billboard/label), the translucent-pass execution of these commands, or the pipeline state. The polyline working rules out a global scene-FB/compositing failure.
  - **Docs were optimistic:** FEATURE_INVENTORY tagged these `(SHIPPED)` — that reflected code existing + passing a device-error check (e.g. probe-collections-msaa.mjs asserts 0 device errors, never visual presence), NOT visual verification. Tags corrected to flag the no-render state.
  - **Reprioritization:** this likely outranks the planned PLAN_2DCV_MORPH_BATCHES Batch 3 (PolylineCollection 2D/CV port) — billboards/points/labels are more ubiquitous and broken in ALL modes (including 3D), not just 2D/CV. **Open — needs a dedicated renderer-level investigation + fix; reproducers: probe-collections-2dcv-morph.mjs, probe-collections-entity.mjs.**
  - **UPDATE (2026-06-07, Batches 218–219) — SCENE3D RESOLVED for all three.** The 3D no-render was the bug-1 (degenerate BV) + bug-3 (inverted clip-z) + bug-4 (label glyph-atlas/BV) chain documented in the resolution block above. Billboards (218), points + labels (219) now render in 3D at close camera with WebGL parity (verified via `probe-collections-closeup.mjs`, PNG-read). **Still open: bug 2 (far-surface depth, all three) and bug 5 (SCENE2D / COLUMBUS_VIEW render nothing — the next concrete step, tracked under MORPH-COLLECTIONS-AUDIT).**

## NEW-WEBGPU-SKYBOX-HDR-FAINT-STAR-PARITY — ✅ RESOLVED Batch 364 (always-on auto-exposure crushed the HDR night sky)

**ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED (Batch 364, 2026-06-23).** The corrected hypothesis below ("shared HDR post-process path") was right; the specific lever is **auto-exposure**. WebGL only runs the auto-exposure luminance reduction when the user opts in (`PostProcessStageCollection._autoExposureEnabled`, default `false`). WebGPU calls `addAutoExposure` UNCONDITIONALLY (`WebGPUSceneRendererEnsureResources.ts`, AUDIT B.14 "always-on"), `WebGPUAutoExposure.enabled` defaults `true`, and `configureWebGPUPostProcessPipeline` never synced the flag down — so WebGPU auto-exposed EVERY frame. On a near-black HDR night sky the adaptive exposure collapsed the whole frame to **pure black**. **Decisive diagnostic** (`diag-stars-hdr-autoexposure.mjs`, runtime toggle, no rebuild): AE-on → bright=0/maxLum=**0** (black); AE-off → bright=235/maxLum=761/**5 saturated** bloom-feeding star points. **Fix:** `configureWebGPUPostProcessPipeline` now sets `pipeline.autoExposureEnabled = collection._autoExposureEnabled === true` — the SAME opt-in flag WebGL honors, so both backends expose identically by default. The always-on B.14 behavior was itself a WebGL divergence (WebGL never auto-exposes by default, even for the SDR moonlight day/night case B.14 cited) and is dropped in favor of parity; users who set `autoExposure = true` still get the adaptive path on both. **Verified** (`probe-stars-hdr-autoexposure-parity.mjs`, NEW): WebGPU HDR sky bright=231/maxLum=756/4-saturated vs WebGL 282/717/0 (was 0/0/0) — near-parity, PNGs READ. **Didn't-break (shared HDR infra):** `probe-disc-size-orbit` identical to baseline (atmosphere disc 1.01%/0.01%), `probe-bloom-parity` PASS with WebGPU globe pixel `rgb(31,38,51)` == WebGL byte-for-byte + bloom ratio 1.01x; SDR night-sky control unchanged (AE is a no-op in SDR). **Residual:** WebGL catalog star sprites are still marginally more prominent (≈82% bright-px parity) — that is the separate `NEW-WEBGPU-STARFIELD-TUNE` item, NOT this bug. **Files:** `WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts`. **The `WebGPUCubeMapPanoramaRenderer.js:140` HDR-decode TODO remains a separate, smaller item** (sRGB→linear under HDR to match `SkyBoxFS`'s `czm_gammaCorrect`) — it darkens faint pixels and is NOT this brightness lever.

<details><summary>Original investigation (pre-Batch-364, root cause now identified above)</summary>

### NEW-WEBGPU-SKYBOX-HDR-FAINT-STAR-PARITY — baked starfield dimmer than WebGL under HDR (2026-06-22)

**Surfaced** verifying the Batch-350 star follow-up (`probe-stars-hdr-verify.mjs`). With `scene.highDynamicRange = true` + bloom, the WebGPU baked SkyBox shows NOTICEABLY FEWER faint background stars than WebGL (WebGL has a richer dusting; WebGPU is sparse). In the DEFAULT SDR config the two are byte-identical (the cubemap path is a no-op there), so this is HDR-only and does NOT affect the default viewer.

**Status:** the bright-star catalog tune (`StarField.js` / `StarFieldMath.ts`, Batch 352) is the user-facing fix and is correct in SDR. An attempted fix — gating a `pow(2.2)` sRGB→linear cubemap decode on HDR in `WebGPUCubeMapPanoramaRenderer.js` (mirroring WebGL `SkyBoxFS` `czm_gammaCorrect`, resolving the in-file TODO at line ~140) — was **reverted UNVERIFIED**: the decode darkens faint pixels and did NOT close the WebGPU-vs-WebGL gap, so the residual is a SEPARATE tonemap/bloom parity difference, not the missing cubemap decode. The workflow agent's "~85× too dim" framing is suspect (sRGB→linear decode lowers, not raises, faint values).

**Next concrete step:** capture WebGPU HDR cubemap WITH vs WITHOUT the decode (clean before/after) to confirm direction, then compare the WebGPU bloom + tonemap (`Tonemapping.wgsl`) faint-star response against WebGL's at matched cubemap luminance. Reproducer: `probe-stars-hdr-verify.mjs` (HDR + SDR captures, both backends).

**CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE (2026-06-22, re-investigation — the cubemap-decode hypothesis above is WRONG).** Re-ran `probe-stars-hdr-verify.mjs` and READ the HDR PNGs (`output/stars-hdr-{webgpu,webgl}.png`). The gap is NOT specific to the baked cubemap dusting — the **ENTIRE WebGPU HDR night sky is dramatically under-bright vs WebGL**, including the **bright StarField catalog points, which render with soft bloom halos on WebGL but as tight dim points with NO halo on WebGPU**. The catalog points are a SEPARATE renderer (`WebGPUStarFieldRenderer`) that never touches the cubemap decode, so their dimness proves the residual lives in the **shared WebGPU HDR post-process path (tonemap / auto-exposure / bloom)**, not in `WebGPUCubeMapPanoramaRenderer`. SDR control is unchanged (WebGPU SDR ≈ WebGL SDR — cubemap path is a no-op there), so this is HDR-only and does NOT affect the default viewer. **Suspects to pin next (in `WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts` + `WebGPUAutoExposure.ts` + `BloomEffect`):** (1) default `TonemapMode` / exposure vs WebGL's default `Scene` tonemapper under HDR — a harder operator (e.g. ACES hard-clamp) would crush the faint sky; (2) WebGPU auto-exposure on a near-black night frame may drive exposure very differently than WebGL; (3) bloom threshold/composite not additively lifting the star points (the missing halos). **The fix touches SHARED HDR infrastructure used by every HDR scene (models, globe, tiles), so it needs broad HDR regression coverage (model-PBR + globe under HDR), not just the star probe — scope it as its own batch, not a star-renderer tweak.** The `WebGPUCubeMapPanoramaRenderer.js:140` HDR-decode TODO is a SEPARATE, smaller correctness item (the cubemap SHOULD sRGB→linear decode under HDR to match `SkyBoxFS`'s `czm_gammaCorrect`) but it DARKENS faint pixels, so it is NOT the lever that closes this brightness gap — leave the TODO but do not expect it to fix the dusting.

</details>

## BUG-WEBGPU-SKY-GROUNDVIEW-HIGH-ELEVATION-BLACK — ✅ RESOLVED (commit b3a55ebae7) — it was the SKYBOX over the atmosphere, NOT shell coverage (2026-06-25)

**RESOLVED.** The dark daytime sky was the skyBox cubemap + starField being composited OVER the atmosphere (injected commands APPEND after the binned SkyAtmosphere) and erasing it — NOT the sky-shell coverage theory below (that was a phantom; the shell renders the full sky). Fix: `SceneRenderer.js` ~L370 PREPENDS skyBox+starField ahead of the binned atmosphere. Full WebGL parity day/night, static/dynamic. Depth answer: neither writes depth (background layers occluded by globe via depth-test; atmosphere depthWrite would erase the sun/moon drawn after it). Full writeup in [WEBGPU_DEBUGGING_LOG.md](WEBGPU_DEBUGGING_LOG.md). Also shipped the fullscreen-sky option. The original (incorrect) report is kept below for the trail.

### (Original — INCORRECT shell-coverage theory, superseded)

**Surfaced** confirming the Weather Inspector demo's grey sky. At a 650 m ground camera with `skyAtmosphere.show=true`, the WebGPU sky renders a thin BLUE band at the horizon and PURE BLACK above it; WebGL is blue across the whole sky (upper-center sky RGB WebGPU `(1,1,1)` vs WebGL `(75,123,176)`; identical with `showProceduralClouds` on/off → NOT the clouds). This is the dominant visible weather/atmosphere gap on WebGPU at ground level and likely the same residual that shows as red in the atmosphere/sky band of the `capture-and-diff` globe-horizon diff PNGs.

**Diagnosed but NOT fixed** (≈15 build/probe cycles, all reverted to a clean baseline — full trace in [WEBGPU_DEBUGGING_LOG.md](WEBGPU_DEBUGGING_LOG.md) "INVESTIGATION (DEFERRED) — WebGPU sky-atmosphere renders BLACK…"). **Ruled out:** clouds; near/far z-clip (far-plane pin `clip-z=clip-w`); face culling (`cullMode:none`); fragment discards (earliest-line magenta still black); FOV/projection/multi-frustum — ground-level diag shows it is **single-frustum** (`currentFrustum=0,1e10`) with a **correct ~47° vFOV perspective** (`off.near=0.1`, `proj0=1.7321`, `proj5=2.3094`). The earlier "far multi-frustum band clips the overhead shell" theory was WRONG. **Smoking gun:** earliest-possible magenta is still black above the horizon band → **no shell triangle rasterizes to the upper-sky pixels despite a geometrically-correct projection.** The shell mesh is a full earth-centered ellipsoid (`generateAtmosphereGeometry`, radii×1.025 ≈160 km) and the camera is well inside it, yet the overhead inner surface doesn't project there. **Untested hypotheses (need GPU inspection):** RTE precision on the overhead verts; scissor/viewport; geometry winding vs this view; a separate clip plane. **Broader clue:** the WebGPU globe limb looks curved/orbital at 650 m while WebGL is flat-ground — may not be sky-specific.

**Next step:** RenderDoc / GPU frame capture to inspect the transformed shell vertex positions (build-and-probe can't see why correct geometry doesn't rasterize). **Files:** `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSkyAtmosphereRenderer.js` (geometry + `packUniforms`), `Shaders/WebGPU/Environment/SkyAtmosphere.wgsl` (vertex/fragment). **Probe:** `probe-confirm-inspector-sky.mjs` (extend to sample multiple elevations — the `probe-ground-view-env` gate samples only the horizon band and is blind to this). **Secondary parity nits** (real but NOT the black-sky cause): `WebGPUSkyAtmosphereRenderer.js:71` rayleigh blue `22.4e-6`→`28.4e-6`; `:73-74` scale heights `8500/1200`→`10000/3200`; `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` `computeAtmosphereColor` fallback (~L2335) lacks the `atmosphereLightIntensity` multiply. **Trace:** 2026-06-25 Weather Inspector confirm.

## NEW-WEBGPU-CLOUD-DEPTH-OCCLUSION — ✅ RESOLVED (Batch 409, commit c71856e071, 2026-06-26)

**RESOLVED.** Implemented per the recipe below: inline `logDepthToEyeDistance` (byte-compatible with `csm_reverseLogDepthToEyeDistance`) reverses the renderer-wide log depth to an along-ray eye distance, and the march clamps `tEnd = min(tEnd, tSceneHit)` after the tStart/tEnd block (sky pixels >= 0.999999 → no-op). `nearPlane@105`/`farPlane@106` added by renaming the Batch-408 reserved pads (add-only, struct stays 108). Verified: sky view unchanged (`probe-cloud-diagonal` GREEN — a wrong reconstruction would clip the sky too), git-stash A/B (`probe-cloud-depth-occlusion.mjs`) confirms the fix is active. RTE + culling (below) remain open. Original entry kept for the trail.

### (Original)

**Surfaced** by the cloud-coverage/RTE investigation workflow (after Batch 406 made clouds fill the whole screen). `ProceduralClouds.wgsl:461` samples `sceneDepth` but **never uses it** — the march (the loop ~L539-628) terminates only on the cloud-shell sphere intersections + transmittance, so volumetric clouds composite **over the globe/terrain that should occlude them**. Visible when looking DOWN at terrain with clouds beyond/below; mild in the demo's straight-up view.

**The fix (recipe — mirror `AerialPerspective.wgsl`, the renderer-wide log-depth contract):**
1. Cesium WebGPU writes **logarithmic depth** into `_depthStencilView` (the buffer the cloud pass gets as `depthView`). Reconstruct eye distance with `csm_reverseLogDepthToEyeDistance` — inline as AerialPerspective.wgsl does (L110-117): `depthFromNear = exp2(logZ * log2FarDepthFromNearPlusOne) - 1.0; return depthFromNear + near;`.
2. **Needs two new uniforms** the cloud struct does NOT currently carry: `near` and `log2FarDepthFromNearPlusOne` (from `UniformState`/the frame). Grow CloudUniforms ADD-ONLY into the V11 tail pads (105-107 are free; one more 16-byte row to 112 if needed) — coordinate the byte table.
3. Sky guard: `if (rawDepth >= farFraction) {` treat as sky → **no occlusion** (let the full shell march). AerialPerspective uses a sky-depth cutoff fraction.
4. Convert eye distance → distance along the cloud ray: reconstruct `eyeDir` like AerialPerspective L194-196 (`ndc = (uv.x*2-1, (1-uv.y)*2-1)`, `eyeH = inverseProjection*vec4(ndc,0,1)`, `eyeDir = normalize(eyeH.xyz/eyeH.w)`); `tSceneHit = eyeDistance / max(-eyeDir.z, 1e-3)` (eye -z depth → ray distance), OR reconstruct the world hit and `distance(rayOrigin, worldHit)`. **Watch the `(1-uv.y)` flip** — the cloud `getWorldRay` does `uv*2-1` directly; verify the conventions line up (this is the #1 footgun).
5. `if (rawDepth < farFraction) { tEnd = min(tEnd, tSceneHit); }` after the tStart/tEnd block, AND `if (rawDepth < farFraction && (t + 0.5*curStep) > tSceneHit) { break; }` in the march loop. No depth WRITE (clouds are a translucent over-composite).
6. **Probe (dedicated):** a LOOKING-DOWN view at terrain with a cloud deck beyond — assert no cloud alpha over the front-facing globe disc (sample pixels where `rawDepth < far` over terrain, confirm transmittance≈1). The existing upward probes won't catch it.

**Files:** `Shaders/WebGPU/Environment/ProceduralClouds.wgsl` (fragmentMain + struct), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUProceduralCloudRenderer.ts` (pack near + log2Far). **Risk:** wrong reconstruction clips clouds badly — verify against AerialPerspective's working math + a probe before claiming. **Trace:** 2026-06-26 cloud-coverage/RTE workflow.

## NEW-WEBGPU-CLOUD-RTE — cloud raymarch runs in absolute ECEF, not RTE — ⚠️ PARTIAL (Batch 412, 442901f890, 2026-06-26)

**PARTIAL.** Batch 412 replaced the naive `raySphereIntersect` with the Haines stable closest-point form (build the perpendicular vector FIRST, square THAT; roots as `tClosest ± halfChord`) — every grazing ray gains precision, roots identical, no view regresses (probe-cloud-diagonal + -genus stay GREEN). **STILL OPEN:** the residual near-RADIAL cancellation (`radius - |ro|`, a ~1e3 m difference of ~6.4e6 m magnitudes) needs full RTE high/low camera (DP emulation in WGSL + encodedCameraHigh/Low struct growth). The residual is ~1 m and **not visibly observed**, so the full DP path stays deferred until a shimmer artifact is actually seen — not worth the struct growth for an unobserved ~1 m wobble. Original entry below.

**Surfaced** same investigation. `ProceduralClouds.wgsl:463` `rayOrigin = cloud.cameraPosition` (absolute ~6.378e6 m) and `raySphereIntersect` computes `c = dot(ro,ro) - radius*radius` — subtracting two ~4.07e13 f32 values (catastrophic cancellation; ~5-7 sig-digits lost vs a 1.5 km shell). Also `samplePos = rayOrigin + rayDir*t` at absolute scale. **NOT the diagonal cause** (that was Batch 406's triangle), but it produces a shimmering/ragged cloud-layer edge + precision wobble at altitude/grazing. **Fix:** do the intersection + march in **camera-relative (RTE)** coords (sphere center = `-cameraPos`), pack camera as `encodedCameraHigh/Low` (EncodedCartesian3) per the project RTE rule, and reformulate `c` as the cancellation-safe `(length(center)-r)*(length(center)+r)`. **Priority:** medium (visible at altitude/grazing, not the headline). **Trace:** 2026-06-26.

## NEW-WEBGPU-CLOUD-CULLING — no frustum/occlusion cull on the cloud pass — ✅ RESOLVED (frustum, Batch 413, 3676fb10f5, 2026-06-26)

**RESOLVED (frustum).** Batch 413 added a frustum cull at the top of `executeProceduralClouds`: the cloud shell is a sphere at the planet origin (radius = planetRadius + cloudLayerTop), so the signed distance to each frustum plane is just `plane.w`, and the shell is OUTSIDE iff some plane has `w < -outerR` (matching Cesium `BoundingSphere.intersectPlane`'s `distanceToPlane < -radius`, confirmed against Core/BoundingSphere.js — the type's "outward" comment is misleading). Uses the typed `cullingVolume.planes` (no new imports). Doesn't over-fire (probe GREEN). **Intentionally NOT done:** the altitude hard-gate — it would pop the visible thin deck out, and the existing low-quality-above-100km resolver covers that perf case (the through-globe correctness is the Batch-409 depth occlusion, not culling). Original entry below.

**Surfaced** same investigation. `executeProceduralClouds` always does the full-screen `pass.draw(3)` when `showProceduralClouds` is on — **no frustum cull, no globe-occlusion cull, no altitude gate** (the `volumetricEnable/DisableAltitude` values are read only to pick the quality tier, not to skip the pass). **Fix:** after device validation (~L422) (1) `BoundingSphere(Cartesian3.ZERO, outerR)` vs `frameState.cullingVolume.computeVisibility` → early-return on OUTSIDE; (2) make `volumetricEnable/DisableAltitude` hard-gate the pass; (3) the depth-occlusion fix above already kills most through-globe clouds, so this is mainly a perf win. **Priority:** low (perf). **Trace:** 2026-06-26.

## NEW-SANDCASTLE2-INDEX-WGSL-IMPORTMAP — ✅ RESOLVED 2026-06-26 — Sandcastle2 broken: deep `@cesium/engine/index-wgsl.js` specifier had no browser-loadable import-map target

**RESOLUTION (2026-06-26):** Fixed exactly along the recipe below, with one happy surprise. (a) Added `outFileName` + `external` options to `bundleIndexJs` and a second `bundleIndexJs` call in `buildEngine` that emits `packages/engine/Build/Unminified/index-wgsl.js`. (b) The feared "near-full second engine copy" did NOT materialize — the emitted bundle is only **113 KB** (0.67% of the 16.8 MB main `index.js`): the WebGPU cluster renderers + WGSL helpers + compat stubs pull in a bounded shared-dep subset, not the whole engine. And **no gallery demo uses these exports at runtime** (the Clustered Lighting demo drives `scene.clusteredLightingEnabled`, the high-level API, not the standalone renderers), so the duplicated instance is inert. The complex "rewrite index-wgsl's shared imports to bare `@cesium/engine`" step was therefore unnecessary — the small inert bundle is acceptable. (c) Flattened the LightTypes + Weather + AtmosphericEffects deep specifiers in `createCesiumJs` to bare `from '@cesium/engine'` (byte-identical variant output — esbuild dedupes). (d) Added `"@cesium/engine/index-wgsl.js"` import-map entries in BOTH `buildSandcastle.js` blocks + a `copyExtraFiles` entry for the build-to-dir path. **Verified:** Sandcastle2 loads with 0 module-resolve/export errors (upstream `3d-tiles-compare` + ported `webgpu-fullscreen-sky`), the ported demo renders (WebGPU sky + custom panel + widgets, screenshot read), thumbnails load. **Files:** `scripts/build.js` (bundleIndexJs + buildEngine + createCesiumJs), `scripts/buildSandcastle.js`. Original diagnosis kept below for history.

---

**Surfaced** loading `Apps/Sandcastle2/index.html?id=*` → `Uncaught TypeError: Failed to resolve module specifier "@cesium/engine/Source/Scene/LightTypes.js"` (and missing gallery thumbnails). PRE-EXISTING (not from the C3 weather batches); the Sandcastle2 build was stale (Jun 12, before the Jun-19 upstream v1.141-143 merge), and the merge changed the import-map / engine layout. `npm run build-sandcastle` regenerates Sandcastle2 but does NOT fix it (structural).

**Root cause chain (fully traced):**
1. Sandcastle2's demo runner (`Apps/Sandcastle2/standalone.html` + `templates/bucket.html`) loads `/Source/Cesium.js` (the gitignored createCesiumJs combined barrel) as a raw ES module, with an import map (in `scripts/buildSandcastle.js`) that maps the EXACT `@cesium/engine` → `packages/engine/Build/Unminified/index.js` — but has NO trailing-slash / deep-subpath entry.
2. `createCesiumJs` (scripts/build.js) emits MOST exports as the bare `from '@cesium/engine'` (import-map resolves them), but **LightTypes, the Weather/AtmosphericEffects public API, AND the WebGPU cluster exports** as DEEP `from '@cesium/engine/Source/Scene/LightTypes.js'` / `from '@cesium/engine/index-wgsl.js'` specifiers, which the exact-only import map can't resolve → the browser throws.
3. LightTypes/Weather/AtmosphericEffects CAN be flattened to the bare `@cesium/engine` (the engine main re-exports them — verified packages/engine/index.js). **But the WebGPU exports CANNOT** — they live in `index-wgsl.js` (separate, because the webgl-only variant strips WebGPU), and the engine main bundle (`Build/Unminified/index.js`) does NOT publicly export `WebGPUClusterBoundsRenderer` etc.; it only contains them internally.
4. The engine build emits ONLY `Build/Unminified/index.js` (one entry) — there is **no browser-loadable `Build/Unminified/index-wgsl.js`** for an import-map entry to point at.

**Fix recipe (the complete fix; a focused build-pipeline change, deferred — touches the engine build + needs cross-variant verification, so not landed at the tail of the C3 session):**
1. Add `packages/engine/index-wgsl.js` as a SECOND Unminified ESM build entry so `packages/engine/Build/Unminified/index-wgsl.js` is emitted (exports the WebGPU cluster + WGSL symbols). The entry build is `buildEngine` (scripts/build.js:1634) → `bundleIndexJs` (scripts/build.js:566). **Two gotchas that make this non-trivial:** (a) `bundleIndexJs` HARDCODES `outfile: ".../index.js"` (L591) → add an `outFileName` option (default `"index.js"`) before a second call can emit `index-wgsl.js`; (b) `bundleIndexJs` sets `external: []` for engine entries (L593), so a naive second bundle pulls index-wgsl's transitive deps (Core/Renderer/Scene) into a near-FULL second engine copy → the "multiple CesiumJS instances" hazard the L592 comment warns about (double download + parse + duplicated stateful singletons: shader/pipeline caches, `setGlobalDefaultRenderer`). The fix MUST mark `@cesium/engine` external for the index-wgsl bundle AND make `index-wgsl.js` import its SHARED (non-WebGPU) deps from the bare `@cesium/engine` (so they resolve to the main instance via the import map), bundling ONLY the WebGPU-specific modules. That's a generation change to the `index-wgsl.js` contents at scripts/build.js:~1522. This singleton concern is why it's a focused task, not a quick add.
2. In `scripts/buildSandcastle.js` (BOTH the `outputToBuildDir` true/false import-map blocks), add `"@cesium/engine/index-wgsl.js": { path: ".../packages/engine/Build/Unminified/index-wgsl.js", typesPath: ... }`.
3. (Optional, cleaner) In `createCesiumJs` flatten the LightTypes + Weather + AtmosphericEffects deep specifiers to the bare `from '@cesium/engine'` (the engine main exports them), reducing the deep surface to just index-wgsl. **Verify with `node Tools/variant-smoke-test.mjs`** (dual + webgl-only + webgpu-only) before committing — createCesiumJs feeds the production variant barrels.
4. `npm run build-sandcastle` + load `Apps/Sandcastle2/index.html?id=3d-tiles-compare` in Edge → assert 0 module-resolve / `is not exported` errors + thumbnails render.

**Partial-fix trail (reverted):** a partial attempt (step 3 bare-flatten + step 2 import-map → the main bundle) got it from the LightTypes error to `index-wgsl.js does not provide an export named 'WebGPUClusterBoundsRenderer'` (the main bundle lacks the WebGPU exports), proving step 1 (the separate index-wgsl bundle) is required. Reverted to keep the production build known-good. **Files:** `scripts/build.js` (createCesiumJs ~L489-540 + the engine Unminified build), `scripts/buildSandcastle.js` (import maps ~L70 / ~L134). **Trace:** 2026-06-26.

## NEW-WEBGPU-FROXEL-FOG-SCATTER-DYNAMIC-RANGE — froxel volumetric fog whiteouts (no usable dynamic range) (2026-06-26)

**Surfaced by Batch 420 (Phase C ground fog).** Enabling the froxel `WebGPUVolumetricFogRenderer` for the first time (it was scaffolded Phase-5a but **off by default and evidently never actually compiled/run** — Principle 7) exposed a chain of latent bugs, all fixed in Batch 420: two WGSL reserved-word identifiers (`enable`, `out`), a composite depth bind-group sample-type mismatch (`depth` vs the float depth-resolve texture actually bound), a perspective-vs-log depth decode in the composite, and a **degenerate fullscreen-triangle `vertexMain` in `VolumetricFogComposite.wgsl`** (uv ranged [0,2]; the composite output reached **0%** of the canvas — the same oversized-triangle bug class as the C3 cloud diagonal). With those fixed the renderer compiles, dispatches, and presents end-to-end (fog composite now covers ~87% of canvas; clouds not regressed).

**THE REMAINING GAP (this entry):** the froxel **scatter integration** (`VolumetricFog.wgsl::integrate`, `accumScattered += transmittance × scattered × sliceThickness`) has **no self-limiting / energy conservation**, so over the long low-altitude horizon path the accumulated scattered radiance jumps past the display's 1.0 clamp across a **<1.2× density window** — empirically bisected: invisible below `peakDensity ≈ 1e-6`, fully clamped-white above `≈ 1.2e-6`, with essentially no usable middle. Result: any visible fog is a **near-total whiteout**, not a graded mist. Batch 420 pins `peakDensity = 1.1e-6` (top of the visible band — meets the ground-concentration criterion but reads as a heavy haze) and leaves volumetric fog + ground fog **default OFF** (byte-neutral) precisely because the only visible output today is a whiteout.

**RESOLVED — Batch 421 (2026-06-28).** The scatter integration is now **energy-conserving single-scatter**: per froxel slice `tau = σ_t·Δz; sliceTransmittance = exp(-tau); inscatter = sourceRadiance·(1 - sliceTransmittance)`, accumulated `accumScattered += transmittance·inscatter; transmittance *= sliceTransmittance`. The slice in-scatter is the analytic transmittance-weighted integral (NOT `× sliceThickness`), so the running in-scatter telescopes to `≤ sourceRadiance` and density maps to opacity via a smooth Beer-Lambert rolloff — no clamp cliff. The scattering pass now writes a **density-independent** `sourceRadiance = albedo·(sun-phase + moon + ambient)` (the `× density` factor moved entirely into the extinction term in `.a`).

**The ACTUAL whiteout root cause (found via GPU column readback of the integrated/scattering 3D textures):** the Henyey-Greenstein **forward-scatter peak overflowed f16** — the per-froxel `sourceRadiance` saturated at **65504** (f16 max) on rays where the HG denominator approached its singularity, so `accumScattered` exploded regardless of `peakDensity` (it was binary-saturated at *any* nonzero density, which is why bisecting `peakDensity` did nothing). Fixed by clamping HG in `VolumetricFog.wgsl::henyeyGreenstein` (anisotropy clamp, denominator floored at the physical `(1-|g|)²`, phase clamped to ≤4). With `sourceRadiance` bounded (~0.2 phase + a 0.7 ambient floor for the milky fill, ground-fog path only), density now drives real optical depth.

**Final tuning (ground-fog path):** `bandHeight = 120 m`, `peakDensity = 1.2e-4` /m, ground-fog ambient floor `0.7`. **Probe-verified** (`Tools/visual-regression/probe-ground-fog.mjs`): 0 device errors, OFF scene lit, OFF-vs-OFF = 0.00 (byte-neutral default), ON `lowerBandBrighten 32.2 > upperBandBrighten 22.9` (mist hugs the ground). Intensity sweep 0.3 / 0.6 / 1.0 → lower band 110 / 120 / 131, visibly thinning mist (read the PNGs: 0.3 = light horizon haze, 1.0 = heavy milky mist, terrain visible through both — NOT a whiteout). **Files:** `VolumetricFog.wgsl` (HG clamp + integrate + density-independent scatter), `WebGPUVolumetricFogRenderer.ts` (tuning + ambient floor). Volumetric fog + ground fog remain **default OFF** (byte-neutral). **Trace:** 2026-06-26 → fixed 2026-06-28.

## WIRE-MODEL-COLOR-ALPHA-SEMANTICS — model.color alpha < 1 pass routing + alpha == 0 hide (2026-07-01)

**Surfaced by WIRE-MODEL-COLOR (model.color / colorBlendMode / colorBlendAmount).** The blend-mode math shipped: `MODEL_HAS_COLOR` (ShaderDefine bit 27, keySalt pattern) gates an `applyModelColor()` FS block in `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl` matching `ModelColorStageFS.glsl` exactly (`mix(diffuse, color, blend)`, `ceil(blend)` highlight multiply, `alpha *= color.a`); the uniforms ride the material UB's reserved lanes (floats 184-187 `_pad_reserved8` = RGBA, float 175 `motionFlags.w` = `ColorBlendMode.getColorBlend`). Probe-verified: `probe-model-color.mjs` (HIGHLIGHT/REPLACE/MIX vs WebGL + untouched off-gate).

**THE REMAINING GAP (this entry):** WebGL's `ModelColorPipelineStage` additionally (a) routes the model to `Pass.TRANSLUCENT` when `model.color.alpha < 1.0` (so the alpha multiply actually blends), and (b) disables the color mask when `alpha === 0.0` (model invisible but still depth-occluding, unless silhouetted). On WebGPU the FS `alpha *= color.a` lands in whatever pass the material's own `alphaMode` chose — an OPAQUE-material model with `color.alpha = 0.5` stays in the opaque pipeline (no blending → renders fully opaque), and `alpha = 0` differs from WebGL's colorMask semantics. Fix shape: fold `model.color.alpha < 1` into the per-primitive pass/pipeline selection in `WebGPUModelRenderer` (the `matInfo.alphaMode === BLEND` sites) the way the dual-command batch-table path already derives a translucent pipeline, and emit a writeMask-0 pipeline variant (or skip color emission while keeping the depth pre-pass) for the `alpha === 0` hide. (Note: WIRE-MODEL-SILHOUETTE has since wired the writeMask-0 base variant for the silhouette path — `getSilhouetteModelPipeline(..., invisible)` — so the `alpha === 0` + silhouette combination renders body-hidden + rim correctly; the non-silhouette `alpha === 0` hide and the `alpha < 1` pass routing remain.) **Files:** `WebGPUModelRenderer.js` (pass selection), `WebGPUModelPipelineCache.js` (writeMask variant). **Trace:** 2026-07-01.

## WIRE-MODEL-SILHOUETTE-TRANSLUCENT-DIVERGENCE — translucent silhouetteColor (alpha < 1) body-wash mismatch, match-vs-document decision (2026-07-01)

**Surfaced by WIRE-MODEL-SILHOUETTE (model.silhouetteColor / silhouetteSize).** The opaque stencil two-pass shipped at parity: `MODEL_SILHOUETTE` (ShaderDefine bit 28, keySalt pattern) gates the rewritten `ModelSilhouetteStage.wgsl` chunk + VS-inflate / FS-colour ifdef blocks in `ModelPBRComplete.wgsl`; the base draw uses a stencil-write pipeline variant (`getSilhouetteModelPipeline` — ALWAYS/REPLACE, per-draw `setStencilReference(model._silhouetteId % 255)`, writeMask-0 when `model.isInvisible()`), and a derived colour command (second material UB with pass-flag lane 107 = 1, expand lanes 105/106, colour lanes 112-115; `getSilhouetteColorPipeline` — stencil NOT-EQUAL, cull off) draws the inflated rim after all of the model's base commands. Probe-verified: `probe-model-silhouette.mjs` (RED/size-4 rim 3905 vs 4036 px, 100% dilated overlap; size-0 off-gate at load noise).

**THE DIVERGENCE (this entry):** with `silhouetteColor.alpha < 1` the derived colour command routes to `Pass.TRANSLUCENT` on BOTH backends (WebGL `deriveSilhouetteColorCommand` parity), but the on-screen result differs. Measured (scratch capture, milk truck, RED@0.5/size 6): **WebGL washes the ENTIRE model translucent-red** (~61k half-red px — its translucent/OIT pass does not carry the scene stencil, so the NOT-EQUAL cutout passes everywhere and the whole inflated model draws); **WebGPU draws the rim only** (~5k px — the translucent pass shares the scene depth-stencil attachment, so the stencil cutout keeps working). WebGPU's result matches the DOCUMENTED intent ("the stencil buffer is used to cutout the part that overlaps the regular model" — `ModelSilhouettePipelineStage.js:78-85`); WebGL's body-wash looks like an upstream OIT-stencil artifact. **Decision needed (match-vs-document, same shape as PARITY-POINT-SPRITE-SHAPE):** replicate WebGL's body-wash for byte-parity, or keep the intended cutout and document the deliberate divergence. Until decided, translucent silhouettes render rim-only on WebGPU. **Files:** `WebGPUModelRenderer.js` (silhouette colour command emission), `WebGPUModelPipelineCache.js` (`getSilhouetteColorPipeline` translucent variant). **Trace:** 2026-07-01.
