## WIRE-PP-LIBRARY-BUILTINS-RESIDUALS — per-stage gaps left by the library built-in interception (2026-07-02)

**Surfaced by WIRE-PP-LIBRARY-BUILTINS (the 7 orphaned `PostProcessStageLibrary` built-ins).** The interception mechanism shipped: `WebGPULibraryPostProcessStage.ts` maps the well-known `czm_*` names (`czm_black_and_white`, `czm_brightness`, `czm_night_vision`, `czm_silhouette`, `czm_edge_detection_<guid>` prefix, `czm_lens_flare`, `czm_depth_view`) to their WGSL twins during the configure pass's user-stage scan (`WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts`), with per-frame enabled/uniform sync + a CPU twin of the czm_* sun/earth frame state for LensFlare. Parity rewrites landed for EdgeDetection (depth-Sobel), NightVision (frame-seeded noise), DepthView (raw depth), Silhouette (vec4 mix), Brightness (`target` reserved-word fix), LensFlare (full gate/mask/ghost/halo port). Also fixed while here: upstream's `removeStages()` compaction only runs AFTER the feature-renderer early-return in `PostProcessStageCollection.update()`, so on WebGPU `postProcessStages.remove(stage)` left an `undefined` hole, `_stages.length` never shrank, and the length-based rebuild gate (Batch 290) leaked BOTH user WGSL stages and library stages until the next add — the FR update now mirrors the compaction. Probe: `probe-pp-library-builtins.mjs` (7/7 stages, cross-backend, off-gate byte-identical).

**Residual per-stage gaps (this entry):**

1. **LensFlare `dirtTexture` / `starTexture` overlays not ported.** The WGSL twin implements the space gate, sun-on-screen gate, isInEarth ghost mask, 4-ghost chromatic chain, halo, and sun-distance weighting (ghost/halo geometry matches WebGL pixel-position-for-pixel-position), but WebGL additionally adds a tiled dirt-texture overlay and modulates the in-space result by the rotating starburst texture (WGSL approximates the star factor as 1.0 → smoother, somewhat brighter ghosts). Fix shape: load `Assets/Textures/LensFlare/{DirtMask,StarBurst}.jpg` into GPU textures at stage init (the stage uniforms carry the URLs), extend the stage's bind group + `LensFlareUniforms`, port the dirt-tile/star-rotate math. M effort.
2. **`selected` feature masking (CZM_SELECTED_FEATURE) unsupported** for EdgeDetection/Silhouette (and BlackAndWhite's selected bypass). WebGL rebuilds the stage shader with `czm_selected()` when `stage.selected = [features]` is set; the WebGPU twins always process the whole frame (identical to WebGL with no selection). Needs the pick-id/selected-texture plumbing — same infrastructure gap as the model-selection post-process path. L effort. **EXTENDED (`SYNC_1145_WEBGPU_PARITY_CENSUS_2026-09-05.md` C-09, 2026-09-05; the census's §4 "Belongs elsewhere" rules that C-09 is extended here and that NO `UPSTREAM-SYNC-1.145-07` item is opened for it — `-07` item 9 is an unrelated open row about cluster (c)'s Karma specs):** the same infrastructure gap also covers **user-authored WGSL post-process stages**, not only the three intercepted library built-ins named above — `PostProcessStageCollection.js:531-539` hands the *entire* `update()` to the feature renderer and returns before any per-stage selected-id logic runs, so a user's own `wgslFragmentShader` stage with `stage.selected = [feature]` is just as unreachable as EdgeDetection/Silhouette are. Separately, 1.145 hardened the GLSL-side `createSelectedTexture` (`PostProcessStage.js:886`) with a `context.limits.maximumTextureSize` clamp plus a one-time warning (`PostProcessStage._oneTimeWarning("postProcessStageSelectedTextureSize", …)`) so an oversized selection degrades gracefully instead of throwing — **when the WebGPU selected-id path above is eventually built, its texture allocation must carry that same clamp and one-time warning**, not a bare allocation that can exceed `context.limits.maximumTextureSize` on WebGPU. (This clamp read is itself correctly layered through the fork's own `context.limits`, not the retired `ContextLimits` global — see `AR-028`'s amendment in `QUEUE_2026-09-03_ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW.md`, which is the unreachability half of this same finding, C-19.)
3. **DepthView encoding divergence (within-tolerance, documented).** WebGL shows `czm_readDepth` (reversed-log → conventional depth); WebGPU shows the raw conventional device depth from `depthSampleableView`. Same near-dark/far-white shape, absolute gray levels differ (probe xMean 43/255 at tol 45). Also the WebGPU sampleable depth copy does not include point-primitive depth (the WebGL depth vis shows the probe's 200px point disc, WebGPU's doesn't). Only worth chasing if a consumer needs numeric depth-vis parity.
4. **Ordering vs user WGSL stages:** intercepted library stages execute AFTER all user `wgslFragmentShader` stages (two separate pipeline arrays), not interleaved in `collection._stages` order. Matters only when a scene mixes both kinds and depends on order. S effort (merge into one ordered list) if it ever bites.

**Files:** `WebGPULibraryPostProcessStage.ts` (registry + stage class), `WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts` (interception + sync + compaction), `WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts` (chain slot), `Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/{BlackAndWhite,Brightness,NightVision,DepthView,EdgeDetection,Silhouette,LensFlare}.wgsl`. **Trace:** 2026-07-02.

## BUG-GLOBE-PIPELINE-NAME-AXES — globe descriptor name doesn't encode all structural pipeline axes (latent central-cache aliasing) (2026-07-02)

**Context.** `WebGPURenderPipelineCache.generateCacheKey` keys on `descriptor.name` (the optional `variant` arg is unused by the globe path — `resolveGlobePipelineEntry` passes only the descriptor). The convention (documented at `WebGPUGlobeSurfacePipelines.ts:371-374`) is therefore "distinct pipeline structure MUST produce a distinct name". Bug 487 (GLOBE-UNDERGROUND-COLOR) fixed the worst instance — the no-cull variant differed only in `primitive.cullMode` with an identical name, so underground tiles aliased to the cull-back pipeline and the underside never rendered (nondeterministic by creation race).

**Remaining latent instances (same class).** The globe descriptor name (`Globe terrain (quant, norm, blend, …labels)`) still does NOT encode:

- `strideBytes` / `hasWebMercatorT` (changes the vertex `arrayStride` + texcoord attribute format — an alias here binds the wrong vertex layout),
- `hasGeodeticSurfaceNormals` (extra attribute + different shader module via `GEODETIC_NORMAL` define),
- `ShaderDefine.LOG_DEPTH` / `GLOBE_IMAGERY_REDUCED` (different shader modules),
- `_sampleCount` (multisample state — canvas-format/MSAA flips are partially covered by the `_scenePipelineFormatGeneration` LOCAL cache wipe, but the CENTRAL cache retains the old-name entry).

Most combinations are coincidentally disambiguated by the existing labels (quant/norm/blend correlate with stride) or by session homogeneity (webMercatorT is uniform per imagery provider), which is why no visible artifact is currently attributed to them — but the failure mode is the Bug 487 shape: silent, race-decided, wrong-pipeline binds.

**Suggested fix (S).** Fold the missing axes into the name (e.g. `, s${strideBytes}, wm${0|1}, d${defines.toString(16)}, ms${sampleCount}`) OR pass a `variant` object to the central cache. Audit the OTHER renderers that use name-keyed central caching for the same convention violation.

## PARITY-POINT-SPRITE-SHAPE-RESIDUALS — residuals surfaced by the point-sprite shape/size parity fix (2026-07-02)

**Surfaced by PARITY-POINT-SPRITE-SHAPE.** The shape/size fix shipped: WebGPU point-cloud quads now rasterize as SOLID SQUARES like WebGL `gl_Points` (the old soft-circle carve in `WebGPUPointCloudRenderer.ts`'s inline WGSL + `PointCloudEDLDepth.wgsl` was WebGPU-only invention — `ModelFS.glsl` only carves a circle under `HAS_POINT_DIAMETER`, the Bentley point-style extension); the phantom 1920×1080 viewport read (`uniformState._context?._canvas` — always undefined) was replaced with the real `drawingBufferWidth/Height`; WebGL point-size attenuation reached parity (per-point `min(geometricError·geometricErrorScale·drawingBufferHeight/sseDenominator / eyeDepth, bakedMax)` in the color/LOD/velocity/EDL-depth VSes via the formerly-`_pad2` UB lane, with `PointCloud.js` giving a constant style `pointSize` priority over attenuation exactly like WebGL's `hasPointSizeStyle` branch, and `boundingSphere` falling back to `_boundingSphere` on the FR path so `TimeDynamicPointCloud.getGeometricError` stops zeroing attenuation); and `PointPrimitiveColor/Pick.wgsl` now mirror `PointPrimitiveCollectionVS` sizing exactly (outlinePercent from unpadded size, scaleByDistance on the TOTAL size, +3px AA padding, `v_pixelDistance = 2/totalSize`). Probe: `probe-point-sprite-shape.mjs` (styled point cloud + attenuation-only cloud gated on gain-NORMALIZED ds4 < 16% — per-channel means equalized before the per-cell compare so the drifting tint residual below cancels while spatial shape/size/coverage breaks still score 20%+; point primitives raw ds4 < 5%; 0 device errors; tighten the normalized gates to ~8% once the tint fix lands).

**Residuals (this entry):**

1. **WebGPU point-cloud blue/brightness COLOR tint — candidate new parity row.** With shape + size now matching, the remaining point-cloud probe residual is a color-path gap: the WebGPU cloud reads bluer/brighter than WebGL on the same PNTS data. It drives essentially ALL of the remaining point-cloud raw-ds4 on both probe scenes and DRIFTS monotonically across consecutive same-session runs (seven 2026-07-02 runs — styled: 9.34/12.14/12.9/13.76/14.52/15.6/16.67%; attenuation-only: 12.29/13.96/14.6/15.52/16.31/17.14/18.85%) — which is why the probe gates the point-cloud scenes on the gain-NORMALIZED ds4 instead of the raw one. Quantified at fix time: WebGL/WebGPU per-channel mean ratios over lit cells ≈ R 0.78 / G 0.72 / B 0.69 (WebGPU ~27-45% brighter, blue lifted most — the probe prints these `gains` every run), and a per-channel gain-equalized compare still leaves ~9.7-12.4% ds4 (itself creeping ~1pp/run), so the tint is NOT a pure global gain — it has a drifting per-point/nonlinear component. The monotone session-correlated creep is itself a lead: it smells like a time/adaptation-dependent stage (auto-exposure/tonemap adaptation or similar) contributing to the WebGPU point-cloud brightness, not a fixed constant offset. Suspect the color pipeline around the point-cloud draw (gamma/linear handling, tonemap interaction, or the RGB path through `buildInstanceBuffer`) rather than geometry — sizes matched in the auditor's footprint check. Worth its own parity ID (shape: `PARITY-POINTCLOUD-COLOR-TINT`) before any probe-gate tightening. M-investigate/S-fix effort.
2. **`czm_pixelRatio` and `u_maxTotalPointSize` unplumbed into the PointPrimitive WGSL UB (pre-existing, acknowledged in the shader comment).** `PointPrimitiveCollectionVS` multiplies the total sprite size by `czm_pixelRatio` and clamps to `u_maxTotalPointSize` (the GL aliased-point-size range cap); the WGSL twin (`PointPrimitiveColor/Pick.wgsl`) does neither — probes run at DPR 1 so this is invisible in CI, but **hiDPI (devicePixelRatio > 1) point primitives will undersize vs WebGL** by the pixel-ratio factor. Fix shape: add pixelRatio (and a large-constant max size — WebGPU has no aliased-point clamp to mirror) to the collection UB pack in the point-primitive renderer. S effort.

**Files:** `WebGPUPointCloudRenderer.ts` (color path, UB pack), `Shaders/WebGPU/Collections/PointPrimitiveColor.wgsl` / `PointPrimitivePick.wgsl` (pixelRatio lanes). **Trace:** 2026-07-02.

## GLTF-PRIMITIVE-MODE-RESIDUALS — residuals surfaced by the glTF POINTS-mode topology fix (2026-07-02; expanded audit 2026-07-31)

**Surfaced by GLTF-POINTS-MODE.** The topology gap shipped: `extractPrimitiveGeometry` now carries `primitiveType` (glTF `primitive.mode`), `WebGPUModelRenderer` maps mode-0 POINTS to a `"point-list"` GPUPrimitiveTopology on `primCache.topology`, and `WebGPUModelPipelineCache` threads a sticky per-primitive topology (same set-before-`getPipeline*` contract as the metadata/customShader chunks; `topologyVariantKey` leaves triangle-list keys byte-identical) through ALL per-primitive pipeline builders (color / depth-write / silhouette model+color / pick / pick-hover / precise-pick 1+2 / pick-metadata / velocity / classification / capture / error-fallback). Non-indexed POINTS primitives synthesize sequential indices at `ensurePrimitiveCache` time so they ride the drawIndexed path (WebGPU CPU-validates non-indexed `draw()` vertex ranges against every vertex-step slot; the 1-element default-attribute buffers pass drawIndexed via robust-access clamping but hard-fail `draw()`). Probe: `probe-gltf-points-mode.mjs` (PointCloudWithRGBColors.glb, 2500 non-indexed mode-0 points: WebGL 6186 vs WebGPU 6179 lit px, centroid Δ 0.2px, mean-channel Δ ≤ 6.2; off-gate `probe-model-pbr-audit` green).

**Residuals (this entry):**

1. **Non-indexed TRIANGLES models with missing attributes hit the same `draw()` validation error (pre-existing, latent).** Any non-indexed glTF primitive that lacks normals/tangents/uv/joints binds the pipeline cache's 1-element default vertex buffers, and the non-indexed `draw(vertexCount)` fails "Vertex range requires a larger buffer" — silently no model (invalid command buffer). The POINTS fix scoped the sequential-index synthesis to `topology === "point-list"` to keep the triangle off-gate byte-identical. `C11-90` widened the synthesis to every mode EXCEPT TRIANGLES (`synthesizesIndices` in the topology table), so LINES / LINE_LOOP / LINE_STRIP / TRIANGLE_STRIP / TRIANGLE_FAN are covered. **Non-indexed TRIANGLES remains OPEN and deliberately untouched** — it is the one case where synthesizing would change the historical `draw(vertexCount)` path, and the off-gate byte-identity of the overwhelmingly common primitive is worth more than closing a latent gap no shipped asset has surfaced. Sizing the default buffers is the alternative fix.
2. **LINES / LINE_LOOP / LINE_STRIP / TRIANGLE_STRIP / TRIANGLE_FAN still render as triangle-list. — ✅ SHIPPED (`C11-90`).** `topologyForPrimitiveType` is gone. `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUModelTopology.ts` is now the single enforceable home for the topology axis: an EXHAUSTIVE seven-mode table, `realizeModelPrimitiveTopology` (called exactly once per primitive from `ensurePrimitiveCache` — preparation, never draw), `modelPrimitiveState` (the only builder of a model/shadow `GPUPrimitiveState`, so `topology` and `stripIndexFormat` can never be written apart), and `buildModelTopologyVariantKey` / `modelTopologyAxisToken` / `parseModelTopologyVariantKey` (build+parse exact inverses). LINES→line-list, LINE_STRIP→line-strip, TRIANGLE_STRIP→triangle-strip (both with the exact `stripIndexFormat`), LINE_LOOP→line-list with each restart-delimited run's closing segment appended, TRIANGLE_FAN→triangle-list expanded around each run's hub. Triangle-list keys stay byte-identical (value AND numeric type), so no cached pipeline is orphaned. Contract: `Tools/visual-regression/model-primitive-topology.spec.mjs` (37/37), whose conversion fixtures are read out of the shipped `Apps/SampleData/models/PrimitiveRestart/*.glb` rather than hand-typed.
3. **`ModelPointCloudStylingStage.wgsl` remains orphaned — it does NOT map cleanly onto point-list.** WebGPU point-list rasterizes fixed 1px points (no `gl_PointSize` analog), which matches WebGL's unstyled `gl_PointSize = 1.0` default (ModelVS.glsl) — that's the parity the fix targets. Point-size STYLING (Cesium3DTileStyle `pointSize`, attenuation) on a Model-path POINTS primitive would need quad expansion like `WebGPUPointCloudRenderer`'s PNTS path; the WGSL styling helper stays as scaffolding for that follow-up (Principle 7 — do not remove).
4. **Shadow topology is only partially corrected in the dirty `C11-184` lane. — ✅ SHIPPED (`C11-90`).** Commands now carry `_shadowCastStripIndexFormat` beside `_shadowCastTopology`; `getShadowCastPipelineCacheKey` derives its topology segment from `modelTopologyAxisToken` (the SAME home the color key uses, so the two cannot drift), `_getOrCreateCastPipeline` builds its `primitive` block with `modelPrimitiveState`, and `WebGPUCSMCastPass` — which shares that factory — forwards the format too. A uint16 and a uint32 strip caster are now distinct cast pipelines; every pre-C11-90 caster key is byte-identical.
5. **Uint8 primitive-restart upcast is incorrect. — ✅ SHIPPED (`C11-90`).** `ModelPrimitiveGeometry` records `indexSourceComponentBytes` (the ORIGINAL accessor width, which `indexType` cannot express) and stays backend-agnostic; the realization promotes `0x00FF` → `0xFFFF` ONLY for the four modes `getMeshPrimitives.js` declares restart-capable, and the spec reads that permitted set out of `getMeshPrimitives.js` itself so ours cannot drift from upstream's. A uint8 LINES/TRIANGLES/POINTS asset keeps `255` as an ordinary vertex index and passes through by reference with zero allocation. Translation copies rather than rewriting in place, because the source array belongs to the cached immutable base descriptor.
6. **Generic Primitive duplicates the topology residual — STILL OPEN after `C11-90`.** `WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.ts`'s own `mapCesiumPrimitiveTypeToWebGPU` maps strips without `stripIndexFormat`, leaves LINE_LOOP unclosed, and treats TRIANGLE_FAN as triangle-list. `C11-90` deliberately scoped itself to the MODEL path; the realization home (`WebGPUModelTopology.ts`) is written as a pure, backend-neutral module precisely so the generic-Primitive path can adopt it without a rewrite, but adopting it means reworking that path's own index ownership and cache keys and must not be conflated with the Model visibility-preparation performance row.

**Required architecture — ✅ IMPLEMENTED for the Model path (`C11-90`):** one immutable-input, cached WebGPU primitive realization
`{topology, indexData, indexCount, indexFormat, stripIndexFormat, vertexCount}`;
no settled-frame rescans or allocations; preserve restart batches in one draw;
key every model pipeline and shadow variant by topology plus strip format; and
carry the same pair in capture records. Route fan/loop conversion through the
preparation/resource lane so it never lands on the render hot path.
Conversion cost model: passthrough returns the caller's array BY REFERENCE
(`allocatedIndexBytes === 0`) — a conversion allocates exactly once, in
preparation, only for LINE_LOOP closure, TRIANGLE_FAN expansion, a uint8
restart translation that actually finds a sentinel, or non-indexed synthesis.

**Files:** `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUModelTopology.ts` (NEW — the one home), `Scene/Model/ModelPrimitiveGeometry.js` (primitiveType extract + `indexSourceComponentBytes`), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUModelRenderer.ts` (realization at `ensurePrimitiveCache` + realized index upload + capture-record and shadow-command axis), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts` (sticky realization + `modelPrimitiveState` at all 12 builders), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUShadowMapRenderer.js` + `WebGPUCSMCastPass.ts` (cast key + descriptor). **Contract:** `Tools/visual-regression/model-primitive-topology.spec.mjs`. **Trace:** 2026-07-02; `C11-90` 2026-08-01.

## RTE-ELLIPSOID-AWARE-RESIDUALS — residuals surfaced by the ellipsoid-aware CSM ground-clamp fix (2026-07-02)

**Surfaced by RTE-ELLIPSOID-AWARE (FEAT-3DT2-03, CSM slice — SHIPPED).** The concrete positional-correctness gap named in the parity report (`WebGPUCSMRenderer.ts:74-79` hardcoded WGS84 radii) is closed: the WGS84 constants are now DEFAULTS, `WebGPUCSMRenderer.setEllipsoid(radii)` (change-detected, degenerate-radii-guarded) recomputes the inverse-square radii, and `WebGPUContext.executeShadowMapCastCommands` threads `scene.ellipsoid?.radii ?? scene.globe?.ellipsoid?.radii` in once per cast frame. `computeVisibleGroundFar` + the ground-clamped `computeFrustumCornersWorldSpace` (new optional trailing `invRadiiSq*` params, WGS84 defaults keep the exported spec API + `defines=0`-style migration behavior identical) now solve against the scene's actual globe. Probe: `probe-ellipsoid-rte.mjs` — synthesized 0.5×-scaled ellipsoid (per the FEAT-3DT2-03 probe note; no Mars/Moon asset needed): pre-fix `computeVisibleGroundFar` diverged from the `IntersectionTests.rayEllipsoid` reference by ~862,000% (7,328 km vs 850 m) and cascade splits ballooned to `maxShadowDistance` (100 km); post-fix both agree to 0.000% and splits tighten to the visible ground (935 m). WGS84 off-gate: pixel mismatch 0.0000% vs the pre-change build + FP-exact groundFar/splits.

**Residuals (this entry) — the REST of the "ellipsoid-aware RTE" umbrella.** Verified during this fix: the RTE encoding itself (`positionHigh/Low`, `encodedCameraHigh/Low`, `mvpRelativeToEye`) is ellipsoid-INDEPENDENT (camera-relative ECEF — no radii appear in the math), so "tileset._ellipsoid is never threaded" does not affect tile POSITIONS through the RTE path. The remaining hardcoded-Earth-radius sites are feature-specific:

1. **Terrain shadow-cast vertical exaggeration (`WebGPUShadowMapRenderer.js` WGSL `EARTH_RADIUS: f32 = 6378137.0`, quantized12 + terrainUncompressed variants).** Only active when `verticalExaggeration !== 1.0`; on a non-Earth globe the exaggeration offset in the CAST pass would mismatch the color pass. Fix shape: add the max radius to the existing `TerrainShadowGlobals` UB (`_pad` lane is free). S effort.
2. **Atmosphere / lens flare / procedural clouds / volumetric fog Earth-radius constants** (`WebGPUEffectsBindGroup.js`, `WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection.ts`, `WebGPUProceduralCloudRenderer.ts`, `WebGPUVolumetricFogRenderer.ts`). These mirror WebGL upstream, which also treats atmosphere-adjacent effects as Earth-keyed (e.g. `PostProcessStageLibrary.createLensFlareStage` defaults to `Ellipsoid.WGS84.maximumRadius`); NOT a WebGL↔WebGPU parity gap, tracked here only for a future non-Earth-scenes epic.
3. **No real Mars/Moon asset test** (`PARITY-RTE-ELLIPSOID-BLOCKER` stands). The scaled-ellipsoid mock verifies the CSM math + cast-shadow placement cross-backend; an end-to-end non-Earth 3D Tileset pixel pass is still deferred until an asset is sourced.

**Files:** `WebGPUCSMRenderer.ts` (setEllipsoid + threaded solves), `WebGPUContext.ts` (per-frame threading), `cesium-js-types.d.ts` (`CesiumScene.ellipsoid`), `Tools/visual-regression/probe-ellipsoid-rte.mjs` (new gate). **Trace:** 2026-07-02.

- **NEW-GLOBE-DAYTIME-OCEAN-BRIGHTNESS** — ✅ SHIPPED (Q10, 2026-07-04). Root cause was NEITHER glint NOR atmosphere daylight brightness (both red herrings from the original triage) — it was the ocean **`diffuseHighlight`** term in `GlobeTerrain.wgsl::computeEnhancedOcean` being **zeroed on every daytime fragment**. WebGL `computeWaterColor` (GlobeFS.glsl L830) applies `diffuseHighlight = waveHighlightColor(0.3,0.45,0.6) * NdotL * mask * (1.0 - fade)` where `fade` is the **atmosphere camera-distance fade** (L428 = `clamp((cameraDist - lightingFadeOut)/(lightingFadeIn - lightingFadeOut),0,1)`) — 0 at close/mid range → full bluish highlight. The WGSL called `computeEnhancedOcean(..., dayFade, ...)` passing the **day/night TERMINATOR fade**, which `fragmentMain` forces to `1.0` whenever `enableLighting` is off (the DEFAULT) → `highlightFade = 1 - 1 = 0` → the highlight vanished, leaving the ocean ~4x darker (deep navy vs WebGL bright blue) at mid-range while night stayed at parity (NdotL≈0 kills the highlight for both). **Fix (2 hunks, WGSL-only, GLSL already correct):** (1) call site passes `tile.groundAtmosphereControl.y` (the identical lightingFade clamp, packed per-tile) instead of `dayFade`; param renamed `dayFade`→`lightingFade`. (2) `tsPerturbationRatio` now derives from the **distance-faded** tangent normal `normalize(vec3(waveN.xy * waveIntensityFade, waveN.z)).z` (matching WebGL L818-819 `normalTangentSpace.xy *= waveIntensity`) — WITHOUT this, correcting hunk (1) unmasked a latent bug where `nonDiffuseHighlight` (peaks as NdotL→0) blew the NIGHT ocean out to saturated cyan (lum 28→208), because the raw `waveN.z` never faded to 1 at orbit. **Verified** (`diag-daytime-ocean-tmp.mjs`, pinned clocks, caribbean-mid `-70.1037,18.485,2000000`): DAY gpu-vs-gl **91.0% → 2.05%** (WebGPU lum 46.4→116.5 vs WebGL 117.3); NIGHT **1.04%** preserved (28.3 vs 29.5); PNGs read — day ocean now bright blue with visible sun-glint bloom, night correctly dark. Off-gate: change is confined to reflective-ocean water fragments (`tile.flags.x>0.5 && waterMask>0.01`); land/non-globe byte-identical; tsPerturbationRatio hunk is byte-identical at close zoom where `waveIntensityFade≈1`.

- **NEW-VECTOR3DTILE-CLASSIFY-CONTAINMENT** — ✅ SHIPPED (Q15R, 2026-07-04) via WebGL-parity **stencil Z-fail**. `WebGPUVector3DTilePrimitiveRenderer` now emits, per batch per ground pass, a stencil-MARK draw (colorWrite off, `depthCompare` less-equal against the BOUND scene depth, `stencilFront.depthFailOp` decrement-wrap / `stencilBack.depthFailOp` increment-wrap, terrain compare-always / tileset compare-equal-0x80, readMask `CESIUM_3D_TILE_MASK` 0x80 / writeMask `CLASSIFICATION_MASK` 0x0f) then a stencil-TESTED color draw (`compare not-equal 0`, depth test off, passOp zero to reset), both in the same TERRAIN/CESIUM_3D_TILE_CLASSIFICATION pass bucket (execute in push order in one render pass → the mark's stencil is visible to the immediately-following color draw). This mirrors `Vector3DTilePrimitive.getStencilDepthRenderState` + `colorRenderState` and compares per-FRAGMENT volume depth vs per-FRAGMENT globe depth in hardware at full precision, sidestepping BOTH FS-reconstruction walls below. The mark + color pipelines use a group(0)-only layout (no globe-depth-texture sample) so they're independent of `_globeDepthView`; pick + velocity keep the depth-sample bind group and are skipped when it's absent. **Verified** (`probe-vector3dtile-vctr.mjs`, restructured): FAR (20 km) IoU **1.000**, NEAR (3 km) IoU **0.932** (area ratio 1.07 — vs the old ~2.25x-area h/(h-1000) over-inflation), at BOTH `msaaSamples=4` (viewer default) AND `msaaSamples=1`; polylines + globe at parity; 0 device errors; PNGs read. **KEY probe lesson:** the WebGPU globe surface + the async stencil pipelines take ~100 frames after `tilesLoaded` to warm up — the probe's old `settle` broke at ~31 frames, yielding a FALSE-NEGATIVE black globe + empty footprint that an earlier revision mis-attributed to an "msaa=1 globe-black gap"; the fix was 200 trailing warmup frames, NOT any renderer change (the globe renders fine at msaa=1 once warm). **Follow-up:** `NEW-VECTOR3DTILE-STENCIL-2DCV-COVERAGE` (below). Files: `WebGPUVector3DTilePrimitiveRenderer.js`, `probe-vector3dtile-vctr.mjs`. **Trace:** 2026-07-04.

  Historical investigation (Q15, superseded by the Q15R stencil fix above) — the depth-sample FS approaches, proven insufficient:
  - **Approach A (eye-distance):** render both volume faces (cullMode "none", depthCompare "always" so back faces reach the FS), decode the sampled surface's log depth to an eye distance via `csm_reverseLogDepthToEyeDistance(surfaceDepth, encodeNear, encodeFar)` (encode = `uniformState._logDepthEncodeNearFar` = `[0.1, 1e10]`), compare to the volume fragment's clip-w eye distance (`1.0/i.pos.w`). **Result:** NEAR (3 km) IoU 1.000 ✅; FAR (20 km) over-discards to 0 ❌ — the `exp2` decode amplifies the depth quantum + any encode-near/far inconsistency into km-scale eye-distance error at 20 km, which exceeds the thin ±1 km volume.
  - **Approach B (log-window-z):** compare in the shared log-window-z space directly (`surfaceDepth <= i.pos.z + eps`); both the globe's sampled depth and the volume's `o.pos.z` are log-encoded with the same encode frustum, so no `exp2` amplification. **Result:** NEAR IoU 0.932 ✅ (slightly loose); FAR still 0 ❌ — the volume's per-VERTEX log z (interpolated) cannot bracket a thin volume at far range against the globe's per-FRAGMENT depth.
  - **Infrastructure blocker (independent):** at `scene.msaaSamples = 1` — the config the standing probe `probe-vector3dtile-vctr.mjs` forces for its NEAR/FAR parity frames (a legacy of the now-fixed `NEW-VECTOR3DTILE-MSAA-PIPELINE` gap, Q2) — the WebGPU globe depth texture (`_globeDepthView`, and `_packedTranslucentDepthView` is null with no translucent content) reads far/empty (`surfaceDepth ≈ 1.0`) for the footprint, so ANY depth-sample containment discards everything. The pre-change classifier only "passed" at msaa=1 because empty depth ≠ 0 dodged its sky-discard and it painted the full (inflated) silhouette. Verify whether the globe depth copy is populated at msaa=1 before relying on any depth-sample classifier there.
  - **Correct fix — stencil Z-fail (WebGL parity):** mirror `Vector3DTilePrimitive.getStencilDepthRenderState` (shipped above — this is what Q15R implemented). The Q15 note's "msaa=1 depth-population blocker" turned out to be a **probe warmup artifact**, not a real infra gap: the bound scene depth-stencil DOES hold the globe surface during the classifier pass at both msaa levels once the globe is warm (~100 frames); the earlier msaa=1 forcing measured too early. **Trace:** 2026-07-04.

- **NEW-VECTOR3DTILE-STENCIL-2DCV-COVERAGE** — 🟦 **BY-DESIGN (reconciled 2026-07-09, Campaign-7 batch 0) — NOT a parity gap; do not schedule as parity work.** Upstream WebGL `Vector3DTilePrimitive` renders 0 px in 2D/COLUMBUS_VIEW for this classifier, so WebGPU's lost 2D/CV coverage under the stencil path is the removal of a WebGPU-exceeds-upstream bonus, not a WebGL↔WebGPU regression. Fix only if a real 2D/CV classifier consumer ever needs it. (surfaced 2026-07-04 by the Q15R stencil fix). The stencil Z-fail classifier needs a clean stencil-testable *surface* depth to clip against. In SCENE3D the globe writes exactly that (parity, IoU ≥ 0.93). In SCENE2D / COLUMBUS_VIEW the reprojected-ENU map does not present a comparable Z-fail surface, so the Batch 178 (`NEW-CLASSIFIER-2D-CV-MORPH`) "WebGPU renders in 2D/CV" bonus regresses under the stencil path: SCENE2D under-marks to 0 px, COLUMBUS_VIEW over-marks the projected silhouette (~whole ROI). **This is NOT a WebGL↔WebGPU parity gap** — upstream WebGL `Vector3DTilePrimitive` renders NOTHING in 2D/CV for this classifier (measured 0 px), so the lost coverage is a WebGPU-exceeds-upstream bonus, not a required feature. `probe-vector3dtile-vctr.mjs` therefore treats the 2D/CV polygon frames as INFO-only (not gated).   - **SUN** (exact per-body integral, like the moon). `Sun.update` computes the camera→sun transmittance each frame (gated on `frameState.skyAtmosphereVisible`), publishes `frameState.sunAtmosphereExtinction`, and stores it on `sun._atmosphereExtinction`. WebGL `SunFS.glsl` multiplies the (gamma-corrected) sun color by `u_atmosphereExtinction`; WebGPU `SUN_SHADER_WGSL` multiplies by a new `extinction: vec3` (floats 28..30 in `packSunUniforms`). Each star's slant transmittance = `zenithTransmittance ^ airmass(elevation)`, `airmass = 1/max(sin elev, 1/38)` (plane-parallel Bouguer, capped at the ~38 Kasten-Young horizon limit). Applied per-star in the VS on both backends: WebGL `StarFieldVS.glsl` (uniforms `u_zenithTransmittance` + `u_cameraUpFixed`, dot with the fixed-frame star dir); WebGPU `StarField.wgsl` (uniforms `zenithTransmittance` + `cameraUpTeme` — camera up rotated into the TEME instance frame so `dot(directionFixed, cameraUpTeme)` === the same elevation sine; rotation-invariant, so both backends match). `zenithTransmittance == (1,1,1)` from orbit → `pow(1, airmass) === 1` → byte-identical.

- **NS-SUN-BLEND-MODE-DIVERGENCE** (surfaced 2026-07-10 by C7-SUN-STARS-EXTINCTION; Principle 9 follow-up; PRE-EXISTING, doc-only, independently schedulable). The sun/moon flare layer is composited with **different blend modes on the two backends**, so the now-extinguished low-horizon sun disc reads differently even though the extinction transmittance is at exact parity. **WebGL** (`Scene/Sun.js` ~line 310) draws the sun billboard with `BlendingState.ALPHA_BLEND` (`src.a × src + (1−src.a) × dst`): the dim red disc + its dark surrounding halo **replace** the sky, so the extinguished sun reads as a dim red disc sitting in a darkened patch of sky (see `probe-sun-stars-extinction-sun-webgl-horizon-low.png`). **WebGPU** (`Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUEnvironmentRenderer.js` lines 517-532, Batch 106 Slice 5c-B) draws the same flare with an **additive** blend (`src.a × src + 1 × dst`): the layer can only *brighten* the destination, so the dimmed sun fades to a faint pale glow over the sky and never darkens the surrounding halo (see `probe-sun-stars-extinction-sun-webgpu-horizon-low.png`). Both looked acceptable before extinction because a full-brightness white disc dominates either composite; extinction exposes the divergence at the dim end. **Fix (deferred):** bring the two backends to the same blend model — either (a) switch the WebGPU sun/moon flare pipeline to alpha blending to match the WebGL `ALPHA_BLEND` reference (requires the WGSL flare shader to output the halo in the alpha channel the way the GLSL path expects, and re-checking the moon flare which shares the same pipeline), or (b) confirm additive is the intended fork look and re-tune the WebGL path to match it. Either direction must stay **off-gate byte-identical** (the change only affects the flare composite, which is always drawn — verify the bright-sun case is unchanged) and be probe-verified against both PNGs. M effort. **Trace:** 2026-07-10.

- **C6-TPDF-DITHER-FINAL** — ✅ SHIPPED (2026-07-09, Campaign 6, WebGPU-only exceed-feature). Opt-in via `scene.ditherEnabled` (optional `scene.ditherStrength`, default ±1 LSB), wired through `WebGPUPostProcessStageCollection` → `pipeline.setTonemapDither()` (writes the 5th uniform float). **Off-gate byte-identical:** default OFF writes strength 0.0 → the added term is exactly `tri * 0 = 0` → frame bit-identical to pre-feature; no new pass/allocation (rides the existing tonemap stage). WebGL unaffected (WebGPU-only). **Verified** `probe-tpdf-dither.mjs` (HDR path, smooth sky strip): OFF distinctColors 99 / maxRun 10 → ON distinctColors 200 / maxRun 4 (banding broken), off-after-toggle frame hash IDENTICAL to OFF, 0 console errors, PNGs read. - **C6-TPDF-DITHER-SDR-PATH** (surfaced 2026-07-09 by C6-TPDF-DITHER-FINAL; Principle 9 follow-up). The shipped TPDF dither lives in the tonemap stage, which is **only enabled when `scene.highDynamicRange = true`** (the HDR post-process pipeline uses rgba16float ping-pong intermediates, so the sub-LSB dither survives in floating point until the final downcast to the 8-bit canvas). In the DEFAULT SDR pipeline the scene framebuffer is `bgra8unorm` (8-bit) — the sky/atmosphere gradients are quantized (and their banding baked) in the SCENE render **before** any post-process stage runs, so a post-tonemap dither cannot recover them. Closing the SDR path needs one of: (a) apply the dither at the point of 8-bit write inside the gradient-producing shaders (`SkyAtmosphere.wgsl` / `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` fog / `AerialPerspective.wgsl`) — scattered but exact; or (b) render the SDR scene to a higher-precision (rg11b10ufloat/rgba16float) target and dither at the final blit — one place but changes default memory/format and must stay byte-identical when off. Both are M effort and independently schedulable. Until then, banding reduction is HDR-only (documented in the shader comment + the tonemap-stage no-op in SDR). **Trace:** 2026-07-09.

- **C6-AERIAL-ELLIPSOID-SNAP** — ⛔ PREMISE DOES NOT REPRODUCE (investigated 2026-07-10, Campaign 6/7; reverted to a clean tree, no code shipped). Brief: port Takram three-geospatial (MIT) `correctGeometricError` into `AerialPerspective.wgsl` — snap the depth-reconstructed world position onto the analytic ellipsoid before the inscatter march to fix the far-zoom coarse-L0/L1-tile **horizon inscatter color error**. **Finding: the technique is effectively inert on Cesium's WebGPU globe.** Cesium tessellates every globe surface tile (incl. coarse LODs) to a 65×65 grid that tracks the analytic ellipsoid tightly, so the depth-reconstructed world positions are already on/above the analytic ellipsoid essentially everywhere. Two faithful ports were built + probed (`probe-aerial-ellipsoid-snap.mjs`, far view = 1200 km alt over 38.8°N, near view = 6 km): (1) **radial snap** onto the WGS84 analytic ellipsoid (latitude-aware; snapping to the scalar equatorial `innerRadius` sphere is wrong — it lifts ALL non-equatorial terrain outward by km) fired on a thin limb sliver only and changed the along-ray march distance negligibly (maxD 0.001, 0 pixels above 6/255) because a radial move at the grazing horizon is nearly perpendicular to the view ray; (2) **ray↔ellipsoid intersection snap** (the geometrically correct "put the fragment on the analytic surface along the ray") changed only ~13 limb pixels by maxD 0.010 (~2.5/255). Both are visually a no-op. A shader tint confirmed the undershoot gate fires only on a ~few-hundred-pixel limb sliver. **The visible far-zoom horizon banding is a DIFFERENT root cause:** the bright bands follow the **tile grid** (rectangular per-tile blocks near the limb), i.e. per-tile depth-discontinuity / low-step (`INSCATTER_STEPS = 10`) march quantization at LOD-tile boundaries — NOT a radial geometric-error undershoot. **Real fixes to schedule instead:** (a) raise/jitter `INSCATTER_STEPS` or add a per-pixel march-start dither in `AerialPerspective.wgsl` (ties into C6-TPDF-DITHER-SDR-PATH's "dither the gradient producer" option-a); (b) investigate the per-tile depth discontinuity feeding `eyeDistance` at coarse-LOD tile seams. The scaffolding for the snap (an opt-in `scene.aerialPerspectiveEllipsoidSnap` flag on a spare `froxelParams.z` bit + an appended `ellipsoidRadii` UBO vec4) is trivial to re-add if a future renderer path (e.g. Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles or a genuinely coarse mesh) produces real geometric error — but it buys nothing on the tessellated globe today. **Trace:** 2026-07-10.

- **C6-FFT-OCEAN** — ✅ SHIPPED v1 (2026-07-11, Campaign 6/7, WebGPU-only exceed-feature; closes the deferred WATER "GPU FFT spectral ocean" gap — zero ocean-surface geometry existed before). A GPU FFT spectral ocean: a per-frame compute chain synthesizes an animated wave displacement + foam map from a Tessendorf/Phillips spectrum, and a camera-anchored RTE ENU grid patch samples it to render a displaced, Fresnel-shaded ocean surface with Jacobian foam. Compute chain (single 256×256 cascade): `OceanInitialSpectrum.wgsl` h0(k)/conj(h0(-k)) (once/on-param-change) → `OceanTwiddle.wgsl` butterfly index+factor LUT (once) → `OceanTimeSpectrum.wgsl` time-evolve h(k,t)=h0·e^{iwt}+conj(h0(-k))·e^{-iwt} into packed Dy+iDx and Dz complex fields (per frame) → `OceanIFFT.wgsl` log2(N) horizontal + log2(N) vertical radix-2 butterfly stages ×2 fields (ping-pong rg32float, per-stage compute passes so writes sync) → `OceanMerge.wgsl` (-1)^(x+y) fftshift correct + 1/N normalize → filterable rgba16float (λ·Dx, Dy, λ·Dz, foam). `OceanSurface.wgsl` VS displaces a 200×200-quad grid patch (grid∈[-0.5,0.5]×patchExtent, world-anchored UV=ENU/L, curvature drop −d²/2R, RTE anchor via EncodedCartesian3 high/low + mvpRelativeToEye — never absolute f32 position) and FS shades finite-diff normal + Schlick Fresnel (F0=0.02) + Blinn sun specular + Jacobian foam, wave-detail faded over the B630 70 km→1e6 m handover band. **License:** FFT butterfly + spectrum packing derived from gasgiant/FFT-Ocean, Popov72/OceanDemo, WebTide (all MIT, attributed in file headers); Phillips spectrum derived from Tessendorf's published SIGGRAPH notes. FFT sign/index conventions CPU-validated against a brute-force IDFT before porting (butterfly output == unnormalized IDFT, no fftshift permutation; the (-1)^(x+y) is only for the centered-spectrum indexing used here). **Opt-in default-off / byte-identical:** `scene.globe.water.ocean.enabled` (default false) lazily creates one `OceanSurfacePrimitive` and adds it to `scene.primitives`; nothing is allocated/dispatched/drawn until enabled; disabling removes+destroys it (frees all GPU textures). `FeatureRendererKey.FFT_OCEAN=53` (COUNT 53→54, add-only) registered via LAZY loader in `WebGPUFeatureRenderers.ts`; `ShaderSourceId.OCEAN_SURFACE=41` (add-only, LOG_DEPTH ifdef). WebGL contexts never register the FR → `OceanSurfacePrimitive.update` early-returns on `!context.isWebGPU` (documented no-op, Principle 2/10). **Verified** `Tools/visual-regression/probe-fft-ocean.mjs` (WebGPU, fresh-load deterministic sessions): OFF-gate off1-vs-off2(toggle) delta **0.0** == base noise-floor off1-vs-off1b **0.0** (byte-identical, no residue); isolated (globe.show=false) coverage OFF **0** → ON **0.553** (patch renders against empty scene); isolated temporal delta **42.7** (waves animate); foam white crest-streaks visible; 0 black/NaN; PNGs read (iso-on = deep-blue choppy FFT sea with foam on the folds — unambiguously spectral, not Gerstner). **v1 follow-ups (Principle 9, all independently schedulable):** (1) `C6-FFT-OCEAN-JONSWAP-TMA` — upgrade the Phillips spectrum to JONSWAP+TMA with Horvath-2015 directional spreading + dual wind-sea/swell layers (research §2 has the WGSL from Popov72, MIT); (2) `C6-FFT-OCEAN-CASCADES` — 3-cascade hard-partitioned k-space (L={250,17,5}) for cm→250 m coverage vs the single 250 m tile (visible tiling today); (3) `C6-FFT-OCEAN-CLIPMAP` — replace the single flat patch with camera-anchored clipmap rings out to ~200 km + LOD (the single ~3 km patch is only visible from low altitude); (4) `C6-FFT-OCEAN-SPECTRAL-NORMALS` — spectral (ik) derivatives + slope-variance→roughness mips instead of the current 1-texel finite-diff FS normal (grainy/aliased at fine detail); (5) `C6-FFT-OCEAN-WATERMASK-SEAM` — actually suppress the B630 terrain water-mask specular under the opaque ocean patch (currently both draw; z-buffer arbitrates but at grazing angles they can double-specular); (6) `C6-PLANAR-REFLECT-REFRACT` (queue #20, already gated on this) — the `OceanSurface.wgsl` FS has the reflection/sky seam pre-built (samples a sky gradient today); wire the mirrored reflection camera + oblique-clip target; (7) `NEW-FFT-OCEAN-WEBGL2-FALLBACK` — dli/waves (MIT) proves a WebGL2 fragment-FFT is feasible; the scene-side primitive + all math are backend-agnostic. Files: `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOceanRenderer.ts` (new), `Shaders/WebGPU/Ocean/{OceanInitialSpectrum,OceanTwiddle,OceanTimeSpectrum,OceanIFFT,OceanMerge,OceanSurface}.wgsl` (new), `Scene/OceanSurfacePrimitive.js` (new), `Scene/GlobeWaterOcean.js` (new), `Scene/GlobeWater.js` (+`ocean` sub-facade getter), `Renderer/FeatureRendererKey.js`, `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUShaderDefines.ts`, `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUFeatureRenderers.ts`, `Tools/visual-regression/probe-fft-ocean.mjs` (new). **Trace:** 2026-07-06 (R-FFT-OCEAN research) → 2026-07-11 (shipped v1).

- **C6-FSR2-UPSCALE** (NEW-FSR2-UPSCALE) — ⏸️ **DEFERRED (premise verified REAL; investigated 2026-07-11, Campaign 6/7, no code shipped — clean tree).** Queue #22 (`QUEUE_2026-07-06_CAMPAIGN7.md`), rated L/epic. Full research register at `RESEARCH_R-FSR2_2026-07-06.md` (license MIT verbatim-verified, pass table, formats, jitter formula, R/D re-pointing checklist). **Premise verification (NOT stale):** grep for `fsr2|superResolution|renderResolutionScale|internalRes|renderWidth|FidelityFX` across `packages/engine/Source` → **zero hits**; there is exactly ONE resolution today (everything derives from `context.drawingBufferWidth/Height`), no internal-res(R)/output-res(D) split, no upscale pass. The reuse anchors the research names all exist and were re-confirmed: `WebGPUTAAEffect.ts` (halton still exported even though TAA itself uses IGN since Batch 195); velocity MRT `_velocityTexture`/`_runVelocityPass` in `WebGPUSceneFramebuffer.ts`/`WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts`; the Scene.js jitter hook `taa.computeJitter`→`taa.applyProjectionJitter` at `Scene.js` ~5564–5581 (absolute-write base-capture pattern); DP-H41 `previousViewProjection`; and `FEAT-SURVEY-48 STP upscaler` still in FEATURE_INVENTORY §D line 998 (FSR2 supersedes it on landing). **Why deferred (not force-landed):** the research itself scopes this at **6–10 days across 4 phases** and it fails the single-task acceptance bar on three independent axes, none self-contained: (1) **6 dense GLSL→WGSL compute-shader ports** (LuminancePyramid/SPD, ReconstructPreviousDepth&Dilate, DepthClip, Lock, Reproject&Accumulate, +RCAS) from the FSR2 v2.2.2 GLSL set — Accumulate + the `ffx_a.h`/`ffx_fsr2_common` helper library alone are ~3–4k lines of dense temporal-resolve math whose correctness (no motion ghosting, no thin-feature washout) can only be judged by a converged multi-frame probe, not a typecheck; (2) a **known-hard WGSL rewrite** — ReconstructPreviousDepth scatters with `InterlockedMax/Min` on an `r32uint` UAV *texture*, and WGSL has **no texture atomics**, so it must be re-architected as a reusable `var<storage> array<atomic<u32>>` scatter-buffer helper (subtle indexing/read-back, must be built as a real artifact not an inline hack per the no-shortcuts rule); (3) a **17-subsystem internal-res/output-res split refactor** with a *silent picking-breakage* risk — the R/D split must re-point Scene.js viewport + jitter dims, `WebGPUContext` depth texture, `WebGPUSceneFramebuffer` (color/id/velocity/refraction), GlobeDepth, OIT, InvertClassification, TranslucentTileClassification, EdgeFramebuffer, Hi-Z pyramid, **PickFramebuffer + pick-coordinate scaling** (canvas-px→R-px in pick/pickPosition/drillPick readback — off-by-one here breaks picking with no visible symptom), and every pre-upscale PP stage + ping-pong, cloud/volumetric-fog/weather targets, while keeping Tonemap/ColorGrading/blit at D. Plus a **fork-specific prep pass** (`FSR2Prep.wgsl`: camera-motion MV synthesis from depth+previous-VP_RTE for globe/terrain/primitives which the velocity MRT does NOT cover, log-depth→linear-r32f linearize because Cesium log depth breaks FSR2's Akeley depth-clip constants, and reactive-mask merge). None of these is a shippable slice on its own: Phase-1 plumbing lands byte-identical-when-off but the acceptance probe requires the feature to **render when ON**, and there is no FSR2 to enable until Phases 2–3 also land — so a single-task landing is either half-a-refactor (broken tree) or a non-FSR2 naive-upscale masquerade (violates the full-feature rule). **Recommended phasing for a dedicated multi-batch run (each lands green with feature off):** (P1) R/D split through a new `renderResolutionScale` (4th `ensureResources` recreate trigger) + Scene viewport/jitter dims + pick-coord scaling → FSR2 off ⇒ R==D ⇒ byte-identical, independently auditable, ≈half the effort; (P2) `FSR2Prep.wgsl` MV-synthesis + log-depth-linearize + reactive target, standalone debug-visualizable; (P3) FP32 (`FFX_HALF=0`) ports of passes 0–4 + RCAS, Quality 1.5× preset, atomic-scatter storage-buffer helper, `probe-fsr2-*.mjs` (SSIM/mismatch-% vs native-res WebGPU + `gpuPassCost` timing, NOT byte parity); (P4) OIT/cloud reactive-mask writers → Balanced/Performance presets → `_f16` variants / subgroup-SPD. **Off-gate contract (for the eventual land):** `scene.fsr2Enabled` default **false** ⇒ no R/D split (R==D), no target allocation, no pass, byte-identical; mutually exclusive with TAA + FXAA at runtime (one-time warn); WGSL-only under the Principle-5 compute exemption (WebGL2 has no compute → WebGL warns + no-ops, byte-identical); add-only `ShaderDefine` bits for the f16 variants (module-cache key masks 24 bits — bits ≥24 need the Batch-476 keySalt). **License:** PORT FidelityFX-FSR2 v2.2.2 (MIT, verbatim-verified) → WGSL, retaining the AMD copyright+permission header in every derived `Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/FSR2/*.wgsl` + `WebGPUFSR2*.ts` file and adding a third-party manifest entry; reference the MIT-retained JuanDiegoMontoya/FidelityFX-FSR2-OpenGL port for pitfalls. **Files (projected):** `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUFSR2Effect.ts` + `WebGPUFSR2Resources.ts` (new), `Shaders/WebGPU/PostProcess/FSR2/{FSR2Common,FSR2LuminancePyramid,FSR2ReconstructDilate,FSR2DepthClip,FSR2Lock,FSR2Accumulate,FSR2Rcas,FSR2Prep}.wgsl` (new), plus edits to `WebGPUSceneRendererEnsureResources.ts`, `WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts`, `WebGPUContext.ts`, `WebGPUSceneFramebuffer.ts`, `WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts`, `WebGPUPickFramebuffer.ts`, `Scene/Scene.js` (jitter dims + `fsr2Enabled`/`fsr2QualityMode`/`fsr2Sharpness`), `WebGPUShaderDefines.ts`, and pre-upscale PP/cloud/fog resize dims; `Tools/visual-regression/probe-fsr2-upscale.mjs` (new). On landing: move FEAT-SURVEY-48 §D→§B as NEW-FSR2-UPSCALE; add DEFERRED entries for T&C mask, autogen-reactive, Ultra-Perf 3.0×, subgroup-SPD. **Effort:** L/epic, 6–10 days, 4 phases. **Trace:** 2026-07-05 (mine, THREEJS_TECH_MINE #2 / register) → 2026-07-06 (R-FSR2 research, GO) → 2026-07-11 (premise verified real, decomposition + phasing recorded; deferred as a multi-batch epic per the honest-partial / clean-tree rule).

- **C6-PLANAR-REFLECT-REFRACT** — ⏸️ **UNBLOCKED-BUT-DEFERRED (premise re-verified REAL + gate now GREEN; investigated 2026-07-11, Campaign 6/7, no code shipped — clean tree).** Queue #20 (`QUEUE_2026-07-06_CAMPAIGN7.md`) rated M/epic and gated behind #19 (FFT ocean) with an explicit "SKIP if FFT ocean not landed" rule. **Premise verification:** (a) NOT stale — no planar reflection exists. `OceanSurface.wgsl` FS (lines 153–158) reflects the sky with a crude *analytic* approximation only (`skyColor = mix(shallowColor, hardcoded (0.55,0.72,0.92), clamp(dot(reflectDir, up)))` blended by Schlick Fresnel); there is no reflection render pass, no oblique near-plane clip matrix, no projective reflection texture, and no per-surface `reflection` opt-in. The only "Reflection"-named file, `WebGPUBindGroupReflection.ts`, is Naga bind-group-layout *introspection*, unrelated. (b) **Gate is now GREEN** — the #19 dependency `C6-FFT-OCEAN` shipped Batch 654 (`08af2cd678`), so the SKIP condition no longer applies; this item is genuinely unblocked and ready to build as the next planned step. **Why deferred (not force-landed):** a faithful three.js-`Reflector` planar reflection is a multi-day *scene-renderer-orchestration* epic in the most intricate subsystem, NOT a self-contained feature-renderer change, and could not be landed verified-green within a single task's budget. The specific structural blocker: the ocean FR emits a **deferred** `WebGPUDrawCommand` via `frameState.commandList.push` (`WebGPUOceanRenderer.ts` ~L977–986, `Pass.OPAQUE`) that the scene renderer executes *later* — so the reflection texture must be produced by a reflected-camera globe/sky re-render **before** that deferred draw runs, which means hooking the 4505-line `WebGPUSceneRenderer` frame orchestration (a camera-snapshot/repoint/restore + offscreen render), not the primitive's `update()`. **Concrete design for the next campaign (reuses proven machinery):** (1) Add opt-in `reflection` option to `OceanSurfacePrimitive` (default off → byte-identical; no target allocated, no extra pass when off). (2) Build the reflected virtual camera by mirroring the main camera across the ocean's local tangent plane at the anchor (`_anchor` + `_up` normal, both already computed each frame), and apply a **Lengyel oblique near-plane clip** (the water plane in eye space) so sub-surface geometry is clipped out of the reflection — the classic Reflector/Water technique. (3) Produce the reflection color target by REUSING the exact reflected-camera re-render pattern already proven in `WebGPUDynamicEnvironmentMapCapture.runSceneCapture` (snapshot `uniformState.camera` proxy fields → repoint to the reflected+oblique camera → ask the globe renderer to build its OWN draw commands → render into the reflection target with `loadOp:'clear'` to the sky fill → restore the main camera in a `finally`, honoring the same `_logDepthEncodeNearFar` stash caveat the capture documents). Single target (one reflected view), not 6 cube faces — cheaper than the env capture. (4) Bind the reflection texture + the reflection view-proj matrix into `OceanSurface.wgsl`; replace the analytic `skyColor` seam (already Fresnel-mixed at L156–158 — the "reflection seam is pre-built" note in C6-FFT-OCEAN follow-up #6) with a **projective** sample of the reflection target (clip→uv), keeping the analytic gradient as the `//>>else`/fallback so `defines=0` stays byte-identical. RTE-correct the projective coords (never an absolute f32 world position). (5) `Refractor`/`Water2` (BSD/MIT) flow-map river advection + screen-space refraction (`C6-SCREEN-SPACE-REFRACT`, queue #24, D, reuses the Hi-Z/scene-depth/scene-color SSR targets) are a *second* increment on top — schedule after the reflection pass lands. **Off-gate contract:** opt-in default-off, byte-identical when off (no target, no pass, no bind-group change on the existing ocean pipeline — gate the new bindings behind a `ShaderDefine` add-only bit + a `//>>else` analytic fallback); WebGPU-only (WebGL never registers the ocean FR → documented no-op, Principle 2/10). **Acceptance probe (to author):** flat ocean patch at low altitude over a coastline; ON = the reflection target shows terrain/sky mirrored with the oblique clip removing below-water geometry (distinguishable from the analytic gradient by reflecting actual terrain silhouettes); OFF = byte-identical to pre-feature (0.0 vs noise floor). **License:** PORT three.js `Reflector`/`Refractor`/`Water`/`Water2` (MIT) with attribution; Lengyel oblique-clip is a published technique (derive). **Files (projected):** `Scene/OceanSurfacePrimitive.js` (+`reflection` option), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUOceanRenderer.ts` (reflection target + reflected-camera pass wiring), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts` (pre-ocean reflection re-render hook, mirrors `runSceneCapture`), `Shaders/WebGPU/Ocean/OceanSurface.wgsl` (projective reflection sample behind a new add-only `ShaderDefine`), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUShaderDefines.ts` (add-only bit), `Tools/visual-regression/probe-planar-reflect.mjs` (new). **Effort:** multi-day (large). **Trace:** 2026-07-05 (mine, THREEJS_TECH_MINE #22) → 2026-07-11 (premise re-verified real, gate green, decomposition recorded; deferred per the queue's gated-tail honest-partial rule).

- **C9-10-CONSUMER-DRIVEN-MRT** (`FAR-403-C0`, queue #27, R3) — ⏸️ **DEFERRED / BLOCKED (premise verified REAL; investigated 2026-07-16, Campaign 9; no code shipped — clean tree).** Goal: make the scene-FB G-buffer/MRT topology demand-driven so a DEFAULT scene (no G-buffer consumer) reports **zero** normal/G-buffer bytes, zero MSAA companion bytes, and zero slot-1 resolves, while any consumer (deferred-lighting/SSR/NPR/contact-shadow/SSGI/debug-overlay) toggled on — independently AND in combination — restores exact MRT bytes with per-consumer pixel parity, preserving HDR/MSAA/resize/device-loss/TAA/pick/classification. **Premise verification (NOT stale — CONFIRMED gap):** `_mrtMode` in `WebGPUSceneFBTargetHelpers.ts:71` is hardcoded `true` at declaration and `setSceneFBMrtMode()` has **zero runtime callers** (grep: only doc-comment mentions) — the topology never flips, so the ~16 MB rgba16float G-buffer (+MSAA companion + resolve) is allocated and bound on EVERY non-pick frame regardless of demand. C9-09 (`FAR-401-C0`, landed 2026-07-16) already built the authoritative per-frame demand record: `computeAttachmentDemand()` → `context._attachmentDemand` with `gbufferDemanded`, and `context.forceSceneMRT` defaults `true` (conservative always-MRT). The executor is ALREADY topology-parametric on `isSceneFBMrtMode()`: the G-buffer alloc site (`WebGPUContext.updateAndClearFramebuffers` ~L3964), the pass-open slot-1 builder (`WebGPUSceneRendererPassRedirect.buildMrtSlot1Attachment` — returns null when mode off, all three scene-pass-open sites funnel through it), and every pipeline's target array (`makeSceneFBTargets` returns length-1 vs length-2 by mode). So the "act on the record" wiring (gate alloc on `gbufferDemanded`, `setSceneFBMrtMode(gbufferDemanded)` before pipelines build each frame, flip `forceSceneMRT` default to false) is individually small. **Why deferred (not force-landed — the acceptance's toggle requirement is the blocker):** a correct mid-session flip is a large cross-cutting change across **31 renderers** with NO flip-safety scaffolding, and a partial landing would break rendering on the exact consumer-toggle path the acceptance mandates. Concrete break: `_mrtMode` is a module-global consumed at pipeline-BUILD time by 31 renderers that call `makeSceneFBTargets`, but each renderer caches its built pipeline under its OWN key that does NOT include an MRT-topology dimension — e.g. the whole `WebGPUCollectionRendererBase` family (billboard/label/point/polyline) keys via `pipelineKeyWithDepthFlag(defines, noDepthTest)` (`WebGPUCollectionRendererBase.ts:208`), a Uint32 whose bits 0-30 are ShaderDefine and bit 31 is `NO_DEPTH_TEST_PIPELINE_KEY_BIT` — **no free bit for topology**. Session starts default (`_mrtMode` false) → collection renderers cache 1-target pipelines; user enables SSR → mode flips true, pass becomes 2-attachment, but the per-renderer cache returns the stale 1-target pipeline → "attachment state not compatible" validation error → black/broken frame. (Only the GENERIC `WebGPURenderPipelineCache.generateCacheKey` is already topology-safe — its `tg:` signature at L721-732 folds the target-array shape — but the 31 per-renderer/model/globe/ocean/voxel/gsplat/etc. caches are not.) The queue row's own phrasing "**Cache exact one-target/MRT variants**" is precisely this: every scene-FB pipeline cache must key BOTH variants by topology (or a global flush-on-flip broadcast must reach all 31 renderers — none exists today). **Additional gating:** queue §3 states "Attachment topology … wait for Gate B unless an explicit gate amendment records why the slice is correctness-independent"; this slice is NOT correctness-independent (it changes frame topology with a feature-break-on-toggle risk), and Gate B is not cleanly passed (the Gate-B item `C9-02A` is PARTIAL/PAUSED and spawned `NEW-WEBGPU-HDR-PICK-FORMAT-CLOSURE` + `NEW-WEBGPU-ASYNC-PICK-PIPELINE-READINESS-CONTRACT`). **Recommended phasing for a dedicated multi-batch run (each lands green, byte-identical when no consumer):** (P0) add a topology dimension to the pipeline-cache key of EVERY scene-FB renderer — widen the collection-family key past 32 bits (`` `${defines}:${mrt}` `` or a safe-int fold, since bits 0-31 are full) and audit each of the 31 `makeSceneFBTargets` callers (billboard, label, point, polyline, buffer-point/polygon/polyline, cloud, compute-instance, cubemap-panorama, depth-plane, derived-command, edge-visibility, ellipsoid, environment, flow-field, gaussian-splat, ground-polyline, ground-primitive, model-pipeline-cache, ocean, point-cloud + EDL, primitive-commands, sky-atmosphere, starfield, vector3d-{clamped-polylines,polylines,primitive}, voxel, weather) so BOTH the 1-target and 2-target pipeline are cacheable and selected by the current mode — verify via a probe that toggles a consumer mid-session with zero validation errors; lands byte-identical because default is still forced-MRT. (P1) gate the G-buffer alloc + MSAA companion + resolve on `context._attachmentDemand.gbufferDemanded` and call `setSceneFBMrtMode(gbufferDemanded)` in `updateAndClearFramebuffers` before any pipeline builds — still with `forceSceneMRT` default true, so still byte-identical but now the machinery is demand-wired. (P2) flip `WebGPUContext.forceSceneMRT` default to false so no-consumer frames drop to one-target and report ZERO bytes; run the full acceptance matrix — per-consumer independently + combinations (SSR/NPR/contact/deferred/SSGI/debug), plus HDR/MSAA1&4/resize/device-loss/TAA(msaa1 velocity path)/pick(single-target already)/classification — each with pixel parity vs pre-change and READ PNGs; report the moving-route p95 delta (G-buffer alloc+clear+resolve bandwidth is the named saved stage). **Off-gate contract:** with `forceSceneMRT` true (or any consumer on) output is byte-identical to today; with it false and no consumer, `getAttachmentDemandStats()` reports `gbufferBytes=0`, `gbufferMsaaCompanionBytes=0`, `slot1ResolveOpens=0`, `sceneColorAttachmentCount=1`, `recordMatchesActual=true`. **NEVER** achieve the zero-bytes result by hardcoding `_mrtMode=false` (that is feature removal — breaks every consumer). **Files (projected):** `WebGPUSceneFBTargetHelpers.ts`, `WebGPUContext.ts`, `WebGPUCollectionRendererBase.ts` (+the key widening) and the per-cache key of the 31 renderers above, `WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts`, `WebGPUGlobeSurfacePipelines.ts`; `Tools/visual-regression/probe-consumer-driven-mrt.mjs` (new, extends `probe-attachment-demand-registry.mjs`). **Effort:** L/epic, multi-batch (P0 alone is the bulk — 31-renderer cache-key audit). **Trace:** 2026-07-16 (C9-10 investigation — premise verified real vs live code; blocked on the absent per-renderer topology-keyed cache scaffolding + Gate-B gating; decomposition recorded per honest-partial / clean-tree rule).

- **C9-11-RETAINED-TERRAIN-DESCRIPTORS** (`FAR-309`, queue #29, R2) — 🟡 **PARTIAL / PAUSED (verified byte-identical closure core LANDED; descriptor/wrapper/array retention deferred; investigated + core landed 2026-07-16, Campaign 9).** FAR-309 is the campaign's biggest single hot-path lever: the WebGPU terrain path allocates, per warm frame, one `readyLayers` array + one `commands` array + per-pass `passLayers` slices + one `TileDrawDescriptor` per pass (`WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.createTileCommands`, ~39,300 across the 1,189-frame audited route, ≈33/frame) and, in the caller `GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.addWebGPUDrawCommandsForTile`, one command-wrapper object **plus one `execute: function(renderPass){…}` closure** per pass per tile (color) and again per pick command. **Premise verified live first:** the churn is real and unchanged (bind-group cache 99.66% hits and pipeline/tile-buffer caches already retain those; the raw per-tile array/descriptor/wrapper/closure OBJECT allocations do not). **Core landed (this task):** both `execute` bodies (color at the old `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer`-consumer L1071 and pick at L1143 in `GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js`) close over **nothing but `this`** — they read only `this._pipeline/_bindGroups/_bindGroup0DynamicOffsets/_vertexBuffer/_indexBuffer/_indexFormat/_indexCount`. Both bodies were byte-identical, so they were hoisted to ONE module-level `executeWebGPUGlobeTileCommand(renderPass)` shared by every color + pick globe tile command (and the wireframe path, which funnels through the same wrapper loop). All call sites invoke `command.execute(renderPass)` method-style, so `this` still binds to the command → **byte-identical behavior**, eliminating every per-frame globe-tile execute-closure allocation (~39,300 across the 1,189-frame audited route, ≈33/frame — the named "execute closures per tile/pass" allocation class) with zero feature/visual change. *(Correction 2026-07-17, close-out audit: the original wording here and in the Batch-682 commit message read the C9-01 figure of ~39,300 as per-frame; it is the route TOTAL over 1,189 frames.)* **Verified:** `npx eslint`/`npx tsc --noEmit`/`npx gulp build` clean; `capture-and-diff globe-default` crossBackend PASS 0.46% (in the established C9-13 0.43–0.77% band; WebGPU + diff PNGs read — correct SF-Bay terrain, diff essentially black/chrome-only); the 9-waypoint moving `probe-camera-track` route (orbit→descent→city→near-ground→literal ground→himalaya) all waypoints green with **zero** console/page/device errors — diffs 0.077–0.091% at orbit (pre-existing atmosphere/chrome delta, unchanged), **0% at descend-sierra/descend-sf-coast/low-oblique/city**, 0.011%/0.017% near-ground/ground, 0.005% himalaya; ground-level + full-detail PNGs read (correct terrain, no artifacts). The pre-existing `probe-clipping-planes-parity` FAIL (a MODEL clip/pick probe, unrelated to globe tiles) was confirmed identical on a stash+rebuild clean baseline — not caused by this change. **Deferred remainder (the larger lever, NOT landed):** retaining the `TileDrawDescriptor` objects, the command-wrapper objects, and the per-tile `readyLayers`/`commands`/`passLayers` scratch spans across warm frames, keyed by an exact revision tuple (mesh/content, imagery set+order, scene mode, water, clipping/shadows, effect generation, HDR/MSAA/log-depth topology, device generation) with camera/frustum values updated in place via the ring's dynamic offsets. **Why deferred:** the per-frame-changing field `_bindGroup0DynamicOffsets` (camera+tile UB ring slice, new offset every frame) and the non-3D fresh `BoundingSphere` mean a retained wrapper must still mutate per-frame fields; the marginal object-allocation saving over the already-landed closure hoist is real but small **relative to the correctness risk** — a retained per-tile wrapper introduces a multi-view aliasing hazard (the same tile rendered into two same-device views/cameras within one frame would clobber another view's offsets/derived-pick/translucency commands) and stale-pipeline/stale-derived-command hazards on format-generation flips (HDR/MSAA/log-depth) and translucency/pick topology changes — exactly the "never visually-weaken a feature for a metric" and multi-view exactness the C9 charter forbids getting wrong. A correct retention needs a per-(renderer-instance = per-device)-keyed per-tile-per-pass packet cache with an explicit revision-tuple invalidation, per-frame in-place dynamic-offset + non-3D-BV update, and derived-command (translucency/pick) staleness handling — a dedicated multi-batch slice with its own 9-waypoint + water/clipping/shadow/exaggeration/2D-CV-morph + multi-view + device-loss acceptance matrix. **Off-gate:** the landed closure hoist is byte-identical by construction (no toggle; it always renders identically). **Files (landed):** `Scene/GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js` (hoisted `executeWebGPUGlobeTileCommand` + two call-site refs). **Files (projected for the remainder):** `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts` (retained descriptor packets + revision keys), `Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTypes.ts`, `Scene/GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js` (retained wrapper cache + in-place per-frame field update), `Tools/visual-regression/probe-retained-terrain-descriptors.mjs` (new). **Effort:** remainder = L/epic, multi-batch. **Trace:** 2026-07-16 (C9-11 — premise verified real vs live code; byte-identical closure core landed + verified; wrapper/descriptor/array retention deferred per honest-partial / clean-tree rule).

- **C9-12-TERRAIN-STATIC-DYNAMIC-UPLOAD-SPLIT** (`FAR-303`, queue #30, R2) — ⏸️ **DEFERRED / BLOCKED (premise verified REAL; investigated 2026-07-16, Campaign 9; no code shipped — clean tree).** Goal: separate stable per-tile/material UB bytes from per-view/per-frustum ring data so changed tiles only rewrite their own ranges and per-frame upload calls AND bytes fall with no stale multi-view or mode data. Acceptance: API-lane writeBuffer bytes/frame drop materially from the ~112.9 KB / 10.03 writes-per-frame Gate-A baseline on settled frames, multi-view + mode-switch + mutation correctness green. **Premise verification (NOT stale — CONFIRMED gap):** the packers still stage the FULL uniform width per tile per imagery pass through the ring every frame — `createCameraUniformBufferHelper` (`WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:1348`) packs `CAMERA_UNIFORM_FLOATS = 232` (928 B → 1024 aligned) and `createTileUniformBufferHelper` (`:1358`) packs `TILE_UNIFORM_FLOATS = 484` (1936 B → 2048 aligned) = **3072 B staged/tile/pass**, both routed through `writeUniformSlice → context.uniformAllocator.allocateAndWrite` (`WebGPUGlobeSurfaceCameraUB.ts:1028`, `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileUB.ts`). C9-01 measured 39,300 descriptors × 3072 B ≈ **115.1 MiB** aligned staging over the route; the ring coalesces this into ~112.9 KB of `queue.writeBuffer`/frame. No static/dynamic split, no persistent per-tile static slab, and no revision-keyed skip exist in live code. The counters `cameraUniformAlignedBytes`/`tileUniformAlignedBytes` (`:1373`/`:1380`) confirm both packs run unconditionally every pass. **Why blocked as a single session (fundamental coupling, not a shortcut gap):** every byte-reducing approach reduces to one of two, and both are epic-scale or forbidden. (A) **The intended lever — WGSL static/dynamic struct split + shared static slab:** split the single group-0 `CameraUniforms`+`TileUniforms` into `ViewUniforms` (per-view, packed once/frame), `TileDynamicUniforms` (`modifiedModelView`/`modifiedModelViewProjection` — the irreducible f64 `view × mesh.center` RTE product, ~128 B → 256 aligned/tile/frame via the ring), and `TileStaticUniforms` (center3D hi/lo, scaleAndBias, minMaxHeight, projected tileRectangle/mercatorY, per-imagery-revision layer blocks, water-mask TS, flags — written to a persistent slab via `queue.writeBuffer` ONLY on a per-tile revision miss). This is the ~12× per-tile upload cut. It requires editing `GlobeTerrain.wgsl` (~3300 lines) group-0 struct declarations + EVERY field access, `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceLayouts.ts` BGL 0, every pipeline layout, `_getOrCreateBindGroup0`, and the shared wireframe (`createWireframeTileCommands`) + env-capture (`getOrCreateCaptureTileCommands`, which also calls `_getOrCreateBindGroup0`) + pick vertex-stage paths — a single atomic bytes-on-wire slice that must be pixel-identical across all scenes and revert as one clean commit. (B) **Per-tile persistent full buffers (no WGSL change):** storing each tile's full UB in its own persistent `GPUBuffer` and skipping re-upload when unchanged would break the healthy 99.66%-hit group-0 bind-group cache — that cache keys on (camera-page, tile-page) buffer IDENTITY with byte offsets riding as dynamic offsets (Batch 292); one persistent buffer per tile means one bind-group create per tile, regressing the exact cache the campaign relies on. Forbidden by rule (never regress a working path for a metric). Only a shared static slab with dynamic offsets (option A) keeps one buffer identity — and that needs the struct split. **The deeper blocker:** knowing WHICH tiles' static bytes changed (to rewrite only their slab ranges) is exactly the exact-revision-key per-tile packet store of `C9-11` Slice 1, whose retained-descriptor/wrapper/array foundation is itself **DEFERRED** (see the C9-11 entry above — landed only the byte-identical execute-closure hoist; the revision-keyed packet cache with the full invalidation tuple is unbuilt). C9-12's static-slab write-gate consumes that revision key; without it there is no correct signal for "this tile's static block is unchanged," and a wrong signal is silent visual corruption (stale imagery UV transforms, frozen ocean waves if `TIME_OFFSET` is misclassified as static, stale exaggeration/clipping). Additionally, the win is on MOVING frames (settled frames already re-stage identical bytes the ring could in principle skip, but the acceptance's "settled frames" reduction still needs the same revision machinery). **Recommended phasing for a dedicated multi-batch run (each lands green + byte-identical off-path; mirrors the execution-guide G6 slices 0–4):** (S0) effects-handle hoist — already landed as `C9-13`/`NEW-GLOBE-EFFECTS-PER-VIEW-PREPARED-HANDLE` (Batch 677); consume its `_getOrCreateFrameEffectsBindGroup` handle. (S1 = the C9-11 remainder) build the per-`GPUDevice`-renderer per-tile `TileRenderPacket` store keyed by the exact revision tuple (mesh `vertices` identity, ordered per-layer texture-view identity + TS/rect bytes + ready count, material type + wgsl source identity, scene mode, water-mask identity + TS + gates, clipping enabled/len/union + useClipDistances, shadow/CSM/cloud-shadow view identities, translucency structure, `_scenePipelineFormatGeneration` AND `_logDepthEnabled` separately, debug flags, device generation, skirt gate) with per-frame in-place refresh of dynamic offsets / non-3D bounding sphere / derived pick+translucency commands; MORPHING + any active debug mode + translucent globe fall back to the legacy per-frame path. (S2 — the WGSL slice) split `CameraUniforms` into `ViewUniforms` + `TileDynamicUniforms` + `TileStaticUniforms`, pack `ViewUniforms` once/frame (preserving the `uniformState._logDepthEncodeNearFar` stash side-effect every frame — depth-plane + classifiers depend on it), write `TileStaticUniforms` to a persistent slab (fixed 256-B slots, free-list, grow-by-page, slot lifetime tied to the `_tileBufferCache` entry with deferred-destroy ≥3 frames) only on packet miss. (S3) fold the `TileUniforms` static list into the slab; detect function-valued imagery `alpha/brightness/…` at pack time → per-frame fallback for that tile; keep `TIME_OFFSET`/fog/exaggeration/split/HSB/translucency-rect per-view (except the antimeridian-clipped `localizedTranslucencyRect`, which is per-tile-static-per-translucency-revision). (S4) sweep residual per-frame allocations + counters (`retainedPacketHits/Misses/Invalidations`, `staticTileBytesWritten`, `dynamicBytesWritten`) + `DEBUGGING_GUIDE.md` sync. **Verification the remainder owes (why it is not a single-session slice):** pixel-identical `capture-and-diff` all scenes; multi-view split-screen both halves; 2D/CV/MORPH; imagery add/remove/reorder/alpha-fade mid-flight; globe translucency on/off; clipping add/mutate/remove; shadows + CSM on/off; exaggeration change; `scene.msaaSamples` + HDR flip (topology generation); device-loss/multi-context; C9-02 terrain-ownership lanes unchanged; the moving multi-altitude camera-track perf lane ≥5% CPU-p95 in the named stage or >3× noise, no route-segment regression. **Off-gate:** with retention disabled (internal A/B `_useRetainedPackets`, or the fallback path) output is byte-identical to today; - **FUT-MULTI-BODY-ATMOSPHERE** — 🔭 **FUTURE (research complete, no code; recorded 2026-07-11, Campaign 7 close-out).** Subsystem 8 (Shadows/Lighting/Atmosphere). Full research register: `RESEARCH_R-MARS-ATMO_2026-07-06.md` (distilled in `RESEARCH_REGISTER_2026-07-06.md` §R-MARS-ATMO). Generalize the atmosphere pipeline from Earth-only to arbitrary celestial bodies (Mars first, airless Moon/Mercury as a gate). **Finding:** our WGSL LUT chain is **already ~80% per-body parameterized** (`AtmosphereParams` carries innerRadius/outerRadius/both scale heights/RGB Rayleigh-Mie-ozone/mieAnisotropy/intensity; no Earth radii hardcoded in the bake). **The actual blocking work list** = a short set of hardcoded Earth constants: (1) `ATMOSPHERE_THICKNESS = 111e3` hardcoded **twice** (`AtmosphereCommon.glsl:10` GLSL + `WebGPUSkyAtmosphereRenderer.js:102` JS) → `u_atmosphereThickness`/profile value, **parity-critical two-site change**; (2) `outerEllipsoidScale = 1.025` (`SkyAtmosphere.js:133`) → derive `1 + thickness/maxRadius`; (3) ozone tent center=25000/halfWidth=15000 (`AtmosphereLUT.wgsl:168-169`) → `absorptionLayerCenter/HalfWidth` params; (4) **no `groundAlbedo`** in the WGSL MS-gather/irradiance kernels (the one place new shader math lands — Bruneton ground-bounce term); (5) **no Mie extinction≠scattering (SSA) split**; (6) `Fog.js` Earth-tuned (gate by profile); (7) `mieAnisotropy` scalar → vec3 for Mars' per-λ blue sun-aureole. **Recommended landing shape:** add a frozen-preset `BodyAtmosphereProfile` value object (`EARTH` == today **byte-identical**, `MARS_STYLIZED` = Collienne-2013 inverted-Rayleigh `(19.918,13.57,5.75)e-6` zero-shader-change Tier-A, `MARS` = physically-grounded Tier-B needing the SSA/vec3-g/groundAlbedo extensions, `NONE` = airless gate — a `hasAtmosphere:false` boolean that skips the pass, NOT zeroed coefficients which still pay the full march). Do items (1)+(3) first as cheap independently-landable Earth-default-byte-identical de-riskers. Per-body LUT re-bake is nearly free (we already re-dispatch on sun-move/ozone-toggle; a body switch is one params-UBO swap, <1 ms; v1 = `lastProfileHash` re-bake key, v2 = per-body LRU slots ~1.4–1.7 MB/body). **Both backends** (Principle 5): WebGL params flow through existing uniforms once thickness is a uniform; no WebGL LUT needed. **License:** CLEAN — real prior art (Bruneton BSD-3, Hillaire/Epic MIT, Takram MIT+BSD-3+Apache stack, OpenSpace/Costa MIT, CosmoScout/Schneegans MIT) all permissive; **parameter VALUES are unprotectable facts** (our LUT chain is in-house so nothing is owed). Takram three-geospatial does NOT do multi-body (Earth-only per its own README); the real prior art is Costa 2021 + Schneegans 2024. **Pitfalls:** Bruneton-family coefficients are km⁻¹ (×10⁻³) vs our m⁻¹ (×10⁻⁶); Costa's published table has ~1000× errata; don't ship `multipleScattering:true` as a Mars default (inverted-order Rayleigh + physical MS = red-amplified horizon); the `AtmosphereLUTResources` "moon" slots are moonlight-IN-Earth's-sky (Batch 629), NOT a moon atmosphere — don't conflate. **Couplings:** SkyAtmosphere, Atmosphere/fog, ModelAtmosphereStage, moon-extinction (Batch 629), cloud Earth-METAR presets. **Probe (to author):** `probe-mars-atmo.mjs` split-screen Earth-vs-Mars low-sun saved view (Tier-A renders on both backends → WebGL-vs-WebGPU pixel diff is the parity gate). **Effort:** multi-slice; (1)+(3) are S, full Tier-B is M. **Trace:** 2026-07-06 (R-MARS-ATMO research) → 2026-07-11 (recorded as FUTURE at Campaign-7 close-out).

Octahedral impostor LOD for the **VOLUMETRIC** `CloudCollection` renderMode (distinct from the shipped `NEW-CLOUD-IMPOSTOR-FS-PARITY` billboard work). Full research register: `RESEARCH_R-IMPOSTOR_2026-07-06.md` (distilled in `RESEARCH_REGISTER_2026-07-06.md` §R-IMPOSTOR). **License:** CLEAN clean-room — octahedral mapping math is standard/uncopyrightable and **already ships in-repo under upstream Cesium Apache-2.0** (`Core/AttributeCompression.js` octEncode/Decode, `Builtin/Functions/octDecode.glsl`, `chunks/functions/csm_octDecode.js`) → zero new license surface; portable refs Godot-Octahedral-Impostors (MIT), SkyWorks/Harris (permissive UNC); **BLOCKED** ImpostorBaker (no license), Amplify (paid EULA), **NVIDIA STBN SDK (non-commercial** — self-generate masks, see R-STBN). **Key finding — this is a QUALITY/BATTERY/STABILITY tier, not the only orbit bridge:** Takram/Guerrilla prove orbit is viable by amortizing INSIDE the march (the cheap step-growth + far-cap already SHIPPED via Batch 641; true STBN + 1/16 amortization still owed via C6-CLOUD-STBN-TAAU). **Recommended TWO phases:** Phase 1 = single dynamic "freeze & reproject" impostor (reuse the existing half-res `rgba16float` premultiplied target + V10 shell-aware temporal reprojection; re-march only when a Harris-2001 staleness predicate trips: planet-centric view angle >~0.5°, resolution deficit, sun-delta, weather/wind hash, altitude-band change) → ~60× march-cost cut at orbit with ~90% existing infra. Default `cloudImpostorMode='off'` → byte-identical. 3D-scene-mode-only; never display unbaked cells (fall back to live march). **Pitfall:** frame SELECTION must be per-camera (planet-centric dir), never per-pixel (per-pixel triangle seams crawl across a planet-filling disc). **Probes (to author):** probe-cloud-impostor-off (byte-identical), -parity (orbit saved-view live-march vs impostor ≤2%), -motion (slow orbit sweep asserts <1 march/frame + sun-jump/weather re-bake triggers). **Depends on:** cloud-unification epic (renderMode toggle). **Effort:** L (Phase 1 M, Phase 2 L). **Trace:** 2026-07-06 (R-IMPOSTOR research) → 2026-07-11 (recorded as FUTURE at Campaign-7 close-out).
